Convenit autem hactenus etiam cum imagine Dei concreata (cujus restaurationem importat); de qua vid. cap. IV. Qua ratione partim differt ab imagine Dei concreata, partim adhuc convenit cum donis gratiae in hac vita. d) e) f) Sic indicantur causae beatitudinis efficiens et impulsivae, de quibus actum est § 21. Qui sunt subjectum Quod, juxta § 22. Ita subjectum Quo indicatur: partim primarium, ratione beatitudinis essentialis, in qua finis noster formalis consistit; partim secundarium, ratione caeterarum partium ad integritatem beatitudinis spectantium. Confer. § 24. Sic enim patet ratio beatitudinis absolute dictae seu ultimae, vid. § 2. et 11.k) In qua consistit finis beatitudinis, juxta § 24. Caput VII. DE MORTE SEU DAMNATIONE AETERNA. § 1.

Opponitur a beatitudini damnatio partim privative,b quatenus carentiam omnium bonorum, quae beatorum felicitatem ingrediuntur, importat, partim contrarie, qua PART. I. CAP. VII.

tenus non nudam beatitudinis absentiam dicit, sed adversitates et cruciatus positivos c sensumque malorum acutissimum continet. Atque ideo doctrinae de beatitudine recte haec altera subjungitur, ut opposita juxta se posita clarius elucescant; quemadmodum et fatendum est, eos, qui bonitate finis theologiae non facile moventur (quippe terrenarum rerum amore corrupti), terreri posse interim consideratione miseriae alias expectandae. Tertium enim non datur, et qui summum bonum non assequuntur, malum summum non effugient; quod constat ex vi propositionum, quibus extrema sors hominum omnium ad duas classes revocatur.

Dan. 12, 2. Joh. 5, 28. 29. Matth. 25, 32. 33. et 46. Huc referri solet, quod status damnatorum vocatur mors se· eunda, Apoc. 2, 11. cap. 20, 6. Mors enim est privatio vitae. Et dicitur secunda, quod privationem vitae alterius, quam expleta hac vita contingere poteramus, importat. Scriptores ecclesiastici poenam damni appellant. Ita idem status aliquando opprobrii seu ignominiae, aliquando ignis aeterni nomine venit. Vid. ll. cc. Daniel, et Matth. Alias poena, senrns dicitur.

Gerhardus: ״Si impiis non metuenda esset gravior aliqua poena, quam redactio in nihilum, non foret ipsis melius, non fuisse natos.“ (Loc. de inferno seu morte aeterna. § 78.) ANTITHESIS. Gerhardus: ״Antithesis: 1. Philo videtur in ea fuisse sententia, infernum nihil aliud esse, quam conscientiae horrorem. . . Hieronymus in ep. ad Avitam, enumerans Origenis haereses, inter alias etiam hanc recenset his omnino verbis: ,Origenes lib. 2. πη,ϊ αρχών ignem gehennae et tormenta, quae S.S. peccatoribus comminatur, non ponit in suppliciis, sed in conscientia peccatorum.‘ . . 2. Photiniani statuunt, impios vel nunquam resuscitandos, vel post resurrectionem ac judicium in nihilum redigendos; definiunt igitur damnationem per ανυπαρξίαν.“ (L. c. § 77. sq.) § '

i. Inprimis carebunt damnati, ex parte intellectus, visime Dei beatifica,a neque donabuntur lumine gloriae,b beatis divinitus collato. Hoc est, non videre vitam, Joh. 3, 36. Eodem referri solet, Ps. 49, 20. de impiis quod dicitur, quod in aeternum non, sint fruituri luce, et in N. T. damnatos projectum iri in tenebras, Matth. 8, 12. cap. 22, 18., velut a Domino, qui est mentium lumen, expulsos, juxta Prosper. üb. III. de vit. contempl. c. 12. (Conf. Gerh. T. VIII. L. de inferno, § 42. p. 590.) Quodque discedere a Christo Matth. 25, 41· et relinqui Luc. 17, 34. dicuntur.

1)E DAMNATIONE AETERNA.

Imo et lumine gratiae, quod in hac vita eontemserunt, ac recto de rebus divinis ac suis judicio carebunt.Lutherus: ״In den Verdammten bleibet dasselbige vernünftige Licht, ja, es wird nur heller, dass sie mehr davon gequälet werden.“ (Opp. T. XI, 256.) § 3. Atque ita facile etiam patet, amorem a Dei, tanquam summi boni clare cogniti, et gaudium b inde resultans plane abfutura esse a damnatis.

Hic enim ex cognitione Dei, tanquam boni nostri, unice nascitur. Quo refertur defectu» aquae, Zach. 9, 11., i. e. refrigerii, gaudii, voluptatis.§ 4. Corporum autem beatorum dotes, per quas ipsa glorificantur,a eodem modo damnatis denegabuntur.b

Claritas profecto, subtilitas et agilitas et impassibilitas aberit. Quae non nisi piis electisque promissa sunt. Quanquam vero corpora damnatorum sunt futura incorruptibilia, tamen neque incorruptibilitas illa ex impassibilitate seu spiritualitate, tanquam intrinseca perfectione, proficiscetur, neque in gloriam corporum illorum cedet, sed in miseriae augmentum, ut haec sit aeterna; de quo infra dicetur.Gerhardus: ״Quod corpora damnatorum dicuntur spiritualia, non est accipiendum sensu Origeniano, quasi nec carnem, nec ossa sint habitura; nec sensu eo, quo beatorum corpora dicuntur spiritualia et gloriflcata 1 Cor. 15, 45., sed sensu latiore, ut opponatur corpori animali, quod cibi, potus, vestium etc. adminiculo indiget.“ (Loc. de morte aet. § 66.) Idem: ״Ut beatorum corpora erunt gloriosa 1 Cor. 15, 44. Phil. 3, 21., sic damnatorum corpora erunt deformia, tetra, abominanda. Sicut gloria beatorum refulgebit per ipsorum corpora instar lucis per vitrum resplendescentis, sic ignominia damnatorum ex anima in corpora ipsorum redundabit. Quodsi enim in hac vita malefici ac facinorosi tetrico vultu de occulta cordium suorum impietate testantur, ,der Mord und Diebstahl siehet ihnen aus den Augen‘, quanto magis in damnatorum corporibus ac faciebus maculae ineluibiles peccatorum apparebuntl“ (L. c. § 52.) § 5.

Inter poenas positivas primum occurrit cognitio illa intellectus, per quam damnati Deum abstracti ve et ex poenis, a partim ut Dominum summae majestatis, sed a PART. I. CAP. VII.

se gravissime offensum, partim ut judicem justum, sed hoc ipso suorum peccatorum vindicem acerrimum, partim ut patrem benignissimum, verum non sibi, sed aliis, qui crediderunt et beati facti sunt, cognoscent.b

Sic Apoc. 6, 17. describuntur, tanquam cognoscentes sedentem super thronum seu Deum summa majestate pollentem, cujus faciem, extrema minitantem, imo inferentem, ferre non possint. Itaque, licet Deum cognoscere ad perfectionem hominis pertineat, tamen sic cognoscere non est perfectionis, sed miseriae gravissimae.§ 6. Similiter se ipsos ita contemplabuntur, ut peccatorum suorum multitudinem et gravitatem, poenarum etiam, quibus affliguntur, meritum, acerbitatem et perennitatem animo reputent.

Ita Sapientiae 5. sub initium proponitur damnatorum querela, qua suam stultitiam accusant seque errasse, in via veritatis, iniquitatis et perditionis callibus expletos esse et perambulasse deserta avia etc. confitentur, superbiae, divitiarum et gloriationis suae vanitatem meditantes. § 7· Homines alios, qui beati sunt, spectabunt, tanquam participes ejus felicitatis, qua ipsi destituuntur, et expertes calamitatum, quibus ipsi premuntur.

Sap. l. c. describuntur videntes justum confidentia magna stantem coram ipsis et stupefacti propter salutem inopinatam ipsius etc. Gerhardus: ״Beatorum in coelo felicitatem non quidem in specie nec πρακτικός, interim tamen in genere ac θεωρητικός videbunt.“ (L. c. § 52.) § 8.

Itaque ex parte voluntatis orietur odium Dei, quippe sibi infensi et implacabilis;a odium sui ipsorum, utpote qui sibi ipsis causa miseriae fuerint;b invidia, ex adspectu alienae beatitudinis resultans;c dolor et tristitia atque anxietas d propter ingentem malorum praesentium cumulum et impatientia e ac desperatio perpetua. f

Vid. Apoc. 6, 16. 17., ubi ingens aversatio Dei, cujus conspectum ferre non possint, indicatur. Et res ipsa docet, voluntatem damnatorum non ferri nec posse ferri in Deum, tanquam sibi bonum, quem irreconciliabiliter adversum habent et norunt. Neque abstinebit voluntas ab omni actu circa Deum occupato, quando Deus intellectui ipsorum obversatur, qualem se erga ipsos gerit, ipsique sensu irae divinae perpetuo affliguntur. Itaque, cum amare Deum non posr sint, odio, quod amori opponitur, eum prosequuntur, prout angeli mali, hostes Dei atque hominum άσπονδοι.

Sap. 5, 4.. 6. 7. Accusatio enim illa displicentiam ac detestationem sui ipsorum indicat. Ita l. c. v. 3. sqq. locuturi dicuntur de justo beato: Hic erat, quem habebamus quondam ludibrio et communi probro. Quomodo relatus est in ßios Dei, et in sanetis sors est illius? Huc pertinet Ψλίψις xai στενοχώρια illa, compressio et coardatio, de qua Rom. 2, 9. Confer. Sap. 5, 3., ubi dicuntur gemere propter angustiam spiritus.

Atque ita pavores, confusiones, fremitus, indignationem, morsus et cruciatus acerbissimos damnatis adscribi legimus. Occasionem effugiendi mala sua non invenientes, quaerentes ac desiderantes mori, seu omnino non esse, aut plane destrui, Apoc. 9, 6.


### Concerning Eternal Death, or Damnation: Pertaining to this, and exhibiting as it were a complex of the former evils, is…

Pertaining to this, and exhibiting as it were a complex of the former evils, is that μανία, or horrible fury, which the blessed Gerhard says causes the damned to fight against God and all creatures, and indeed even against themselves. "They will be angry at God," he says, "and will blaspheme Him because of the magnitude of the pains and punishments which they will feel are inflicted upon them by Him. They will be angry at all creatures, because, destitute of all their consolation, they remain in eternal darkness. They will wish for death and destruction for themselves because of the atrocity of the torments and the bitterness of the pains, although otherwise nature abhors death and seeks its own preservation." (L. c. on Hell, § 52, p. 617.)

Gerhard: "The question is asked: Do the damned retain the faith and hope which they had in this life? Some of the scholastics, such as Alensis p. 3, q. 64, art. 7, Durand. 3, sent. dist. 23, q. 9, and others affirm it... Resp.: 1. Saving faith, consisting of knowledge, assent, and trust, is not in the damned, as is evident; otherwise they would not be damned. 2. Whether historical knowledge of the articles of faith will have a place in them is rightly doubted, for knowledge shall pass away (ἡ γνῶσις καταργηθήσεται), 1 Cor. 13: 8. If the force of disease and pain induces oblivion of human knowledge in this life, how much more will infernal torments induce oblivion of divine knowledge! 3. Assent regarding that article of faith, that God exists and that He is the avenger of crimes, will be in the damned, just as in the demons, but it will be forced and wrung from them by the sense of the torments inflicted upon them. Augustine, lib. de fide et operibus, cap. 16: 'The faith of demons is expressed through fear.' 4. It could also not inconveniently be said that what James asserts regarding the faith of demons refers to the course of this life, that while it still endures, before the devils are cast into the infernal fire with the damned men, they believe that God exists, by whom they are one day to be thrust into Tartarus; but when they actually experience those torments, they no longer believe, but know and feel. 5. The damned know that they are to be tormented eternally, not through any supernatural act of faith, but through the judicial sentence which they receive at the point of death and especially on the day of judgment. 6. There will be in the damned a continuous and perpetual despair, and consequently also no hope. For the slightest hope would alleviate the magnitude of the pains." (L. c. § 72.) PART I. CHAPTER VII.

9. Moreover, by this very fact, the will of the damned, being entirely turned away from God, will be determined to evil, so that whatever they do displeases God, and they themselves sin incessantly in their thoughts, words, and deeds. For just as the love of God above all things is the sum of the divine law, so the absence of divine love and the perpetual hatred of God cannot but entail ἀνομία [lawlessness] and a perpetual disagreement with the law in the faculties and operations of the damned.

Fechtius: "It cannot be otherwise than that they either always sin, or do not have the law, which is absurd, 1 John 3:4." (Sylloge controvers. p. 95.)

Certainly, that which proceeds from an impure soul, not regenerated by grace but abandoned by God as a punishment for sins, cannot please God.

Gerhardus: "The question is asked: Are all the actions of the damned evil? The sufferings of the damned will be morally good, because they proceed from the justice and divine will, the rule of all goodness; although physically and naturally they are evil to the damned, that is, adverse and hostile. But all the actions of the damned will be evil: 1. Because the damned will be obstinate and hardened in evil. The depravity of the will, in which and with which they died, will adhere to them immovably and immutably forever. 2. Because they will always be in an actual hatred of God, which arises in them from the perpetual and immovable consideration of the most miserable state in which they know they will remain for all eternity. Hence, they also perpetually and directly turn themselves away from God, the highest good, to whose glory they ought to refer all things. 3. Because they will blaspheme God on account of the magnitude of their pain and torments, Rev. 14: 11. Now, where there is blasphemy of God, to whom alone the highest honor is due, there can be nothing good. 4. Because all the actions of the devils are also evil." (L. c. § 76.)

For where there is ἀνομία, there is sin. And the law concerning loving God (which simultaneously involves the negative law concerning not having hatred for God) is immutable. Therefore, although the damned, by reason of their present state, cannot love God, but can hate Him, and do hate Him; yet because they are considered as having fallen into this state by their own fault and from preceding sins, they do not thereby withdraw themselves from the obligation of the immutable law, which neither natural death removes, nor can remove, since a creature, obligated by nature to the law, does not entirely cease to be, nor does it cease to be a rational creature. Thus, the end of a man’s life and of divine μακροθυμία [long-suffering] are not, therefore, an absolute end of sin. And there is room for the punishments of sins after death, such that sins can be punished by sins. Nor is it absurd for the divine majesty to leave the damned in a perpetual state of sin and therefore of offense to Him, since the damned do not bear those sins with impunity, inasmuch as they sustain extreme misery at the same time that they sin, and are never to be delivered from their misery.

Although we do not therefore maintain that the divine majesty is perpetually infested by the blasphemies of the damned, committed by external act and as if with one voice. We are speaking only of the most profound corruption of the will, which cannot but be sinful.

OF ETERNAL DAMNATION. J. Ad. Osiander: "It is not probable that the damned in hell sin always, especially by blaspheming." (Colleg. th. P. VI, 229.)

Dannhauerus: "It is the second death, inflicted in hell by God, who is angry, immediately upon the whole man, with the loss and sensation of being tormented, . . . with the loss and forfeiture of every good (explained by outer darkness), and consequently also of that solace which they might be able to derive from blasphemies as a kind of vengeance against God. 'Vengeance is a good, sweeter than life itself.' For it seems more probable and more just to the divine glory (although we modestly submit our judgment here) that there will be a measure and a limit to blasphemies and sins against God (whose μακροθυμία ends with this world). The damned despair, but without sin; for despair is not properly a sin, but only sadness and consciousness of sin from the sentence of condemnation, and an estimation of the impossibility of liberation, and the cessation of the attempt to attain glory. Yet they are not blessed for this reason, that they do not sin in act, since they still possess sin, though it is restrained." (Hodos. Phaen. 4. p. 197.) §

10. The bodies of the damned will be tormented by hell-fire, which is true and properly so-called, and inextinguishable. That they will be truly punished by it is evident from Matt. 10:28, where it is said that bodies are destroyed in Gehenna. Cf. b. Gerhard, L. de Inferno § 83, p. 683, 684. See especially Matt. 25:41, where Christ the Judge, about to pronounce sentence from the tribunal, is read to be about to indicate this kind of punishment to the damned, whom we certainly believe will speak properly, not tropically and obscurely. And it is otherwise very frequent in Scripture that the punishments of the damned are called by the name of fire. See Is. 66, last verse; Mark 9:47, 48; Rev. 21:8. Thus, indeed, it is also certain that that fire will not be spiritual (for thus it would not be fire properly so-called), but material and corporeal. However, to wish to explain its nature more distinctly is more curious than useful.

Quenstedtius: "When it is asked what is to be understood by hell-fire, to which devils and the damned are already addicted or are to be addicted, doctors, both ancient and modern, depart into diverse opinions. I. The opinion is of those who establish that hell-fire will be material, corporeal, elemental. Thus, indeed, the fathers think, as Tertullian, L. de anima c. 7, n. 30 and 40; Augustine, T. 5, l. 21 de Civ. Dei c. 10, where he says: 'Why should we not say that, although in wondrous yet true ways, even incorporeal spirits can be afflicted by the punishment of corporeal fire? Yea, spirits, demons, although incorporeal, are to be tormented by corporeal fires.' And after a few words: 'That Gehenna, which is also called the lake of fire and brimstone, will be corporeal fire.' . . Almost all the scholastics and papists follow these. . . The reasons for this opinion are chiefly these: 1. Because one must not depart from the letter unless evident necessity leads us away from it; wherefore, since Holy Scripture describes the punishments of hell by fire, it must be accepted ῥητῶς and in the literal sense. 2. Because flame, brimstone, smoke, and wood are attributed to hell-fire; therefore, it is certainly corporeal and properly so-called fire. . . But these reasons do not yet sufficiently prove that the fire of hell will be material and elemental; for 1) Holy Scripture expressly says that all elements are to be conflagrated on that judicial day, 2 Pet. 3:10; but with this conflagration of the world and substantial destruction, which almost all theologians prove, it cannot..."

the assertion concerning a material and properly so-called hellfire consists. 2) This opinion rests upon the false hypothesis of certain fathers, scholastics, and papists, namely, that the world will not perish κατ’ ουσίαν (according to substance), but only κατα ποιότητα (according to quality), or that the world, without the destruction of its substance, will be changed for the better regarding its accidents. If this opinion stands, it must be conceded to them that even after the final judgment, just as other elements will exist, so too will fire properly so-called, by which the damned may be tormented. 3) Matt. 25:41, hellfire is called eternal fire. But a material and properly so-called fire cannot be eternal, for it requires fuel for its preservation by which it may be fed. 4) Because hellfire will also act upon devils and souls, but material fire cannot act upon spirits. For nothing can act outside the sphere of its object. And if it were to act, the spirit would be weaker than the body, which is absurd. . . The Scholastics. . . say that hellfire is elevated by the principal cause so that it can act upon a spirit. . . But in truth: 1) This opinion presupposes a fire such as has not yet been proven by the Scholastics. 2) It does not follow: God can elevate this fire, therefore He uses this fire thus elevated. 3) Nor is it an objection that Scripture describes this fire by flame, sulfur, smoke, and wood; for Scripture is accustomed to speak of things pertaining to the future age using the phrases of this age, just as it describes the joys of the heavenly life through weddings and banquets (Matt. 8:11; Luke 22:30). . . II. The second opinion is that the fire by which the machinery of the heavens and the earth will be dissolved and destroyed will, by divine command, envelop the damned with its coarser part, and that this fire will be preternatural and an instrument of perpetual torture. This is the view of D. G. Calixtus. . . Akin to this opinion is that of certain Calvinists, such as Keckelmann (System. Th. 1. 2. c. 7), who thinks that "subterranean fires, divinely increased and intensified, will torture the bodies of the impious." The same is the opinion of Zanchius (in 2 Thess. 1. Com. 6. Op. f. 458) and Alstedius (in Theol. Polem. P. 4. controv. II. p. 376). But 1) where will such fire be, once all worldly creatures have been consumed by fire? 2) D. Dannhauer (Hodosoph. Phaen. 12. p. 1500) says: "Fire, after it has devoured the world consigned to the pyre, will return to nothingness due to a lack of fuel." 3) It follows from this opinion that hellfire does not yet exist, nor are the souls of the damned tormented by it. For the fire that is to exist only after the conflagration of the world does not yet exist. . . III. The third opinion is that of those who think that Holy Scripture describes the state and condition of the damned by means of fire, not because there is any fire properly so-called in Hell, but to signify thereby the most bitter torments and pains of the damned. For there are pains that arise from fire which are the most acute and greatest of all. This opinion is embraced among the fathers by Ambrose, who in his commentary on Luke (bk. 7, ch. 14) discourses on this fire thus: "Neither is there any bodily gnashing of teeth, nor any perpetual fire of bodily flames, nor is the worm bodily." Damascenus, who in his *Orthodox Faith* (bk. 4, ch. 28) says in the final words: "The impious and sinners will come into eternal fire, ονχ υλικόν, οἷον τὸ παρ’ ἡμῶν, ἀλλ’ οἷον, οἶδεν ὁ θεός, not material: that is, such as is among us, but such as God knows." Among our own theologians, the blessed Aeg. Hunnius. . . D. Gerlachius. . . the blessed Balduinus. "At this point we warn," says the blessed Gerhard (Harmon. Evang. c. 165, p. 910a), "that just as in the former part of the sentence (Matt. 25) by the kingdom to which the just are called, the highest felicity, beatitude, joy, and glory are understood, so in this latter part of the sentence, by the fire into which the damned are banished, the highest unhappiness, misery, pains, and torments are signified, either metaphorically or certainly synecdochically." D. Dannhauer (Hodos. p. 3) teaches: "The words of Christ in Mark 9 ought not to be taken concerning elemental and corporeal fire, or corporeal worms, but concerning immaterial fire and most exquisite pains." Of the same opinion among the Calvinists are Franc. Junius, Tilenus, Danaeus, Baynoldus, and others. This opinion is confirmed 1) from Isaiah (last chapter, last verse): "Their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched." But such as the worm is, such also will the fire be.

Latin:

Pertinet huc et quasi complexum priorum malorum exhibet μανία, seu furor ille horribilis, quod damnatos adversus Deum et omnes creaturas, adeoque etiam adversus se ipsos pugnare dicit b. Gerhardus. Deo, ait, irascentur eumque blasphemabunt ob magnitudinem dolorum d poenarum, quas ab ipso sibi inflictas sentient. Irascentur omnibus creatu־ ris, quod omni earum solatio destituti in aeternis tenebris maneant. Sibi ipsis mortem d exitium optabunt ob tormentorum atrocitatem ac dolorum acerbitatem, cum alias natura a morte abhorreat ac sui conservationemquaerat. L. de inferno § 52. p. 617.

Gerhardus: ,,Quaeritur: An damnati retineant fidem et spem, quam in hac vita habuerunt? Quidam ex scholasticis, ut Alensis p. 3. q. 64. art. 7., Durand. 3. sent. dist. 23. q. 9. et alii atfirmant... Resp. : 1. Fides salvifica, constans notitia, assensu ac fiducia, non est in damnatis, ut constat; alias enim non essent damnati. 2. Notitia historica articulorum fidei an in illis locum sit habitura, merito dubitatur, v yap γνώσις καταμγηΰήαεται, 1 Cor. 13, 8. Si vis morbi ac dolorum inducit oblivionem scientiae humanae in hac vita, quanto magis cruciatus infernales scientiae divinae! 3. Assensus circa illum fidei articulum, quod sit Deus et quod sit vindex scelerum, erit in damnatis, perinde ut in daemonibus, sed coactus et expressus per sensum tormentorum, sibi inflictorum. Augustin, lib. de fide et operibus cap. 16.: ,Fides daemonum exprimitur per timorem.‘ 4. Posset etiam haud incommode illud, quod de fide daemonum Jacobus asserit, ad hujus vitae curriculum referri, quod, eo adhuc durante, antequam diaboli cum hominibus damnatis in infernalem ignem projiciantur, credant, esse Deum, a quo aliquando sint in tartarum detrudendi; sed quando reipsa illos cruciatus experiuntur, non amplius credunt, sed sciunt et sentiunt. 5. Damnati sciunt, se in aeternum cruciandos, non per actum aliquem fidei supernaturalem, sed per judiciariam sententiam, quam in articulo mortis et cumprimis in die judicii accipiunt. 6. Erit in damnatis continua et perpetua desperatio, ac proinde etiam spes nulla. Nam minima spes dolorum magnitudinem levaret.“ (L. c. § 72.) PART. I. CAP. VII.

9. Hoc ipso autem voluntas damnatorum, a Deo plane aversa, determinata erit a ad malum, ut, quicquid agunt, Deo b displiceat, ipsique cogitationibus, dictis et factis, indesinenter c peccent. Quemadmodum enim dilectio Dei super omnia legis divinae summa est, sic absentia amoris divini et odium Dei perpetuum non potest non importare ανομίαν et disconvenientiam cum lege in facultatibus et operationibus damnatorum perpetuam.

Fechtius: ״Fieri non potest, quin semper aut peccent, aut legem non habeant, quod absurdum, I Joh. 3, 4.“ (Sylloge controvers. p. 95.)

Non potest sane placere Deo, quod ab animo impuro nec per gratiam regenito, sed in poenam peccatorum a Deo deserto proficiscitur.

Gerhardus: ״Quaeritur: An damnatorum actiones omnes sint malae? Passiones damnatorum moraliter bonae erunt, quia a justitia et voluntate divina, omnis bonitatis regula, progrediuntur; quamvis physice ac naturaliter damnatis sint malae, id est, adversae et inimicae. Actiones vero damnatorum omnes erunt malae: 1. Quia damnati erunt in malo obstinati ac obdurati. Pravitas voluntatis, in qua et cum qua fuere mortui, immobiliter ac immutabiliter in perpetuum eis adhaerebit. 2. Quia semper erunt in actuali Dei odio, quod ex perpetua et immota consideratione miserrimi status, in quo se norunt in omnem aeternitatem permansuros, in ipsis oritur. Inde etiam perpetuo ac directe avertunt se a Deo, summo bono, ad cujus gloriam omnia deberent referre. 3. Quia blasphemabunt Deum prae doloris et cruciatuum magnitudine, Apocal. 14, 11. Jam vero ubi blasphemia Dei, cui unice summus honor debetur, ibi nihil potest esse boni. 4. Quia etiam diabolorum actiones omnes sunt malae.“ (L. c. § 76.)

Ubi enim ανομία, ibi peccatum. Et lex de diligendo Deo (quae simul involvit legem negativam de non-odio habendo Deo) immutabilis est. Damnati ergo, licet pro ratione status praesentis non possint Deum diligere, sed odisse possint, atque oderint; quia tamen conside:· rantur ut sua culpa et ex praecedentibus peccatis in hunc statum delapsi, non ideo subducunt se ab obligatione legis immutabilis, quam nec mors naturalis tollit, aut tollere potest, quando creatura, per naturam obligata legi, non prorsus desinet esse, neque rationalis creatura esse cessat. Itaque terminus vitae hominis et μαχροΰυμίας divinae non ideo sunt terminus peccati absolutus. Ac peccatorum suppliciis ita locus est post mortem, ut tamen peccata peccatis puniri queant. Nec absurdum est, divinam majestatem damnatos in perpetuo peccati adeoque offensionis suae statu relinquere, quando peccata illa damnati impune non ferunt, quippe miseriam extremam simul, dum peccant, sustinentes neque unquam a miseria sua liberandi.

Quanquam non ideo statuamus, divinam majestatem blasphemiis damnatorum, actu externo et velut uno ore commissis, perpetuo infestari. De voluntatis corruptione profundissima, quae non potest non esse peccaminosa, tantum nobis sermo est.

DE DAMNATIONE AETERNA. J. Ad. Osiander: ״Non est probabile, damnatos in inferno semper peccare, imprimis blasphemando.“ (Colleg. th. P. VI, 229.)

Dannhauerus: ״Est mors secunda, a Deo irato immediate totius hominis damno sensuque cruciati, in inferno inflicta, . . . damno ac jactura omnis boni (tenebris exterioribus explicata), consequenter etiam illius solatii, quod ex blasphemiis quadam quasi.vindicta in Deum capere possent. ,Est vindicta bonum vita jucundior ipsa.‘ Videtur enim probabilius et ad gloriam divinam justius (quanquam hic judicium modeste submittamus), fore blasphemiarum et peccatorum contra Deum (cujus μακρο&νμία cum hoc mundo finitur) modum ac terminum. Desperant damnati, sed sine peccato; desperatio enim proprie non est peccatum, sed tantum tristitia et conscientia peccati e sententia damnatoria et aestimatio impossibilitatis liberationis ac intermissio conatus assequendae gloriae. Neque tamen ideo sunt beati, qui non peccant actu, cum adhuc habeant peccatum, sed coercitum.“ (Hodos. Phaen. 4. p. 197.) §

10. Corpora damnatorum cruciabuntur a igne infernali vero ac proprie dicto b et inextinguibili.c Ea enim revera punitum iri, constat ex Matth. 10, 28., ubi dicuntur corpora perdi in gehenna. Conf. b. Gerhard. L. de Inferno § 83. p. 683. 684. Vid. inpriiqis Matth. 25, 41., ubi Christus judex, sententiam pro tribunali laturus, hoc supplicii genus damnatis aliquando indicaturus legitur, quem proprie, non tropice et obscure locuturum utique credimus. Atque alias frequentissimum est in Scriptura, ut supplicia damnatorum ignis nomine appellentur. Vid. Es. 66, ult. Mare. 9, 47. 48. Apoc. 21, 8. Ita vero etiam constat, ignem illum non fore spiritualem (sic enim proprie dictus ignis non fuerit), sed materialem et corporeum. Distinctius autem ejus naturam velle exponere, curiosum magis, quam utile est.

Quenstedtius: ״Quando quaeritur, quid per ignem infernalem, cui jam addicti vel addicendi sunt diaboli et damnati, intelligatur, in diversas abeunt doctores, tam antiqui, quam recentiores, sententias. I. sententia est eorum, qui statuunt, infernalem ignem fore materialem, corporeum, elementarem. Ita quidem patres sentiunt, ut Tertullianus L. de anima c. 7. n. 30. et 40., Augustinus T. 5. 1. 21. de Civ. Dei c. 10., ubi ait: ,Cur non dicamus, quamvis miris, tamen veris modis etiam spiritus incorporeos posse poena corporalis ignis affligi? Imo spiritus daemones, licet incorporei, corporeis ignibus cruciandi.‘ Et post pauca: ,Gehenna illa, quod etiam stagnum ignis et sulphuris dictum est, corporeus ignis erit.‘ . . Hos omnes fere scholastici et pontificii sequuntur. . . Rationes pro hac sententia hae sunt potissimum: 1. Quia a litera non est recedendum, nisi evidens nos ab ea deducat necessitas, quare, quoniam Scriptura s. poenas inferni describit per ignem, ρητώς et in sensu literali hoc est accipiendum. 2. Quia tribuuntur igni infernali flamma, sulphur, fumus, ligna, utique ergo est ignis corporeus et proprie dictus. . . Ast hae rationes nondum satis probant, ignem inferni fore materialem et elementarem; nam 1) s. Seriptura diserte dicit, omnia elementa in die illo censorio esse conflagranda, 2 Petr. 3, 20.; sed cum hac mundi conflagratione et substantiali destructione, quam omnes ferme theologi probant, non potest Baieri Comp. ed. Walther. II. 14 PART. I. CAP. VII.

consistere assertio de infernali igne materiali et proprie sic dicto. 2) Nititur haec opinio falsa hypothesi quorundam patrum, scholastieorum et pontificiorum, sci. mundum non κατ’ ουσίαν, sed tantum κατα ποιότητα interiturum, sive, mundum sine substantiae interitu, in melius quoad accidentia commutatum iri. Qua sententia stante, ipsis concedendum erit, fore adhuc post judicium extremum, ut alia elementa, ita etiam ignem proprie dictum, quo torqueri possint damnati. 3) Matth. 25, 41. infernalis ignis dicitur ignis aeternus. At vero materialis et proprie sic dictus ignis non potest esse aeternus, requirit enim ad sui conservationem pabulum, quo alatur. 4) Quia ignis infernalis aget etiam in diabolos et animas, ignis autem materialis non potest agere in spiritus. Nihil enim potest agere extra sphaeram sui objecti. Et si ageret, spiritus debilior foret corpore, quod absonum. . . Scholastici. . . dicunt, elevari ignem infernalem a causa principali, ut in spiritum agere possit. . . Verum enim vero: 1) Haec sententia supponit ignem, qualis nondum probatus est a scholasticis. 2) Non sequitur: Deus potest ignem hunc elevare, ergo hoc igne sic elevato utitur. 3) Nec obstat, quod Scriptura per flammam, sulphur, fumum, ligna hunc ignem describat; solet enim Scriptura de rebus ad futurum saeculum pertinentibus phrasibus hujus saeculi loqui, quemadmodum et gaudia vitae coelestis per nuptias et convivia describit Matth. 8, 11. Luc. 22, 30. . . II. sententia est, ignem illum, per quem coelorum terraeque machina dissolvetur et destruetur, divino nutu damnatos crassiore sui parte involuturum, huneque ignem praeternaturalem, perpetuique cruciatus instrumentum fore. Ita sentit D. G. Calixtus. . . Huic sententiae affinis est illa quorundam Calvinianorum, ut Keckelmanni System. Th. 1. 2. c. 7., qui existimat, ,ignes subterraneos divinitus auctos atque intensos impiorum corpora cruciaturos esse.‘ Eadem est sententia Zanchii in 2 Thess. 1. Com. 6. Op. f. 458., Alstedii in Theol. Polem. P. 4. controv. II. p. 376. Ast 1) finde talis ignis, omnibus mundanis creaturis consumtis per ignem? 2) D. Dannhauerus Hodosoph. Phaen. 12. p. 1500. inquit: ,Ignis, postquam depaverit mundum in rogum datum, ex defectu alimenti in nihilum redibit.‘ 3) Sequitur ex hac sententia, ignem infernalem nondum exstare, nec damnatorum animas eo torqueri. Qui enim ignis demum post conflagrationem mundi futurus est, ille nondum est. . . III. sententia est eorum, qui existimant, s. Scripturam describere statum et conditionem damnatorum per ignem, non quod proprie detur aliquis in Inferno ignis, sed ut inde significaret acerbissimos cruciatus et dolores damnatorum. Sunt enim dolores, qui ab igne proveniunt, omnium acutissimi et maximi. Hanc sententiam amplectuntur ex patribus Ambrosius, qui 1. 7. in Luc. c. 14. de hoc igne sic disserit: ,Neque corporalium aliquis stridor dentium, neque ignis aliquis perpetuus flammarum corporalium, neque vermis est corporalis.‘ Damascenus, qui 1. 4. O. F. c. 28. verbis extremis inquit: ,Impios et peccatores venturos in ignem aeternum, ονχ υλικόν, o)ov τό παρ’ ημών, αλλ’ οΐον, ύό?ίη ο θεός, non materialem: illum, qualis est apud nos, sed qualem, novit Deus.‘ Ex nostris theologis b. Aeg. Hunnius . . . D. Gerlachius . . . b. Balduinus. ,Hoc loco illud monemus‘, inquit b. Gerhardus Harmon. Evang. c. 165. p. 910. a,, ,ut in priore sententiae parte (Matth. 25.) per regnum, ad quod vocantur justi, summa felicitas, beatitudo, laetitia et gloria intelliguntur, ita in hac posteriore sententiae parte per ignem, in quem damnati ablegantur, summam infelicitatem, miseriam, dolores et cruciatus, vel metaphorice vel certe synecdochice significari.‘ D. Dannhauerus Hodos. p. 3. docet: ,Verba Christi Mare. 9. non debere accipi de elementar! et corporeo igne, de vermibus corporeis, sed de igne immateriali ac exquisitissimis doloribus.‘ Ejusdem sententiae sunt ex Calvinianis Franc. Junius, Tilenus, Danaeus, Baynoldus et alii. Confirmatur haec sententia 1) ex Esa. ult. v. ult.: ,Vermis eorum non morietur, et ignis non extinguetur.‘ Qualis autem vermis, talis quoque ignis futurus erit.


### Concerning Eternal Death, or Damnation: But by the worm, the Fathers and the Scholastics understand the spiritual and…

But by the worm, the Fathers and the Scholastics understand the spiritual and analogical worm of a gnawing conscience. Therefore, by the fire, the most exquisite pain and torture is also signified metaphorically.

2) From Matthew 25, where the Savior, speaking by design concerning the final judgment and infernal punishments, after having said, "Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire," immediately adds: "And these shall go away into everlasting punishment." Which final words seem to intimate that by infernal fire, the most grievous punishment of Gehenna is designated in a general sense. . .

IV. Finally, there is the opinion of those who prefer to withhold judgment here rather than to establish anything certain. Augustine embraces this opinion in Book 20 of *The City of God*, ch. 16, where he says: "What kind of fire this is, and in what part of the world or of the universe it will be, I think no man knows, unless perhaps he to whom the divine Spirit has shown it.". . The blessed Gerhard follows the same in *Loci de Infern.* § 69, where he says: "We do not doubt that it is possible by divine power for corporeal fire to torture devils and incorporeal souls, but whether that fire will truly be corporeal, material, and visible, or rather incorporeal, invisible, and immaterial, we leave in the middle (although we lean more toward the latter). And we pray to God earnestly that He may not manifest that to us through the knowledge of experience. It is better to be solicitous with all zeal through true and serious conversion about fleeing that fire, than to contend odiously and idly about the nature of that fire." D. Althofer in *Harm. Evang.* on Luke 16:25 and D. Glassius in *Phil. Sacr.* hold the same. (Th. did.-pol. P. I. c. 14. s. 2. q. 4. f. 820—824.)

Fechtius: "Fire not elemental, and yet properly so called, is water not moist, and yet properly so called. What kind that will be, if it is not elemental, is not clear." (*Controvers. syll.* Giessen 1768. p. 95.) See Matthew 3:12, where it is called πῦρ ἄσβεστον, and chapter 25:41, where it is called αἰώνιον. §

11. But it is also not improbable that the organs of the senses and the senses themselves will be tortured with peculiar punishments. And concerning the sense of touch, while the opinion concerning fire properly so called stands, there can be no doubt. Namely, that those who sinned through the organs of the senses should also be punished through the same. See the preceding §. As for the punishments of the remaining senses, there are those who think that, regarding sight, the horrible spectacles of demons appearing in a certain form, and the sight of other damned persons, have a place; regarding hearing, their own groans and those of companions weeping and gnashing their teeth; regarding taste, foul flavors and thirst; regarding smell, the stench of sulfurous fire. Others, however, take those things which are brought forward from the Scriptures on this matter metaphorically and parabolically, concerning the most grievous pains, depicted by those things which can happen to man in this life that are most bitter.

See the blessed Gerhard, *L. de Inferno* § 71. p. 665. 666. 667. Hafenrefferus: "What are those tortures? They are the most exquisite pains of soul and body (for both had sinned), arising from the dread and sense of the most just wrath and divine vengeance against sins, the most sorrowful consciousness of which they carry about with them, the baseness of which is manifest, and for which there is also no remission in the future, and thence the pun[ishment]..." PART 1. CHAPTER VII. ... nor can any mitigation or end be hoped for. Whence, with horrible lamentation and wailing, the wretched will detest their former impiety, by which they securely neglected the commands of the Lord, fraternal admonitions, and all means of attaining salvation, but in vain. For in perpetual anguish, horrible trembling, in shame, confusion, and ignominy, in unquenchable fire, in weeping and gnashing of teeth, in eternal and horrendous darkness, torn away from the grace and favor of God, they will be tormented among devils horribly and without end for eternity. — "

I do not yet understand, however, what those torments are like?" Resp.: Because the future torments of the damned far exceed the keenness of every human mind, so that we are never able to attain the magnitude of them even by thought, therefore what they are or what they will be like cannot be sufficiently expressed in words. Scripture, however, in order to show that these are the greatest and most exquisite torments, likens them to those things by which the highest pain of both soul and body is wont to be excited in this life. Therefore, they are compared now to fire, now to the gnashing of teeth, now to worms, and to whatever other things can be named that are most full of sadness and pain. (Loc. th. 1. 3. loc. 9. p. 484—486.)

Gerhardus: "The eyes will be tormented by the sight of demons, the ears by the gnashing and groaning of the companions of punishment, the sense of smell by an intolerable stench, the sense of taste by the most rapid thirst and hunger, the sense of touch and all members by cold and fire. The imagination will suffer from the apprehension of present pains, the memory from the recollection of past pleasures, the intellect from the consideration of lost goods and the evils, present and future, to which they have arrived. Let the same judgment be held concerning the members of the body, in all and each of which the damned will suffer, because they abused all and each for the ignominy of the Creator and turned them into weapons of iniquity.

Rom. 6:13." (L. c. § 53.) The same: "To the burning fire is almost everywhere joined the gnawing worm. By it, however, seems to be understood the perpetual and continuous bite of conscience, arising from the recollection of sins, a certain rabid displeasure and fruitless repentance, the greatest and never-interrupted anguish of heart. For just as worms gnaw corpses with a continuous bite, so that internal worm of conscience will perpetually lacerate the souls of the damned. Just as worms are born in putrefying corpses, so a putrefied conscience begets spiritual and immortal worms." (L. c. § 51.)

The same: "It is asked: Whether, besides fire and the worm, other bodily punishments, truly and properly so called, are to be established in hell? 1. Bonaventura (4. sent. dist. 44. art. 2. quaest. 2.) argues that in hell there is not only punishing fire, but four elements, by which souls and bodies are punished... 2. But Beda establishes that there is cold in hell. The same seems to be the opinion of Jerome in his commentary on chapter 10 of Matthew... and of others whose footsteps most Papists follow, establishing that in hell there is a very wide receptacle of the coldest waters like a sea, into which the damned pass from the fire, snatched by demons, and after the heat suffer cold, from which the gnashing of teeth arises. But the saying of Job from the Hebrew text is not correctly rendered...

3. Those who attribute true cold to hell establish that there is gnashing of teeth in it; but some of the ancients more correctly explain it metaphorically concerning the envy and fury of the damned, as we saw above. 4. They explain weeping as continuous groaning. Hugo of Saint Victor (d. 1): 'No voice sounds in hell except woe, woe.' Thomas (in addit., q. 97. art. 3): 'Weeping can exist in the damned according to a certain commotion and disturbance of the head and eyes, but the resolution and flow of tears cannot exist in them. They will utter great groans, and do those things which those who weep are wont to do, although they shed no tears.' But if they acknowledge a metaphor in the word 'weeping,' why do they so greatly recoil from it in other things and insist simply on the letter? 5. Smoke, true and not metaphorical, from the matter of eternal..."

OF ETERNAL DAMNATION. Bonaventura posits that it is born of sulfur in hell... 6. Most all here acknowledge sulfur properly so-called, and they even add that a foul odor is to be emitted from the bodies of the damned through intentional species, just as a sweet odor exhales from the bodies of the blessed. 7. It is the opinion of many that the damned are to be tormented by hunger and thirst properly so-called. But it seems most simple, because of the arguments set forth above, to take all these things metaphorically and parabolically concerning the supreme and ineffable torments of the damned, which are depicted by those things which can befall man in this life that are by far the most bitter and troublesome.” (L. c. § 71.) §

12. That there will be degrees of infernal punishments cannot be denied. However, to define them more distinctly according to the diversity of any subjects is not equally easy. Thus Christ, in Matt. 10:15, ch. 11:22 and 24, and Luke 10:12, denounces heavier punishments upon the Jews of His own time, and specifically upon the inhabitants of the cities of Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum, than upon the citizens of the cities of Sodom, Gomorrah, Tyre, and Sidon. Indeed, it is probable that more vehement stings of conscience will be found in those who have sinned more often and more grievously against their conscience; and that more intense pains, even regarding the body, will be inflicted upon those who were more industrious in this life in using their bodies to practice sins.

However, it is customary to inquire concerning the infants of the Gentiles: Whether the punishment of the damned, beyond the lack of the beatific vision, is also constituted in real infernal torments? In which question, indeed, the blessed Musaeus preferred to remain in suspense (ἐπέχειν); see *Ausführl. Erklärung* Q. ult. p. 704, 705. Consonant with this are the things which the blessed Huelsemann wrote in *praelect. F. C. Art. VIII. 8. II. M. I. § 3. p. 444. Prop. IX.*, that we can indeed pronounce this concerning the infants of the Gentiles: that according to the norm of the revealed Word they have no part in eternal beatitude, John 3:36, 2 Thess. 1:8; but concerning the quality and quantity of the punishment, we can determine nothing.

But if, indeed, we conceive—which is the opinion of some of our own—some hope of salvation to be conferred upon these infants through the extraordinary grace of God (although perhaps a hope conjoined with greater fear of the opposite than when there is talk of the salvation of Christian infants dying without baptism), and thus we think they will not be damned, there will be no need for the question concerning the punishment of loss alone, or also of sense, regarding them.

Quenstedtius: “Concerning the infants of parents who are established outside the boundaries of the church, or who are on the outside, it does not pertain to us to judge, according to that of the apostle 1 Cor. 5:13: τοὺς ἔξω ὁ θεὸς κρινεῖ, cf. v. 12.” (L. c. P. IV. c. 5. s. 2. q. 10. f. 1165.)

Latin:

BE DAMNATIONE AETERNA. Sed per vermem patres et scholastici spiritualem et analogicum vermem remordentis conscientiae intelligunt. Ergo et per ignem metaphorice exquisitissimus significatur dolor ac cruciatus.

2) Ex Matth. 25., ubi Salvator, ex instituto de extremo judicio et poenis infernalibus agens, cum dixisset: ,Discedite a me maledicti in ignem aeternum‘, statim subjungit: ,Et ibunt in supplicium aeternum.‘ Quae verba ultima videntur innuere, per ignem infernalem in genere designari supplicium gehennae gravissimum. . .

IV. denique sententia eorum est, qui hic 'επεχειν malunt, quam certi aliquid statuere. Amplectitur hanc sententiam Augustinus L. 20. de Civ. Dei c. 16., ubi inquit: ,Hic ignis, cujusmodi et in qua mundi vel rerum parte futurus sit, hominem scire arbitror neminem, nisi forte, cui Spiritus divinus ostendit.‘ . . Eandem sequitur b. Gerhardus Loc. de Infern. § 69., ubi ait: Non ambigimus, ,divina potentia fieri posse, ut ignis corporeus cruciet diabolos et animas incorporeas, sed an ignis ille revera corporeus, materialis et visibilis, an vero incorporeus, invisibilis et immaterialis sit futurus, in medio relinquimus (quamvis in partem posteriorem magis propendeamus). Ac Deum serio precamur, ne per experientiae notitiam illud nobis manifestet. Praestat, omni studio per veram ac seriam conversionem de fugiendo igne esse solicitum, quam de natura illius ignis odiose et otiose digladiari.‘ Eadem habent D. Althoferus Harm. Evang. in Luc. 16, 25. et D. Glassius Phil. Sacr.“ (Th. did.-pol. P. I. c. 14. s. 2. q. 4. f. 820—824.)

Fechtius: ״Ignis non elementarie, et tamen proprie dictus, est aqua non humida, et tamen proprie dicta. Qualis illo futurus sit, si non est elementarie, non liquet.“ (Controvers. syll. Giessae 1768. p. 95.) Vid. Matth. 3, 12., ubi πυρ ααβεατον, et cap. 25, 41., ubi αΙώνιον dicitur.§

11. Sed et sensuum organa sensusque adeo ipsos peculiaribus poenis cruciatum iri, non improbabile est.a Et de tactu quidem, stante sententia de igne proprie dicto, dubium esse non potest.b Nempe ut, qui per organa sensuum peccarunt, per eadem etiam puniantur. Vid. § praeced. Quod ad reliquorum sensuum poenas attinet, sunt, qui, quoad visum, horrenda daemonum in certa specie apparentium spectacula, damnatorum quoque aliorum aspectum; quoad auditum, gemitus proprios ac sociorum plorantium ac dentibus stridentium; quoad gustum, sapores foedos ac sitim; quoad olfactum, foetorem ignis sulphurei locum habere putant. Alii tamen ea, quae in hanc rem ex Scripturis afferuntur, metaphorice et parabolice accipiunt de doloribus gravissimis, per ea, quae homini in hac vita accidere possunt acerbissima, depictis. Vid. b. Gerhard. L. de Inferno § 71. p. 665. 666. 667.

Hafenrefferus: ,,Quinam sunt illi cruciatus? Sunt animi et corporis (utrumque enim peccaverat) exquisitissimi dolores, orti ex pavore ac sensu justissimae irae vindictaeque divinae contra peccata, quorum tristissimam conscientiam secum circumferunt, quorum turpitudo patet, quorum etiam nulla in posterum remissio et inde poe PART. 1. CAP. VII. narum nulla mitigatio aut finis sperari potest. Unde horribili lamentatione et ejulatu pristinam impietatem suam, qua jussa Domini, qua fraternas admonitiones et omnia salutis assequendae media, secure neglexerunt, miseri detestabuntur, sed frustra. Nam in perpetuo angore, tremore horribili, in pudore, confusione et ignominia, in igne inextinguibili, in fletu et stridore dentium, in aeternis et horrendis tenebris, avulsi a Dei gratia et favore, inter diabolos horrendum et sine flne in aeternum excruciabuntur. —

Nondum tamen intelligo, quales illi sint cruciatus? Resp.: Quia futura damnatorum tormenta omnem humanae mentis aciem longe excedunt, ut neque cogitatione magnitudinem illorum unquam assequi valeamus, ideo quinam aut quales illi futuri sint, verbis satis exprimi non potest. Scriptura tamen, ut, maximos et exquisitissimos istos cruciatus esse, ostendat, illis rebus eoe assimilat, quibus in hac vita summus et animi et corporis dolor excitari solet. Propterea nunc igni, nunc stridori dentium, nunc vermibus, nunc tristissimis tenebris, et quaecunque aliae res tristitiae et doloris plenissimae nominari possunt, comparantur.“ (Loc. th. 1. 3. loc. 9. p. 484—486.)

Gerhardus: ״Oculi cruciabuntur daemonum aspectu, aures supplicii sociorum stridore et gemitu, odoratus intolerabili foetore, gustus rapidissima siti ac fame, tactus et omnia membra frigore et igne. Imaginatio patietur ab apprehensione praesentium dolorum, memoria a recordatione praeteritarum voluptatum, intellectus a consideratione bonorum amissorum et malorum, ad quae devenerunt, praesentium ac futurorum. Idem judicium esto de corporis membris, in quibus omnibus ac singulis damnati patientur, quia omnibus et singulis ad creatoris ignominiam abusi ad iniquitatis arma eadem converterunt. Rom. 6, 13.“ (L. c. § 53.)

Idem: ,,Igni urenti ubique ferme conjungitur vermis rodens. Per eum vero intelligi videtur morsus conscientiae perpetuus et continuus, ex peccatorum recordatione ortus, rabida quaedam displicentia et infructuosa poenitentia, angor cordis maximus et nunquam interruptus. Ut enim vermes continuo morsu cadavera arrodunt, sic internus ille conscientiae vermis damnatorum animas perpetuo lancinabit.. Quemadmodum in cadaveribus putrescentibus nascuntur vermes, sic conscientia putrefacta vermes gignit spirituales et immortales.“ (L. c. § 51.)

Idem: ,,Quaeritur: An praeter ignem et vermem etiam aliacorporalia supplicia vere et proprie sic dicta in inferno statuenda? 1. Bonaventura 4. sent. dist. 44. art. 2. quaest. 2. disputat, in inferno non solum esse ignem punientem, sed quatuor elementa, quibus animae et corpora puniantur. . . 2. Verum frigus esse in inferno, statuit Beda. Eadem videtur sententia Hieronymi in comm. cap. 10. Matth. . . et aliorum quorum vestigiis insistunt plerique pontificii, statuentes, in inferno esse latissimum frigidissimarum aquarum receptaculum instar maris, in quod ex igne transeant damnati, a daemonibus rapti, et post ardorem patiantur frigus, ex quo stridor dentium oriatur. Sed dictum Jobi ex Hebraeo textu non est recte redditum. . .

3. Stridorem dentium in inferno esse statuunt, qui verum frigus illi attribuunt; sed quidam ex veteribus rectius metaphorice exponunt de livore ac furore damnatorum, ut vidimus superius. 4. Fletum exponunt de gemitibus continuis. Hugo Victorinus d. 1.: ,Nulla in inferno vox nisi vae, vae sonat.‘ Thomas in addit, q. 97. art. 3.: ,Fletus potest esse in damnatis secundum quandam capitis et oculorum commotionem et turbationem, sed lacrymarum resolutio et fluxus in illis esse nequit. Edent magnos gemitus, atque ea faciunt, quae flentes facere consueverunt, quamvis nullas lacrymas fundant.‘ Atqui si in voce fletus metaphoram agnoscunt, cur eam in aliis tantopere refugiunt et literae simpliciter insistunt? 5. Fumum verum, non metaphoricum, ex materia aeterni

sulphuris natum, in inferno statuit Bonaventura. . . 6. Foetorem sui phureum proprie sic dictum plerique omnes hic agnoscunt, quin et addunt, ex corporibus damnatorum tetrum odorem emittendum per species intentionales, quemadmodum ex beatorum corporibus suavis odor exhalat. 7. Fame ac siti proprie dicta damnatos torquendos esse, plurimorum est opinio. Sed videtur simplicissimum ob argumenta superius exposita, haec omnia metaphorice ac parabolice accipere de summis et ineffabilibus damnatorum cruciatibus, qui depinguntur per ea, quae homini in hac vita obtingere possunt longe acerbissima ac molestissima.“ (L. c. § 71.) §

12. Gradus poenarum infernalium fore,a negari non potest. Distinctius tamen illos definire pro diversitate quorumvis subjectorum,b non aeque facile est. Sic Christus Matth. 10, 15. cap. 11, 22. et 24. Luc. 10, 12. Judaeis sui temporis, ac speciatim incolis urbium Chorazin, Bethsaida et Capernaum, graviores poenas denunciat, quam civibus urbium Sodomae, Gomorrhae, Tyri et Sidonis. Equidem probabile est, conscientiae morsus vehementiores in illis fore deprehendendos, qui saepius graviusque contra conscientiam peccarunt; intensiores etiam quoad corpus dolores illis inflictum iri, qui corpore suo in hac vita ad exercenda peccata magis operosi fuerunt.

De infantibus gentilium autem disquiri solet: Utrum poena übrum, praeter carentiam visionis beatificae, etiam in realibus cruciatibus infemalibua constituta sit? in qua quidem quaestione b. Musaeus maluit έπέχεο; vid. Ausfiihrl. Erklärung Q. ult. p. 704. 705. Cui consona sunt, quae b. Huelsemannus scripsit in praelect. F. C. Art. VIII. 8. II. M. I. § 3. p. 444. Prop. IX., de infantibus gentilium hoc quidem pronundare nos posse, quod juxta normam verbi revelati partem in aeterna beatitudine non habeant, Joh. 3, 36. 2 Thess. 1, 8.; de qualitate autem et quantitate supplicii nihil determinare.

Quod si vero, quae quorundam nostratium sententia est, spem aliquam salutis, infantibus his per extraordinariam Dei gratiam conferendae (quanquam fortasse spem cum majore formidine oppositi conjunctam, quam ubi de salute infantum Christianorum absque baptismo decedentium sermo est) concipiamus adeoque eos damnatum non iri existimemus, quaestione de poena damni solius, aut etiam sensus, quoad hos, opus non erit.

Quenstedtius: ,,De infantibus parentum, qui extra ecclesiae pomoeria constituti sive qui foris sunt, ad nos nihil attinet judicare, juxta illud apostoli 1 Cor. 5, 13.: TmV ΐξω ό θεος κμινεϊ, cf. v. 12.“ (L. c. P. IV. c. 5. s. 2. q. 10. f. 1165.)


### Concerning Eternal Death, or Damnation: Luther: “In what state they (unbaptized infants) are, or what becomes of them,…

Luther: “In what state they (unbaptized infants) are, or what becomes of them, we commend to the divine goodness. They have neither faith nor baptism; but whether God receives them in a singular way and grants them faith, does not exist in the Word, nor do we dare to determine it.” (Ad Gen. 25:10. *Exeget. opp. lat. Cur. Elsperger. Erlang. 1830. Tom. VI. p. 123.*)

Carpzovius: “What is posited here (article 2) by the Augsburg Confession, some doctors have accepted and understood absolutely, as if PART I. CHAP. VII.

all children of infidels born outside the church are damned here, and a condemnatory sentence is passed upon them absolutely; just as D. Paul Tarnov., Prof. Rostoch., in Comm. on John, part 1, ch. 3, quest. 5, p. 265, not only draws and refers this article along with the Apology, but also the antithesis of Article IX, and refutes those who suspend judgment regarding the salvation of the children of infidels (έπεχονντας), namely Hunnius in ch. 7 of Genesis, last quest., p. 183, Meisner in Decad. 1, Anthropol. disp. 7, q. 5, p. 208 et sqq., and Gesner, disp. 14 on the F. C. ch. 11, H. 52, p. 352.

But the Aug. Conf. speaks, as is plain and clear, of those who are not regenerated at all.

However, the Aug. Conf. does not say that it is impossible for those infants to be regenerated extraordinarily and become members of the church. Rightly, therefore, is that saying of the apostle applied to the question of the salvation of these infants, 1 Cor. 5:12: "For what have I to do to judge them also that are without?"

For in that passage the apostle does not speak only of the judgment of jurisdiction, which the church has through the binding key over putrid and wicked members, but in general of the judgment which is passed by Christians concerning pagans and those outside; nor does he who thus suspends his judgment on this question pass a different judgment than what Christ has revealed in the Scriptures, John 3:18, 36 and 2 Thess. 1:8, which is what Tarnovius objects and thinks.

For what Christ and the apostle pronounced in the cited places remains true perpetually, and is also approved and asserted by us concerning those who persevere in their unbelief.

But the judgment that is passed concerning the state of infidels, insofar as they are and remain such, is one thing; the judgment concerning the modes of converting infidels is another, by which we judge and think that, even if they are not ordinarily converted and regenerated, God can nevertheless, in a way known to Himself and extraordinarily, endow the children of infidels with saving faith, even if this is unknown to us, and it does not follow that if they are not regenerated ordinarily, they must therefore be damned, since God can grant them saving faith extraordinarily. (Isagog. in libros symb. p. 153.)

Dannhauer: "It remains that we say something, or rather do not say something, about the infants, τοῖς έξω. For concerning adults who, because of the neglect of baptism, to which, as well as to repentance, they are obligated, are to be set before the final judgment, there is no question, by the express testimony of D. Paul, Acts 17:30, 31; concerning ethnic infants snatched away by sudden death, the question alone remains; but the question remains.

Let this be the buckle and the line, where Scripture (which describes the divine order, not likewise the economy) defines nothing expressly.

Although the analogy of faith makes us hope well of them, from which it is certain that no one is absolutely reprobated, and that only actual resistance contrary to the means of faith damns; such contumacy is not in those infants.

2. The example of the infants of the Ninevites. They were born outside the church to idolatrous parents; and yet the Lord looked upon them with a merciful eye (έλεήμονι οφθαλμώ), Jon. 4:11, not to destroy them with the first death, but to grant the grace of vocation to their parents and to spare them.

It is a wonder that these infants were spared, and immunity (ασυλίαν) from the first death was granted, and not likewise to the infants of the Sodomites, the antediluvians, the inhabitants of Jerusalem; but he will cease to wonder who considers that those Ninevites also, with their parents, repented in their own way: they lacked maternal milk, and hence implored divine clemency with their wailing, and were even exposed by their mothers to the enticement of mercy.

Now if the Father of mercies protects infants born outside the church from the first death, much more does He protect them from the second death, which is the greatest of all evils." (Hodosoph. Phaen. X. p. 506—508.)

Scherzer: "As regards the infants of Christians dying without baptism, that remains: it is not the deprivation, but the contempt of the sacrament that damns.

But concerning the infants of the Gentiles dying, as those who are without (τοῖς έξω), we do not judge, 1 Cor. 5:12.

But that we should assert that all are indiscriminately damned is forbidden by the infinite mercy of God, the universal will of God to save men, unless they place an obstacle, the universal merit of Christ, and the hand of the Lord to save also extraordinarily, not

abbreviated, and the prayers of the Church, poured out by the command of the Apostle in 1 Timothy 2:1 for all men without exception and founded upon the universal merit of Christ (loc. cit. vv. 3 ff.). Who, unless rashly, would say that these are in vain? It would certainly be harsh to condemn a Gentile infant absolutely, on the grounds that he did not take care to be baptized himself, which was, however, not in his power. Therefore, the contempt of the sacrament, since it has no place in them, cannot condemn them. Hence, we neither doubt their state, with the blessed Meisner (Anthropol. Decad. I, disp. 7, q. 2, p. 215), nor do we condemn them outright as the Papists do, but we hope the best for them. . . Meanwhile, they are not saved by any absolute decree, nor outside of Christ, nor without faith, as many as are saved even outside the Church. For no one can please God without faith in Christ (Hebrews 11:6), nor is the hand of the Lord shortened, so that He cannot extraordinarily kindle faith in them.” (System, loc. VII, pp. 169 ff.) §

13. The efficient cause of the evils, the complex of which is imported by damnation, can be stated neither as one nor in the same way.

For insofar as damnation imports the privation of the beatific vision and of the love and joy arising therefrom, its efficient cause, speaking per se and properly, is not given.

However, the cause of the positive acts of the intellect and will pertaining to this is the soul itself, deserted by God.

The causes of the evils of the body are partly the fire of hell, and partly the evil angels.

But insofar as damnation is viewed by way of punishment, it can thus be referred to the Triune God and Christ as the judge, as its cause.

According to those things which we have distinctly set forth from § 2 to 11.

Certainly, our theologians do not dare to call God the efficient cause of damnation, speaking absolutely. But they also not undeservedly distinguish the meritorious cause from the efficient.

Furthermore, the evils of the state of damnation themselves vary, so that not all can relate to a truly and really causing cause—especially one that is single and proximate—by way of a genuine effect. Concerning which, see § 2. For this is only of real and positive effects, not of privations. Concerning which, it was treated in § 5 and following up to 9.

Eliciting such acts within itself; although objects also contribute what is their own.

Certainly, the will, deprived of the light of glory and grace without any hope of restoration, determines itself to evil. According to § 10 and 11. See Chapter III, on angels, § 56, p. 141. (Cf. the testimonies of Scherzer and Rambach cited in Part I, ch. 3, § 56.)

Where the cause of the punishment is he who punishes, or he who by his own authority and power causes men to be subjected to the evil of punishment; which others in this place call the inflicting cause of the punishment of damnation. PART I. CHAPTER VII.

k) Who is able to destroy (and does destroy) both soul and body of the impious in hell, Matt. 10:28. Who will repay affliction (eternal damnation, which is evident from the context) to those who afflict the faithful, 2 Thess. 1:6. l) For that act of punishing is a divine work ad extra (outward).

m) This, of course, is the executor of divine judgment, using divine power and might, who will effectively command the impious, as the cursed, to depart from Him into eternal fire, so that they may immediately and actually go into eternal punishment, Matt. 25:41, 46. He, with flaming fire, will inflict vengeance on those who do not know God, etc., 2 Thess. 1:7, 8.

n) He will certainly withdraw every influx of grace; He will deny the influx necessary for conferring the light of glory and the beatific vision. Whence it is necessary that the lack of this vision and of the other goods that depend upon it should follow. Yet it is not to be established on that account that the cause of damnation is from an absolute good pleasure or decree. For this is an act of the consequent, not the antecedent, divine will, by which He is moved toward the punishment of the impious, and thus of those foreknown, insofar as they are such. Likewise, it is not to be thought that a special positive influx is attributed to God, by which the will of the damned is determined toward those things which are morally evil. For it is evident from what has been said that this also is foreign to God.

Furthermore, if any of our own deny that God is the cause of damnation, they at the same time affirm that God is the author and severe executor of the decree of damnation. See the blessed Brochmand, System. Vol. I, Book on Predestination, chap. II, Sect. II, p. 253. Who himself also writes in Vol. II, Book on Hell, chap. I, Sect. III, p. 616: That God is not the author of hell, neither insofar as it is damnation and destruction itself, Hosea 13:9, nor insofar as sin is the means leading to it, Ps. 5:5, James 1:13; but that God is to be considered the author of hell in three other ways: 1) because He prepared the place of hell, etc., Matt. 25:42; 2) because He adjudges the impious to hell, Mark 3:29, John 8:18, 36; 3) because God Himself inflicts those punishments, which are indeed horrible, but most just, 2 Pet. 2:4, Jude v. 6, 2 Cor. 5:10.

But also the blessed Gerhard, Book on Hell, § 27, teaches that God is in a certain way the cause of hell, p. 559, and in the following § 31 he says this is done by reason of preparation, threatening, infliction, and preservation, p. 565 sqq. The blessed Scherzer follows him, System. Book XXIV, § 5, p. 644 sqq. § 14.

The internal impulsive cause of the punishment of damnation on the part of God is the vindicatory justice of God. As the internal cause προηγουμένως (primarily) in this place, Gerhard acknowledges the same, l. c. § 33, p. 570. To which satisfaction must be made by those who have injured the infinite majesty, through their own sufferings, after they have refused to make another’s satisfaction their own. Some add here the veracity of God, or infallible truth, by which He is moved to fulfill His threats. And not wrongly. Although both the threats and their fulfillment proceed from divine justice.

Latin:

Lutherus: ,,In quo statu sint (non baptisati infantes) aut quid de iis flat, commendamus divinae bonitati. Non habent fidem nec baptismum; num vero singulari modo eos recipiat Deus et det fidem, non exstat in verbo, nec nos statuere audemus.“ (Ad Gen. 25, 10. Exeget. opp. lat. Cur. Elsperger. Erlang. 1830. Tom. VI. p. 123.)

Carpzovius: ״Quod ab Augustana Conf. hic (artic. 2.) ponitur, id nonnulli doctores absolute acceperunt atque intellexerunt, quasi PART. I. CAP. VII.

omnes infidelium liberi extra ecclesiam nati hic damnentur, sententiaque condemnatoria absolute in illos feratur; prout D. Paul Tarnov., Prof. Rostoch., in Comm. super Johann, part. 1. c. 3. quaest. 5. p. 265. non modo hunc articulum cum Apologia, sed etiam antithesin articuli IX. eo trahit atque refert, et έπεχονντας ac judicium de infidelium liberorum salute suspendentes, Hunnium in cap. 7. Genes, qu. ult. p. 183., Meisnerum in Decad. 1. Anthropol. disp. 7. q. 5. p. 208. et sqq., Gesnerum disp. 14. in F. C. cap. 11. H. 52. p. 352., refutat.

Verum loquitur Aug. Conf., prout planum et clarum illud est, de illis, qui plane non regenerantur.

Fieri autem non posse, ut infantes isti non extraordinarie regenerentur et membra ecclesiae fiant, Aug. Conf. non dicit. Merito igitur ad quaestionem de horum infantum salute applicatur illud apostoli 1 Cor. 5, 12.: ,Quid mea (interest), de iis, qui foris sunt, judicare?‘

Non enim in dicto isto apostolus tantum de judicio jurisdictionis, quod per ligantem elavem in putrida et scelerata membra ecclesia habet, loquitur, sed in genere de judicio, quod circa paganos et externos a Christianis fertur; nec, quod quidem Tarnovius objicit ac putat, qui ita suspendit in hac quaestione judicium suum, aliud judicium fert, quam quod Christus in Scripturis revelaverit Joh. 3, 18. 36. ac 2 Thess. 1, 8.

Nam quod Christus et apostolus in allegatis locis pronuntiarunt, id perpetuo, uti verum manet, ita etiam a nobis probatur et asseritur de perseverantibus in incredulitate sua.

Aliud autem est judicium, quod fertur de statu infidelium, quatenus tales sunt et manent; aliud vero est judicium de modis convertendi infideles, quo censemus et putamus, etiamsi non ordinarie convertantur ac regenerentur, tamen modo sibi cognito et extraordinarie Deum fide salvifica donare posse infidelium liberos, etiamsi id a nobis ignoretur, et non sequi, si ordinarie non regenerentur illi, propterea damnare debere, cum Deus extraordinarie illis fidem salvificam possit concedere.“ (Isagog. in libros symb. p. 153.)

Dannhauerus: ,,Superest, ut aliquid etiam dicamus, vel potius non dicamus, de infantibus, τ07ς έξω. Nam de adultis, qui ob neglectum baptismi, ad quem, sicut et poenitentiam, obligati sunt, quotquot judicio extremo sistendi sunt, expresso D. Pauli testimonio Act. 17, 30. 31., non quaeritur; de infantibus ethnicis cita morte abreptis solum manet quaestio; sed manet quaestio.

Hic fibula esto ac linea, ubi scriptura (quae ordinem divinum describit, non item oeconomiam) expresse nihil definit.

Quanquam quod bene de iis speremus, faciat I. analogia fidei, ex qua constat, neminem absolute reprobari, solam resistentiam actualem mediis fidei adversam damnare; cujusmodi contumacia in illis infantibus non est.

2. Exemplum infantum Ninivitarum. Erant illi geniti extra ecclesiam a parentibus idololatris; et tamen Dominus eos έλεήμονι οφϋα'λμώ respexit Jon. 4, 11., ne perderet eos morte prima, sed gratiam vocationis ipsorum parentibus faceret atque parceret.
