For Cocceius feigns that in the Old Testament there was only a toleration of sins, which could not yet be remitted because Christ had not yet suffered. But the passion of Christ operates forward and backward, as the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world (Rev. 13:8), who by His death expiated the transgressions under the Old Testament (Heb. 9:15); otherwise He would have had to suffer more often, which the apostle in v. 25 sqq. considers an absurdity, concluding by this very fact that the satisfactory and expiatory death of Christ pertained to both testaments." (System. th. loc. 16, p. 450.) §

7. The internal impulsive cause is the goodness or gratuitous favor of God. And this is indeed the cause virtually, or so-called according to our mode of conceiving, to which Scripture accommodates itself. Which the apostle calls χάρις του Θεου, the grace of God Himself (not a gift efficiently produced in us by God, but the grace which is in God), by which He pursues us, though we are unworthy (Rom. 3:24), the riches of mercy and the great love with which God has loved us (Eph. 2:4, 5), and χρηστότητα καί φιλανθρωπίαν (Titus 3:4). Baier’s Comp. ed. Walther. III. 17 PART III. CHAP. V.

Osiander: "The Papists say: Justification does not come to us only through extrinsic grace, namely the gratuitous favor of God, but also through intrinsic or infused grace, that is to say, through good works that have proceeded from grace within us. . . They object: Grace here is not opposed to works done out of grace, inasmuch as these are rather subordinated to it, but to the works of nature and the law. . . I answer: Works of the law and of nature do not exist, for they are mere sins, inasmuch as they proceed from an evil tree and are therefore evil fruits, Matt. 7. . . Paul excludes everything that can produce boasting when he says: 'By grace you have been saved, so that no one may boast.' But if by grace he understood habitual grace, not all boasting would be excluded; for he who acts out of habitual grace can boast that those fruits are not of another tree, but his own, brought forth, to be sure, through his own form, even if it was implanted in him by God." (Colleg. th. system. V, 69. sq.)

Quenstedtius: "We do not indeed deny that the grace of God is sometimes taken metonymically for the gifts of grace; however, we deny that the grace by which we are justified is anything other than the gratuitous favor and mercy of God. . . We distinguish between grace freely given (*gratis data*), which the scholastics call spiritual gifts, which are granted to a man not so much for his own salvation as for the salvation of others, see 1 Cor. 12:4, and grace making one pleasing (*gratum facientem*), through which we are rendered pleasing to God; and this is found either in God Himself, namely His benevolence, by which He reconciles us to Himself in Christ, or in us, such as faith and all theological virtues, through which we are renewed and sanctified." (L. c. s. 2. q. 2. f. 766.)

ANTITHESIS. Quenstedtius: "The antithesis of the scholastics and Papists, who make justifying grace a gift and benefit of God, or a permanent quality and an infused supernatural habit, and who pronounce anathema upon those who maintain that the grace by which we are justified is only the favor and benevolence of God. . . The Council of Trent, sess. 6, can. 11, pronounces anathema upon those who maintain that the grace by which we are justified is only the favor of God. Bellarmine, 1. 1. de gratia et lib. arb. c. 3: 'It is the common opinion of theologians,' he says, 'that grace is a supernatural habit infused into us by God, by which the soul is adorned and perfected, and is thereby rendered just and pleasing and acceptable to God.'" (L. c. s. 2. q. 2. f. 766.) §

8. The external impulsive cause, and that the principal and meritorious one, is Christ the Mediator, by reason of His active and passive obedience.

Which do…es not abolish the gratuitous favor of God in the business of justification, nor is it itself excluded by it, since it is rather owed to divine grace that God sent His Son, who might satisfy for us so that we could be justified, and that He accepts this alien merit as if it were our own. Cf. b. Mus. Disp. cit. § 23, 24, 25.

Namely, having sufficient, and therefore infinite, power or dignity, price and value, to move God to pronounce us just. Just as in Rom. 3:24 we are said to be justified by the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, or, that God in the act of justification looks upon the price

of redemption, which Christ paid for sinners, and moved or impelled by this, God remits our sins. And in 2 Cor. 5:21, it is said that God made Christ, who knew no sin (since He was innocent and supremely holy), to be sin for us (having imputed our sins to Him, as He took upon Himself our cause and our place, and thus regarded Him as a piacular victim, to be slaughtered and…righteous before God) through Him. To the same point pertains the fact that Christ is said to have been made righteousness for us by God, namely, that through Him we might be made righteous before God, 1 Cor. 1:30. For since we were not only obligated to fulfill the law of God, but also to provide satisfaction for the transgression of the law, which divine justice demands (neither of which is in our power), and Christ took upon Himself and performed both in our place, now both move God to pronounce us, for whose sake it was performed, righteous, just as if we ourselves had fulfilled the law and had ourselves provided the satisfaction due for our sins. Whence also that merit of Christ is called our righteousness.

Gerhard: "Although in many sayings of Scripture the work of redemption is attributed to the death and shedding of the blood of Christ, this is by no means to be taken exclusively, as if the holy life of Christ were thereby excluded from the work of redemption; but it is to be thought that this is done because it never shone forth more clearly that the Lord loved and redeemed us than in His passion, death, and wounds, as the pious ancients say, and because the death of Christ is as it were the final line and complement, τέλος, the end and perfection of His entire obedience, just as the apostle says in Phil. 2:8: 'Christ humbled Himself, becoming obedient to the Father even unto death, even the death of the cross.' What is more? It is plainly αδύνατον (impossible) to separate the active obedience from the passive in this merit, because in the very death of Christ that voluntary obedience and most ardent love concur, the former of which regards the heavenly Father, the latter us humans." (Loc. de justific. § 55.)

The same: "Let it therefore be certain that the active and passive obedience of Christ is the meritorious cause of our justification. But what will become of the habitual righteousness of the human nature of Christ? Will it be entirely absent from the merit of our righteousness? By no means, since the obedience and satisfaction of Christ redounds to our benefit and becomes meritorious for this reason and from this source: first, because it is the obedience of the Son of God Himself, whence the infinite dignity and majesty of the person imparts infinite power, dignity, and efficacy to His merit. John 6:51: 'My flesh is that which I will give for the life of the world' (Christ’s flesh could be given for the life of the world for this reason and from this source, because it is the very flesh of the Son of God...). Then, because it is the obedience of a most innocent, most holy, and most pure person. Heb. 7:26." (Loc. de justific. § 56.)

ANTITHESIS. Quenstedt: "Antithesis: 1. Of the Socinians, who assert that we are justified by the sole grace and kindness of God without the intervention of any merit; that the principal cause of our justification is the pure and absolute grace of God, without regard to the merit of Christ. Likewise, that not the merit of Christ, but our own obedience is the cause of justification... 2. Of certain Calvinists, such as Zacharias Ursinus, Caspar Olevianus, Johannes Piscator, and others, who place the merit of justification solely in the passive obedience, or the obedience of the passion and death of Christ... 3. Of the Papists, who sew the rags of their own works onto the merit of Christ; for they maintain: 1.) That man, through preceding dispositions elicited by the powers of free will, merits initial grace or the aids of actual grace, and justification itself, *ex congruo* (by congruity). Thus Bellarmine and others. 2.) They assert that man merits the increase of grace *ex condigno* (by condignity). Thus Alexander Pesantius and others. 3.) They also contend that man merits eternal life itself, although they teach differently concerning this merit of eternal life." (L. c. s. 2. q. 3. f. 771. sq.)

Chemnitius: "The instrumental cause is twofold: 1. Teaching, revealing, offering, and exhibiting the benefits of justification, through which God communicates those goods to us. And this is the voice of the Gospel and the use of the sacraments, or, as the ancients speak, the vocal and visible Word. 2. Receiving or apprehending, by which we apply to ourselves those goods which are offered in the Gospel, so that we may be made partakers of them. It is, therefore, as it were the hand of God delivering, and the hand of man receiving that which is delivered." (Loci th. Part. II. f. 294.)

Latin:

Usus aphorismi hujus in didacticis est, ut de fructu passionis dominicae, de materia nobis ad justitiam imputabili, deque communi justificandi modo certi simus.

In polemicis adversus pontificios, qui fructum passionis dominicae demum post prolatum in cruce verbum τετέλεσται, i. e., ,consummatum est‘, Joh. 19,30., coepisse volunt; adversus Socinianos et quosdam Remonstrantes, qui, patres tantum umbram futurorum bonorum (cum tamen non beneficia mortis Christi, sed ipse Christus exhibitus Hebr. 10, 1. per hanc vocem significetur) habuisse gratiamque Dei per transennam duntaxat adspexisse, contendunt; contra Calvinianos, qui contra suas hypotheses et contra conscientiam objiciunt, Christum non esse redemtorem universalem propterea, quod non potuerit pati pro illis, qui tempore mortis suae fuerunt in inferno, usus aphorismi hujus esse potest.“ (Theol. posit.pol. II, 369. 370. sq.)

Scherzerus: ,,Abutitur Coccejus loco apostolico, quasi Rom. 3, 25. αφεσις et 7rάρεσις ita distinguerentur, ut πάρεσις sit nuda tolerantia peccatorum, αφεσις vero perfecta remissio. Quod falsissimum est et falsa hypothesi nititur. Fingit enim Coccejus, in V. T. locum habuisse tantum tolerantiam peccatorum, quae remitti nondum potuerint propterea, quia Christus nondum esset passus. At Christi passio operatur ante et retro, tanquam agni mactati jam ab origine mundi, Apoc. 13, 8., qui morte sua expiavit et praevaricationes sub V. T., Ebr. 9, 15.; alias saepius debuisset pati, quod apostolus v. 25. sqq. pro absurdo habet, hoc ipso, mortem Christi satisfactoriam ac expiatoriam ad utrumque testamentum pertinuisse, concludens.“ (System, th. loc. 16. p. 450.) §

7. Causa impulsive a interna est bonitas seu gratuitus favor b Dei. Et ipsa quidem virtualiter causans, seu nostro modo concipiendi sic dicta, cui Scriptura se accommodat. Quam χάρη a τού Θεου, gratiam ipsius Dei (non donum a Deo in nobis efficienter productum, sed gratiam, quae sit in Deo), qua nos indignos prosequatur, appellat apostolus Rom. 3, 24., divitias miserieordiae et caritatem multam, qua Deus nos dilexerit, ad Eph. 2, 4. 5., χρψ στότητα καί φιλανθρωπίαν Tit. 3, 4· Baieri Comp. ed. Walther. III.17 PART. III. CAP. V.

Osiander: ,,Pontificii dicunt: Justificatio non tantum contingit nobis per gratiam extrinsecam, gratuitum nempe Dei favorem, sed et per gratiam intrinsecam seu infusam, nimirum per bona opera, ex gratia in nobis profecta. . . Excipiunt: Gratia hic non opponitur operibus ex gratia factis, utpote quae eidem potius subordinantur, sed operibus naturae atque legis. . . Respondeo: Opera legis et naturae non dantur, sunt enim mera peccata, utpote quae ex arbore mala proficiscuntur et proinde sunt fructus mali Matth. 7.. . Omne id, quod gloriationem potest parere, excludit Paulus, cum dicit: ,Gratia salvati estis, ne quis glorietur.‘ At si per gratiam intelligeret gratiam habitualem, non excluderetur omnis gloriatio; nam qui ex gratia habituali agit, ille potest gloriari, illos fructus non esse alterius arboris, sed proprios, prolatos scii, per formam propriam, utut a Deo inditam sibi.“ (Colleg. th. system. V, 69. sq.)

Quenstedtius: ,,Non diffitemur quidem, quandoque gratiam Dei metonymice accipi pro donis gratiae; eam tamen gratiam, qua justificamur, aliam esse negamus, quam gratuitum Dei favorem et misericordiam. . . Disting. inter gratiam gratis datam, quam scholastici vocant dona sc. spiritualia, quae non tam ad propriam, quam aliorum salutem homini conceduntur, vide 1 Cor. 12, 4., et inter gratiam gratum facientem, per quam Deo grati reddimur, et haec vel in Deo ipso reperitur, benevolentia scii., qua nos iri Christo sibi reconciliat, vel in nobis, ut fides et omnes virtutes theologicae, per quas renovamur et sanctifleamur.“ (L. c. s. 2. q. 2. f. 766.)

ANTITHESIS. Quenstedtius: ״Antithesis scholasticorum et pontificiorum, qui gratiam justificantem donum et beneficium Dei sive qualitatem permanentem et habitum supernaturalem infusum faciunt, et illis, qui statuunt, gratiam, qua justificamur, esse tantum favorem et benevolentiam Dei, anathema dicunt. . . Concilium Trident, sess. 6. can. 11. anathema dicit illis, qui statuunt, gratiam, qua justificamur, esse tantum favorem Dei. Bellarminus 1. 1. de gratia et lib. arb. c. 3.: ,Theologorum communis sententia est‘, inquit, ,gratiam esse habitum supernaturalem a Deo nobis infusum, quo anima exornatur et perficitur, adeoque justa Deoque grata et accepta redditur.‘“ (L. c. s. 2. q. 2. f. 766.) §

8. Causa impulsiva externa,a eaque principalis ac meritoria,b est Christus mediator,c ratione obedientiae suae activae et passivae.d

Quae non tollit gratuitum Dei favorem in negotio justificationis, aut ab eo ipsa excluditur, cum potius hoc ipsum debeatur gratiae divinae, quod Deus Filium suum misit, qui pro nobis satisfaceret, ut justificari possemus, quodque hoc meritum alienum, ac si nostrum esset, accipit. Conf. b. Mus. Disp. cit. § 23. 24. 25.

Nempe sufficientem, adeoque infinitam habens virtutem sive dignitatem, pretium ac valorem, movendi Deum ad nos justos pronunciandos. Prout Rom. 8, 24· dicimur justificari per redemtionem, quae est in Christo Jesu, seu, quod Deus in actu justificationis respiciat pretium

redemtionis, quod Christus pro peccatoribus solvit, eoque motus aut impulsus Deus nobis remittat peccata. Et 2 Cor. 5, 21. dicitur Deus Christum, qui peccatum non noverit (cum insons et summe sanctus esset), pro nobis fecisse peccatum (peccata nostra ei imputasse, tanquam causam nostram et vices in se suscipienti, atque ita eum spectasse velut hostiam piacularem, pro peccatis nostris mactandam et offerendam), ut nos efficeremur justitia Dei (justi coram Deo) per illum. Eodemque pertinet, quod Christus dicitur nobis factus a Deo justitia, scilicet, ut per ipsum justi fieremus coram Deo, 1 Cor. 1, 30. Cum enim non tantum obligati fuerimus ad legem Dei implendam, verum etiam ad praestandam pro legis transgressione satisfactionem, quam justitia divina postulat (quorum neutrum est in nostra potestate), Christus autem utrumque nostro loco in se susceperit ac praestiterit, jam utrumque movet Deum ad nos, quorum causa praestitum est, justos pronunciandos, aeque ac si nos ipsi legem implevissemus et satisfactionem pro peccatis debitam ipsi praestitissemus. Unde et meritum illud Christi nostra justitia dicitur.

Gerhardus: ,,Quamvis in compluribus Scripturae dictis morti et effusioni sanguinis Christi redemtionis opus tribuatur, id tamen haud quaquam exclusive accipiendum, ac si sancta Christi vita ab opere reredemtionis per hoc excludatur; sed ideo illud fleri existimandum, quia nusquam illuxit clarius, quod nos dilexit et redemit Dominus, quam in ipsius passione, morte ac vulneribus, ut loquuntur pii veteres, et quia mors Christi est velut ultima linea ac complementum, τέλος, flnis et perfectio totius obedientiae, sicut apostolus inquit Phil. 2, 8.: ,Christus exinanivit se, factus obediens Patri usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis.‘ Quid? quod plane αδύνατον est, activam obedientiam a passiva in hoc merito separare, quia in ipsa Christi morte concurrit voluntaria illa obedientia et ardentissima dilectio, quarum prior Patrem coelestem, posterior nos homines respicit.“ (Loc. de justific. § 55.)

Idem: ,,Certum igitur esto, obedientiam Christi activam et passivam esse meritoriam causam nostrae justificationis. Sed quid de habituali humanae naturae Christi justitia fiet? nun! illa a merito nostrae justitiae plane exulabit? Minime vero, cum obedientia et satisfactio Christi inde atque ideo cedat in commodum nostrum ac fit meritoria, primo, quia est ipsius Filii Dei obedientia, unde infinita dignitas et majestas personae conciliat infinitam vim, dignitatem atque efficaciam ejusdem merito. Joh. 6, 51.: ,Caro mea est, quam dabo pro mundi vita‘ (inde atque ideo Christi caro pro mundi vita dari potuit, quia est ipsius Filii Dei propria caro. . .). Deinde, quia est innocentissimae, sanctissimae ac purissimae personae obedientia. Hebr. 7, 26.“ (Loc. de justiflc. § 56.)

ANTITHESIS. Quenstedtius: ,,Antithesis: 1. Socinianorum, asserentium, nos sola Dei gratia ac benignitate nullius interventu meriti justificari; principalem justificationis nostrae causam esse puram ac absolutam Dei gratiam, sine intuitu meriti Christi. Item, non Christi meritum, sed nostram obedientiam justificationis causam esse. . . 2. Quorundam Calvinianorum, ut Zach. Ursini, Casp. Oleviani, Joh. Piscatoris et al., qui meritum justificationis in sola passiva seu passionis et mortis Christi obedientia. . . ponunt. . . 3. Pontificiorum, qui merito Christi operum suorum lacinias assuunt, statuunt enim, 1.) hominem per praevias dispositiones, ex viribus liberi arbitrii elicitas, mereri primam gra PART. III. CAP. V. tiam vel auxilia gratiae actualis, ipsamque justificationem ex congruo. Ita Bellarminus et al. 2.) Asserunt, hominem mereri ex condigno augmentum gratiae. Ita Alexander Pesantius et al. 3.) Contendunt etiam, hominem ipsam vitam aeternam mereri, de quo tamen merito vitae aeternae diversimode docent.“ (L. c. s. 2. q. 3. f. 771. sq.)

Chemnitius: ,,Duplex est causa Instrumentalis, 1. docens, patefaciens, offerens et exhibens beneficia justificationis, per quam Deus nobis communicat bona illa. Et haec est vox evangelii et usus sacramentorum vel, sicut veteres loquuntur, verbum vocale et visibile. 2. Recipiens seu apprehendens, qua nobis applicamus illa bona, quae in evangelio offeruntur, ita ut eorum participes reddamur. Est igitur quasi manus Dei tradens et hominis manus suscipiens id, quod traditur.“ (Loci th. Part. II. f. 294.)


### On Justification: Gerhardus: "The instrumental cause on the part of God is the Word and the…

Gerhardus: "The instrumental cause on the part of God is the Word and the sacraments, through which and in which the benefits of Christ are offered to men; on our part, it is faith, which embraces and applies to itself the goods offered in the Word and the sacraments. Hence, some say that the organic cause of justification is twofold: one internal, namely faith; the other external, namely the Word and the sacraments. If one wishes to speak accurately, he would call the instrumental cause with respect to God the ministry of the Word and the dispensation of the sacraments, so that it may be intimated that the Word of God preached and announced in the ecclesiastical ministry, and the sacraments as they are administered and dispensed, are understood here, through which media the Holy Spirit wills to be effective and to kindle, increase, and confirm faith in the hearts of men." Luke 24:47: "Thus it behooved Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead the third day, and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name"; Acts 13:38: "Through Christ is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins, and by all things from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses"; Rom. 10:17: "Faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God"; 2 Cor. 5:18: "God hath reconciled us to himself by Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation." The Word, therefore, both ακουστόν [audible] and ορατόν [visible], is the instrumental cause of justification, namely in the legitimate use divinely constituted and ordained, which we have declared more broadly by the similitude of the scepter of King Ahasuerus—not resting, but touched—in the tract de Evang. § 47. (Loc. de justific. § 64.)

Meisnerus: "Two media occur in the one act of justification: the one δοτικόν [giving] on the part of God, which is the Word with the sacraments; the other ληπτικόν [receiving] on the part of us, which is faith and the apprehension of grace. Just as in the reception of any gift, both the hand of the giver and the hand of the receiver are required, so in the spiritual reception of righteousness, both are also necessary: the offering of God through the Word and the acceptance of man through faith. Therefore, just as we are properly said to be justified by the Word and sacraments as the offering media, so also by faith as the apprehending medium. For God would never remit sins unless man apprehended grace; therefore, faith or fiduciary apprehension, because it has the nature of a medium, is rightly and properly said to justify. For instrumental causes are not to be opposed to principal causes in the business of our justification, but all are to be joined together. God justifies us, the merit of Christ justifies, the Word with the sacraments justifies, faith justifies, we are justified by the remission of sins. All are said properly, but not in the same way. God justifies πρῴτως [primarily] and principally; Christ ἱλαστικῶς [propitiatorily] or meritoriously; the Word δοτικῶς [givingly] or oblatively; faith ληπτικῶς [receivingly] or apprehensively; the remission of sins οὐσιωδῶς [essentially] and formally. Our pious ancestors embraced all these, and indeed the whole foundation of our salvation and Christianity, in this brief but truly golden aphorism: 1. God gives it, 2. Christ earns it, 3. The Word proclaims it, 4. Faith receives it, 5. The sacraments seal it, 6. The Holy Spirit confirms it, 7. Works bear witness to it."

8. the cross tests it, 9. the Last Day reveals it, which things, being most worthy of note, can for the sake of memory be included in these verses: 1. God gives, 2. Christ acquires, 3. the Word exhibits, 4. True faith draws, 5. the holy symbols confirm, 6. the Spirit is the earnest, 7. Deeds prove, 8. the cross explores, 9. the great light reveals.

( Philosoph, sobr. I, 429. sq.) Carpzovius: “This must still be added: that the Augsburg Confession treats of the Word and Sacraments here (Art. 5) as they are instrumental means and act by way of physical operation, since the question in this place is whence faith comes and whether the Word and Sacraments produce it. For besides this mode of operation, another belongs to the Word and Sacraments, which is moral in nature and consists in the giving, offering, or bestowing, conferring, and sealing of the justifying good. For one must not confuse the action of the Word and Sacraments insofar as they generate, nourish, and excite faith, and the action of the Word insofar as it concurs proximately to justification. For while in the former action the Word and Sacraments behave as organs both effective of supernatural powers for believing and excitative of the spiritual motions of faith, in the latter—namely, in justification—they are at least dative, collative, and obsignative organs of the justifying good, which is the obedience of Christ. Whence, just as the mode of operation of the Word and Sacraments must be accepted in the former way in the doctrine of conversion and in this place, where the inquiry is concerning the origin of faith, so it is accepted in the latter way in the doctrine of justification, insofar as and to the extent that the Word and Sacraments concur proximately to it.” (Isag. in libros symbol. p. 251.)

Apology of the A. C.: “One cannot deal with God, God cannot be apprehended, except through the Word. Therefore, justification is effected through the Word, as Paul says in Rom. 1:16: ‘The Gospel is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth.’” (Art. 4, p. 98 sq.)

Smalcald Articles: “We will now return to the Gospel, which gives counsel and help against sin in more than one way; for God is superabundantly rich in His grace. First, through the oral Word, in which the forgiveness of sins is preached to the whole world, which is the proper office of the Gospel. Second, through Baptism. Third, through the holy Sacrament of the Altar. Fourth, through the power of the keys, and also through the mutual conversation and consolation of brethren, Matt. 18: ‘Where two are gathered together, etc.’” (P. III, art. 4, p. 319.)

Hollazius: “That the Eucharist is an exhibitive medium of justifying grace is clear from the fact that the pouring out of the eucharistic cup is said to be done for the remission of sins, Luke 22:20.

Obs.: Through the Sacrament of the Altar, justification is continued rather than begun, for the reason that no one becomes a partaker of the body and blood of the Lord with saving fruit unless he has first examined himself, i.e., whether he is in the faith, 1 Cor. 11:28, and thus has already been a believer and justified beforehand and in a state of reconciliation; meanwhile, however, justifying faith is confirmed and preserved through the Sacrament of the Altar, and thus justification is continued.”

(Exam. P. III, S. 1, c. 8, q. 8, p. 903.) Luther: “The enthusiasts of the present day also push the first commandment; they say: We also proclaim grace and mercy through Christ and do not reject the article of the first commandment, and they say that I, Luther, lie about them. But look at them regarding this: they confess the dead Christ, who hung on the cross and made us blessed—that is true; but they deny that through which we receive Him, that is, the means, the way, the bridge, and the path; these they break down.

The Jews also believe that there is a God, but they deny the way by which one comes to God, namely, through Christ’s humanity. The Turk also confesses God, but denies the way, the means, the bridge upon which one comes to God; that is, they do not want the grace of God, Christ, nor any Sacraments, through which one...” PART III. CHAP. V. of grace comes. It is the same and goes with them as if I were to preach to someone: "There I have a treasure," and yet did not hold the treasure before his nose, nor give him the keys to it—what would this treasure help him? They lock away from us the treasure that they ought to hold before our noses, and lead me on a wild goose chase: they refuse and take from me the access and the delivery, the use and the possession of the treasure.

Therefore, the enthusiasts also say much about God, about the forgiveness of sins and the grace of God, and also that Christ has died; but as to how I obtain Christ and how grace comes to me, so that I get it, so that we come together, there they say: "The Spirit must do it alone." They lead me on a wild goose chase: they say that the external and oral Word, Baptism, and the Sacrament are of no use, and yet they preach about grace. That, to me, is called announcing the treasure and speaking finely of it, but taking away the key and the bridge upon which I am to come to the treasure.

Now, God has ordained it so that this treasure is given and offered to us through Baptism, the Sacrament of the Altar, and the external Word. For these are the means and instruments through which we come to God’s grace. They deny this.

I say this because the devil is so quick and confesses these words, but he denies the means through which we come to it; that is, they do not deny the treasure, but the use and benefit of the treasure; they take and withdraw from us the manner, means, and ways by which we come to it and are made partakers of the treasure, and how we should and may come to grace. "You must," they say, "have the Spirit"; but how I can have the Spirit, that they will not let me have. Now, how can I receive the Spirit and believe, if the Word of God is not preached to me and the Sacraments are not administered? I must have the means; for faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the oral Word, Rom. 10:17.

Summa summarum: No sect can arise that does not run counter to the First Commandment and stumble over Christ Jesus, and in this article all heretics are gathered together in one sum. Therefore, let us remain by the article: "You shall have no other gods," and pay diligent attention to this purpose and scope. For if we let it out of our sight, then the gate and door are flung wide open to all spirits of faction.

God has never wanted to have His worship in the world without external means. In the Old Testament, He gave the Jews a way by which one should find Him; there was a certain place of the Tabernacle or Tent of Meeting, the altar, the lampstand, the Levites, and God did not let Himself be found without external means and ways. He always proposed an external means to them, so that they might indeed find Him; He did not let them wander about in error without a way and external means.

Latin:

Gerhardus: Instrumentalis causa ex parte Dei sunt verbum et sacramenta, per quae et in quibus beneficia Christi hominibus offeruntur, ex parte nostra fides, quae oblata in verbo et sacramentis bona amplectitur sibique applicat; inde quidam causam organicam justificationis dicunt aliam esse internam, fidem scilicet, aliam externam, verbum scilicet et sacramenta. Si quis accurate velit loqui, causam instrumentalem respectu Dei vocaverit ministerium verbi et dispensationem sacramentorum, ut innuatur, verbum Dei in ministerio ecclesiastico praedicatum et annunciatum ac sacramenta, prout administrantur et dispensantur, hic intelligi, quae per media Spiritus Sanctus in cordibus hominum vult esse efficax et fidem in illis accendere, augere et confirmare. Luc. 24, 47.: ,Sic oportebat Christus pati et resurgere a mortuis tertia die et praedicare in nomine ejus poenitentiam et remissionem peccatorum‘; Act. 13, 38.: ,Per Christum annunciatur vobis remissio a peccatis et ab omnibus, quibus non potuistis in lege Mosis justificari‘; Rom. 10, 17.: ,Fides ex auditu, auditus vero per verbum Dei‘; 2 Cor. 5,18.: ,Deus nos reconciliavit sibi per Christum et dedit nobis ministerium reconciliationis.‘ Verbum igitur tum ακουστόν tum ορατόν est causa Instrumentalis justificationis, nimirum in legitimo usu divinitus constituto et ordinato, quod similitudine D. Brentii a sceptro regis Ahasveri non quiescente, sed contacto desumta in tract. de Evang. § 47. latius declaravimus.“ (Loc. de justiflc. § 64.)

Meisnerus: ,,Duo in uno justificationis actu media occurrunt, alterum δοτικόν ex parte Dei, quod verbum est cum sacramentis, alterura λ1/πτικόν ex parte nostri, quod fides est et gratiae apprehensio. Sicut in omni alicujus muneris receptione requiritur et manus dantis et manus acceptantis, sic in spirituali justitiae δοχϊ! utrumque etiam est necessarium, oblatio Dei per verbum et acceptatio hominis per fidem. Igitur quemadmodum proprie dicimur justificari verbo et sacramentis ut mediis offerentibus, ita et fide ceu medio apprehendente. Nunquam enim Deus peccata remitteret, nisi homo gratiam apprehenderet, ideoque fides vel flducialis apprehensio, quia habet rationem medii, recte et proprie justificare dicitur· Non enim sunt opponendae causae instrumentales principalibus in negotio justificationis nostrae, sed omnes conjungendae. Justificat nos Ileus, justificat Christi meritum, justificat verbum cum sacramentis, justificat fides, justificamur remissione peccatorum. Omnia dicuntur proprie, sed non eodem modo. Justificat Deus πμώτως et principaliter; Christus ίλασηκώς vel meritorie; verbum δοτικώς vel oblative; fides ληπηκώς vel apprehensive; remissio peccatorum ονσιωδώς et formaliter. Haec omnia adeoque totum salutis nostrae et christianismi fundamentum pii majores nostri complexi sunt brevi hoc, sed vere aureo aphorismo: 1. Gott gibts, 2. Christus erwirbts, 3. das Wort verkündigts, 4. der Glaub empfähets, 5. die Sacramente versiegelns, 6. der Heilige Geist bekräftigte, 7. die Werke bezeugens,

8. das Kreuz prüfts, 9. der jüngste Tag eröffnets, quae cum notatu sunt dignissima, memoriae causa his versiculis includi possunt: 1. Dat Deus, 2. acquirit Christus, 3. verbum exhibet, 4. haurit Vera fides, 5. firmant sacra symbola, 6. Spiritus arrha est, 7. Facta probant, 8. crux explorat, 9. lux magna revelat.“ ( Philosoph, sobr. I, 429. sq.)

Carpzovius: ,,Hoc addi adhüc debet, Augustanam Confessionem de verbo et sacramentis hic (artic. 5.) agere, prout operantia media sunt et per modum operationis physicae agunt, cum quaestio sit hoc in loco, unde fides sit et an verbum et sacramenta eandem operentur. Praeter hunc enim operandi modum verbo et sacramentis alius competit, qui moraliter sese habet et in datione, porrectione seu oblatione, collatione et obsignatione boni justifici consistit. Neque enim confundi debent actio verbi et sacramentorum, quatenus fidem generant, alunt atque excitant, et actio verbi, prout ad justificationem concurrit proxime. Cum enim in priori actione verbum et sacramenta sese habeant ut organa tum effectiva virium supernaturalium ad credendum, tum excitativa motuum spiritualium fidei, in posteriori, sc. in justificatione, organa saltem dativa sunt, collativa et obsignativa boni justifici, quod est obedientia Christi. Unde, sicuti priori modo in doctrina de conversione et hoc in loco, ubi de origine fidei quaeritur, accipi debet modus operandi verbi et sacramentorum, ita posteriori modo in doctrina de justificatione accipitur, quatenus et in quantum proxime verbum et sacramenta ad eam concurrunt.“ (Isag. in libros symbol. p.251.)

Apologia A. C.: ,,Cum Deo non potest agi, Deus non potest apprehendi, nisi per verbum. Ideo justificatio fit per verbum, sicut Paulus inquit Rom. 1, 16.: ,Evangelium est potentia Dei ad salutem omni credenti‘.“ (Art. 4. p. 98. sq.)

Articuli Smalcaldici: ,,Wir wollen nun wieder zum Evangelio kommen, welches gibt nicht einerlei Weise, Rath und Hilfe wider die Sünde; denn Gott ist überschwänglich reich in seiner Gnade. Erstlich durchs mündliche Wort, darin geprediget wird Vergebung der Sünde in aller Welt, welches ist das eigentliche Amt des Evangelii. Zum andern durch die Taufe. Zum dritten durchs heilige Sacrament des Altars. Zum vierten durch die Kraft der Schlüssel, und auch per mutuum colloquium et consolationem fratrum Matth. 18.: Ubi duo fuerint congregati etc.“ (P. III. art. 4. p. 319.)

Hollazius: ,,Eucharistiam esse medium exhibitivum gratiae justificantis, liquet ex eo,. quia effusio poculi eucharistici dicitur fieri in remissionem peccatorum, Luc. 22, 20.

Obs.: Per sacramentum coenae continuatur potius, quam inchoatur justificatio, propterea, quod nemo cum salutari fructu corporis et sanguinis dominici fit particeps, nisi qui seipsum prius probaverit, sc. num sit in fide, 1 Cor. 11, 28., adeoque fidelis et jam ante justificatus et in statu reconciliationis fuerit; interim tamen fides justifica per sacramentum coenae confirmatur et conservatur atque adeo justificatio continuatur.“ (Exam. P. III. S. 1. c. 8. q. 8. p. 903.)

Lutherus: ,,Die Schwärmer heutiges Tages treiben auch alle das erste Gebot; sagen: Wir verkündigen auch Gnade und Barmherzigkeit durch Christum und verwerfen nicht den Artikel des erstön Gebotes, und sagen, ich, Lutherus, lüge sie an. Aber siehe ihnen darauf: sie bekennen den gestorbenen Christum, der am Kreuz gehangen und uns selig gemachet, das ist wahr; aber sie leugnen das, wodurch wir ihn bekommen, das ist, das Mittel, den Weg, die Brücke und Steig, den brechen sie ein.

Die Juden glauben auch, dass ein Gott sei, aber den Weg, wie man zu Gott komme, nämlich durch Christi Menschheit, verleugnen sie. Der Türke bekennt auch Gott, aber verleugnet den Weg, das Mittel, die Brücke, darauf man zu Gott kommet, das ist, die Gnade Gottes, Christum wollen sie nicht haben, auch keine Sacramente, dadurch man zu PART. III. CAP. V. der Gnade kommet. Es ist gleich und gehet mit ihnen, als wenn ich Einem predigte: Da habe ich einen Schatz; und hielt ihm doch den Schatz nicht vor die Nase, gäbe ihm auch nicht die Schlüssel dazu, was hülfe ihm dieser Schatz? Sie schliessen uns den Schatz zu, den sie uns sollten vor die Nase stellen, und führen mich auf einen Affenschwanz: den Zutritt und die Ueberreichung, den Brauch und Besitzung des Schatzes weigert und nimmt man mir.

Sagen darum die Schwärmer auch viel von Gott, von Vergebung der Sünden und der Gnade Gottes, auch dass Christus gestorben sei: aber wie ich Christum erlange und wie die Gnade zu mir kommet, dass ich sie kriege, dass wir zusammenkommen, da sagen sie: der Geist muss es alleine thun; führen mich auf den Affenschwanz: sagen, das äusserliche und mündliche Wort, die Taufe und Sacrament sei kein nütze, und predigen doch von der Gnade. Das heisset mir den Schatz verkündigen und fein davon sagen; aber den Schlüssel und die Brücke weggenommen, darauf ich zum Schatze kommen soll.

Nun hat es Gott also geordnet, dass dieser Schatz durch die Taufe, das Sacrament des Abendmahls und äusserliche Wort uns gegeben und dargereichet wird. Denn das sind die Mittel und Instrumente, dadurch wir zu Gottes Gnade kommen. Das verleugnen sie.

Das sage ich darum, dass der Teufel so geschwinde ist und bekennet diese Worte, aber er verleugnet das Mittel, dadurch wir dazu kommen, das ist, sie leugnen nicht den Schatz, sondern Brauch und Nutz des Schatzes; sie nehmen und entziehen uns die Weise, Mittel und Wege, wie wir dazu kommen und des Schatzes gemessen und wie wir zur Gnade kommen sollen und mögen. Du musst, sagen sie, den Geist haben; aber wie ich den Geist haben kann, das wollen sie mir nicht lassen. Nun, wie kann ich den Geist überkommen und glauben, wenn man mir nicht prediget das Wort Gottes und die Sacramente reichet? Ich muss das Mittel haben; denn der Glaube kommet aus dem Gehör, das Gehör aber durch das mündliche Wort, Rom. 10, 17.

Summa Summarum: Es kann keine Rotte aufkommen, sie muss wider das erste Gebot laufen und an Christum Jesum sich stossen, und werden in diesem Artikel alle Ketzer in einer Summa gesammlet. Darum lasset uns bleiben bei dem Artikel: Du sollt nicht andere Götter haben; und auf diesen Zweck und Scopum fleissig Achtung haben. Denn lassen wir es uns aus den Augen thun, so ist allen Rottengeistern Thor und Thür aufgesperret.

Gott hat nie ohne äusserliche Mittel seinen Gottesdienst in der Welt haben wollen. Im Alten Testament hat er den Juden eine Weise gegeben, dabei man ihn sollte finden; da war ein gewisser Ort des Tabernakels oder Hütten des Stifts, der Altar, Leuchter, die Leviten, und liess Gott sich nicht finden ohne äusserliche Mittel und Weise. Er hat ihnen allewege ein äusserliches Mittel vorgeschlagen, damit sie ihn ja finden sollten; er liess sie nicht ohne Weise und äusserlich Mittel in der Irre herumgehen.


### On Justification: But, as our enthusiasts now run about and depart from this way which God has…

But, as our enthusiasts now run about and depart from this way which God has given us in the New Testament, so the Jews also abandoned the same way and sought other paths.

God cannot be our God unless He gives us something external by which we may find Him, such as the oral Word and the two Sacraments. If I do not grasp God through external things, how then can I encounter Him? Therefore, all heretics have been against the First Commandment and have offended against it in all sorts of human works and cut out the promise and grace of God that is placed therein; indeed, they deny God Himself, rejecting the benefit and use, so that one may not come to grace." (Interpretation of several chapters of the 5th Book of Moses. 1529. Jena. Tom. III. p. 2501 sqq.)

The same: "One sees this in all enthusiasts and spirits of faction throughout, that they are all in the error that they do not understand how sins are forgiven. For ask the Pope and all his doctors, and they will not be able to tell you what absolution

accomplish; for upon this doctrine the whole Papacy stands: that grace is infused into man through a secret operation, and whoever wishes to attain it must repent, confess, and make satisfaction. But if one asks what the Absolution and the Keys do, they say it is an external order that is maintained in the Church. Thus, they do not place the forgiveness of sins upon the Word and faith, where it must be placed, but upon our repentance, confession, and satisfaction. But such is entirely a fabricated doctrine, by which people are seduced and pointed to the wrong path.

Thus the Anabaptists also say: What should Baptism do for the forgiveness of sins? It is, after all, only a handful of water! The Spirit must do it if we are to be truly cleansed from sins; the water cannot do it. They therefore also draw the forgiveness of sins away from the Word and will not let it remain as it is, as the pious little people say here, that such power has been given to men. The Sacrament-enthusiasts also say likewise, that there is only bread and wine in the Sacrament, therefore one cannot find the forgiveness of sins there; the Spirit must give it, the flesh is of no use.

In sum: no sectarian spirit, no priest nor monk has been able to see that the forgiveness of sins is a power given to men, as it stands here in the Gospel. Therefore learn here, so that you may be able to speak of the matter: I know well, and also confess, that God alone forgives sin; but I must also know this, whereby I may perceive that my sins are forgiven me.

There the Holy Scripture teaches me and all Christians that, if I want to have the forgiveness of sins, I must not sit in a corner and say: My God, forgive me my sin, and then wait for an angel to come from heaven and tell me: Your sins are forgiven you.

For God promises that He will come down to me and Himself promise me the forgiveness of sins. Such happens firstly in Holy Baptism; for there is His command that I should be baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. And furthermore, there stands with such command the promise: He who believes and is baptized will be saved, Mark 16:16. Yes, you say, is Baptism not just water? It is true; but it is not water alone, it is God’s Word with it.

Thus, when you go to your pastor, who has a special command for such things, or otherwise to a Christian, and desire that he comfort you and absolve you of your sins, and he says to you: I, in the stead of God, announce to you through Christ the forgiveness of all your sins: here you should be certain that your sins are truly and certainly forgiven you through such an external Word, for Baptism and the Word will not lie to you...

Therefore the Anabaptists and other sects have at once lost the forgiveness of sins, Baptism, the Sacrament, the Christian Church, and all Christian works, because they cast away the Word which they hear from their neighbor and consider it nothing other than if a cow were bleating. Now, even if God were to speak through a cow or another animal, as He once spoke through a donkey, one should nevertheless not despise His Word, but let it be valid; why then would one despise it because men speak it by God’s command and order? For although you hear a human voice, you are nevertheless hearing God and certainly find the forgiveness of sins therein, if you only accept it with faith.” (Hauspostille. Sermon for the 19th Sunday after Trinity. Halle Ed. Vol. XIII, 2078—2080.)

The same: “Thereafter, think that the Keys or the forgiveness of sins does not rest upon our repentance or worthiness, as they teach and pervert; for that is entirely Pelagian, Turkish, heathen, Jewish, Anabaptistic, enthusiastic, and antichristian; but, on the contrary, that our repentance, works, heart, and whatever we are, should PART III. CHAP. V. ...build upon the keys and, with full consideration, confidently rely upon them as upon God’s Word, and in the loss of body and soul, by no means doubt what the keys say and give to you; it is as certain as if God Himself were speaking it; for He does indeed certainly speak it Himself; for it is His command and Word, and not a man’s word or command. But if you doubt, you are calling God a liar, perverting His order, and building His keys upon your repentance and worthiness. You ought to repent (that is true), but that the forgiveness of sins should become certain because of that, and confirm the work of the key, that is to forsake faith and deny Christ. He does not want to forgive and grant you sin for your sake, but for His own sake, out of pure grace, through the key. . .

Christ says: What you bind on earth, etc. Note here that He has certainly, certainly promised that what we bind and loose on earth shall be bound and loosed; here is no "false key." He does not say: "What I bind and loose in heaven, that you shall also bind and loose on earth," as the teachers of the "false key" fool themselves. When would we ever find out what God binds or looses in heaven? Never, and the keys would be in vain and of no use. He also does not say: "You shall know what I bind and loose in heaven"; who would or could know? But this is what He says: "If you bind and loose on earth, then I will also bind and loose in heaven; if you do the work of the keys, then I will do it too; yes, when you do it, then it shall be done, and it is not necessary that I do it after you." What you bind and loose (I say), that I will neither bind nor loose, but it shall be bound and loosed without My binding and loosing; it shall be one and the same work, Mine and yours, not two different ones; one and the same key, Mine and yours, not two different ones; do your work, and Mine is already done; if you bind and loose, then I have already bound and loosed. He obligates and binds Himself to our work; yes, He commands us to do His own work; why then should we make it uncertain, or reverse it and pretend that He must first bind and loose in heaven? Just as if His binding and loosing in heaven were something different than our binding and loosing on earth, or as if He had other keys up in heaven than these on earth, when He nevertheless clearly and plainly says that they are the keys of heaven and not the keys of the earth. . .

But such thoughts about two kinds of keys come from the fact that one does not hold God’s Word to be God’s Word, but because it is spoken by men, one looks at it just as if it were human words, and thinks that God is high above and far, far, far away from such a word that is on earth, stares up toward heaven for it, and imagines yet other keys. . .

Do not let yourself be led astray here by the Pharisaical chatter with which some fool themselves, asking how a man can forgive sin when he cannot give grace, nor the Holy Spirit. Remain with the words of Christ and be certain that God has no other way to forgive sin than through the oral Word, which He has commanded to us men. Where you do not seek forgiveness in the Word, you will stare in vain toward heaven for grace or, as they say, for "inner forgiveness."

But if you speak, as the sectarians and sophists also do: "Many hear the binding and loosing of the keys, yet they do not turn from their ways and remain bound and unloosed, therefore there must be something else than the Word and the keys: the Spirit, Spirit, Spirit must do it." But do you think that he who does not believe the binding key is not bound? He shall surely experience in his own time that, because of his unbelief, the binding has not been in vain, nor has it failed. Likewise, he who does not believe that he is loosed and his sin forgiven, he shall also in time surely experience how very certain his sins were already forgiven him, and he did not want to believe it. St. Paul says Romans...

3, 3.: “Because of our unbelief, God will not fail. We are not speaking now of who believes the keys or who does not; we know quite well that few believe; rather, we are speaking of what the keys do and give. Whoever does not accept it, indeed has nothing; the key does not fail on that account. Many do not believe the Gospel, but the Gospel does not fail or lie on that account. A king gives you a castle: if you do not accept it, the king has not lied or failed, but you have deceived yourself and it is your fault; the king has certainly given it. . . For it is God’s command and word that the one speaks and the other hears; both are bound, upon the salvation of their souls, to believe this as certainly and firmly as all other articles of faith.” (Writing on the Keys. 1530. XIX, 1172—1177.) §

9. The less principal impulsive cause is faith in Christ. This indeed moves God to justify man, yet not by its own dignity, power, or value, but by the virtue and dignity of the object which it apprehends.

In the Solid Declaration of the Formula of Concord, this is expressed thus: Faith does not justify because it is itself such a good work and such an excellent virtue, but because it apprehends and embraces the merit of Christ in the promise of the Gospel, *de Justif. Fid.* p. m. 684.

Latin:

Aber, wie unsere Schwärmer jetzt laufen, und lassen von dieser Weise, welche uns Gott gegeben hat im Neuen Testament, also verliessen die Juden auch dieselbige Weise und suchten andere Wege.

Gott kann nicht unser Gott sein, er gebe uns denn etwas Aeusserliches, daran wir ihn finden, als das mündliche Wort und die zwei Sacramente. Wenn ich Gott nicht ergreife durch äusserliche Dinge, wie kann ich ihn denn antreffen? Darum sind alle Ketzer wider das erste Gebot gewesen und haben sich daran vergriffen in allerlei Menschenwerken und schneiden aus die Verheissung und Gnade Gottes, so darein gesteckt ist, ja, verleugnen Gott selbst, verwerfen den Nutzen und Brauch, dass man zu der Gnade nicht kommen möge.“ (Auslegung über etliche Capitel des 5. Buchs Mosis. 1529. Hai. Tom. III. p. 2501. sqq.)

Idem: ,,Das siehet man an allen Schwärmern und Rottengeistern durchaus, dass sie alle in dem Irrthum sind, dass sie nicht verstehen, wie die Sünden vergeben werden. Denn frage den Pabst und alle seine Doctores, so werden sie dir nicht können sagen, was die Absolution

ausrichte; denn auf dieser Lehre bestehet das ganze Pabstthum: die Gnade werde dem Menschen eingegossen durch eine heimliche Wirkung, wer dazu kommen wolle, der müsse reuen, beichten und genugthuh. So man aber fragt, was die Absolution und die Schlüssel thun, sprechen sie, es sei eine äusserliche Ordnung, die in der Kirche gehalten werde. Stellen also die Vergebung der Sünden nicht auf das Wort und den Glauben, da sie doch muss auf gestellet werden, sondern auf unsere Reue, Beichte und Genugthuung. Aber solches ist durchaus eine erlogene Lehre, dadurch die Leute verführet und auf den Unrechten Weg gewiesen werden.

Also sagen die Wiedertäufer auch: Was sollte die Taufe zur Vergebung der Sünden thun? Ists doch nur eine Hand voll Wassers! Der Geist muss es thun, so wir recht von Sünden sollen rein werden; das Wasser kann’s nicht thun. Ziehen also Vergebung der Sünden auch vom Wort hinweg und wollens bei dem nicht lassen bleiben, wie die frommen Leutlein hier sagen, dass solche Macht den Menschen gegeben sei. Die Sacramentsschwdrmer sagen auch also, es sei im Sacrament nur Brot und Wein, darum könne man Vergebung der Sünden da nicht finden, der Geist müsse es geben, das Fleisch sei kein nütz.

In Summa: kein Rottengeist, kein Pfaff noch Mönch hat das können sehen, dass Vergebung der Sünden sei eine Macht, den Menschen gegeben, wie es hie stehet im Evangelio. Darum lerne hie, dass du könnest von der Sache reden: Ich weiss wohl, bekenne auch, dass Gott allein die Sünde vergibt; aber ich muss auch dies wissen, wobei ichs merken könne, dass die Sünden mir vergeben werden.

Da lehret die heilige Schrift mich und alle Christen, wenn ich Vergebung der Sünden will haben, müsse ich mich nicht in Winkel setzen und sagen: Mein Gott, vergib mir meine Sünde, und alsdenn warten, wenn ein Engel vom Himmel komme und mir sage: Deine Sünden sind dir vergeben.

Denn Gott verheisset, er wolle sich zu mir herunter finden und selbst Vergebung der Sünden mir Zusagen. Solches geschieht erstlich in der heiligen Taufe; denn daselbst ist sein Befehl, dass man mich taufen soll im Namen des Vaters und des Sohnes und des Heiligen Geistes. Und stehet ferner bei solchem Befehl die Zusagung: Wer da glaubt und getauft wird, der wird selig werden, Marc. 16, 16. Ja, sprichst du, ist doch die Taufe nur Wasser! Wahr ists; aber solch Wasser ists nicht allein, es ist Gottes Wort dabei.

Also wenn du zu deinem Seelsorger gehest, der solches einen sonderlichen Befehl hat, oder sonst zu einem Christen, und begehrest, dass er dich tröste und absolvire von deinen Sünden, und er zu dir spricht: Ich, anstatt Gottes, verkündige dir durch Christum Vergebung aller deiner Sünden: hie sollst du gewiss sein, dass dir deine Sünden durch solch äusserlich Wort wahrhaftig und gewiss vergeben sind, denn die Taufe und das Wort werden dir nicht lügen. . .

Darum haben die Wiedertäufer und andere Rotten zugleich Vergebung der Sünden, Taufe, Sacrament, die christliche Kirche und alle christliche Werke verloren, weil sie das Wort, so sie von ihrem Nächsten hören, wegwerfen und für anders nicht halten, denn so irgend eine Kuh blekete. Nun, wenn denn Gott gleich durch eine Kuh oder ander Thier redete, wie er einmal durch eine Eselin geredet hat, sollte man gleichwohl sein Wort nicht verachten, sondern gelten lassen; warum will mans denn verachten, dass es die Menschen aus Gottes Befehl und Ordnung reden? Denn ob du wohl eines Menschen Stimme hörest, so hörest du doch Gott und findest gewisslich Vergebung der Sünden dabei, wenn du es nur mit Glauben annimmst.“ (Hauspostille. Predigt Dom. XIX. p. Trin. Hai. Tom. XIII, 2078—2080.)

Idem: ,,Darnach denke, dass die Schlüssel oder Vergebung der Sünden nicht stehet auf unserer Reue oder Würdigkeit, wie sie lehren und verkehren; denn das ist ganz pelagianisch, türkisch, heidnisch, jüdisch, wiedertäuferisch, schwärmerisch und endechristisch; sondern, wiederum, dass unsere Reue, Werk, Herz und wTas wir sind, sollen sich PART. III. CAP. y. auf die Schlüssel bauen und mit ganzem Erwägen getrost darauf ver· lassen, als auf Gottes Wort, und bei Leibs und Seelen Verlust ja nicht zweifeln, was dir die Schlüssel sagen und geben, es sei so gewiss, als־ rede es Gott selber; wie ers denn gewisslich selbst redet; denn es ist sein Befehl und Wort und nicht eines Menschen Wort oder BefehL Zweifelst du aber, so lügenstrafest du Gott, verkehrst seine Ordnung und bauest seine Schlüssel auf deine Reue und Würdigkeit. Reuen sollst du (das ist wahr), aber dass darum die Vergebung der Sünden sollte gewiss werden und des Schlüssels Werk bestätigen, das heisst den Glauben verlassen und Christum verleugnet. Er will dir die Sünde nicht um deinetwillen, sondern um sein selbst willen, aus lauter Gnaden, durch den Schlüssel vergeben und schenken. . .

Christus spricht: Was ihr bindet auf Erden u. s. w. Merke hie, dass er gewiss, gewiss zugesagt, es solle gebunden und los sein, was wir auf Erden binden und lösen; hie ist kein Fehlschlüssel. Er spricht nicht: Was ich im Himmel binde und löse, das sollt ihr auf Erden auch binden und lösen, wie die Lehrer des Fehlschlüssels narren. Wann wollten wir erfahren, was Gott im Himmel binde oder lösete? Nimmermehr, und wären die Schlüssel vergebens und kein nütze. Spricht auch nicht: Ihr sollt wissen, was ich im Himmel binde und löse; wer wollte oder könnte wissen? Sondern so spricht er: Bindet ihr und löset auf Erden, so will ich mit binden und lösen im Himmel; thut ihr der Schlüssel Werk, so will ichs auch thun; ja, wenn ihrs thut, so solls gethan sein, und ist nicht noth, dass ichs euch nachthue. Was ihr bindet und löset (spreche ich), das will ich weder binden noch lösen, sondern es soll gebunden und los sein ohne mein Binden und Lösen; es soll einerlei Werk sein meines und eures, nicht zweierlei; einerlei Schlüssel meine und eure,, nicht zweierlei; thut euer Werk, so ist meines schon geschehen; bindet und löset ihr, so hab ich schon gebunden und gelöset. Er verpflichtet und verbindet sich an unser Werk; ja, er beflehlet uns sein selbst eigen Werk; warum sollten wirs denn ungewiss machen, oder umkehren und vorgeben, er müsse vorhin binden und lösen im Himmel? Gerade als wäre sein Binden und Lösen im Himmel ein anders, denn unser Binden und Lösen auf Erden, oder als hätte er andere Schlüssel droben im Himmel, denn diese auf Erden, so er doch deutlieh und klärlich saget, es seien des Himmels Schlüssel und nicht der Erde Schlüssel. . .

Es kommen aber solche Gedanken von zweierlei Schlüsseln daher, dass man Gottes Wort nicht für Gottes Wort hält, sondem weil es durch Menschen gesprochen wird, 80 siehet man es eben an, als wärens Menschenworte, und denkt, Gott sei hoch droben und weit, weit, weit von solchem Wort, das auf Erden ist, gaffet darnach gen. Himmel hinauf und dichtet noch andere Schlüssel. . .

Lass dich hie nicht irren das pharisäische Geschwätz, damit sich Etliche selbst närren, wie ein Mensch möge Sünde vergeben, so er doch die Gnade nicht geben kann, noch den Heiligen Geist.: Bleibe du bei den Worten Christi und sei du gewiss, dass Gott keine andere Weise hat, die Sünde zu vergeben, denn durch das mündliche Wort, so er uns Menschen befohlen hat. Wo du nicht die Vergebung im Worte suchst, wirst du umsonst gen Himmel gaffen nach der Gnade oder, wie sie sagen, nach der innerlichen Vergebung.

Sprichst du aber, wie die Rottengeister und Sophisten auch thun: Hören doch viel der Schlüssel Binden und Lösen, kehren sich dennoch nicht dran und bleiben ungebunden und ungelöset, darum muss etwas anders da sein, denn das Wort und die Schlüssel: der Geist, Geist, Geist muss es thun. Meinst du aber, dass der nicht gebunden sei, der dem Bindeschlüssel nicht gläubet? Er solls wohl erfahren zu seiner Zeit, dass um seines Unglaubens willen das Binden nicht vergeblich gewesen ist, noch gefehlet hat. Also auch, wer nicht gläubet, dass er los sei und seine Sünde vergeben, der solls mit der Zeit auch wohl erfahren, wie gar gewiss ihm seine Sünden jetzt vergeben sin$ gewesen und ers nicht hat wollen gläuben. St. Paulus spricht Röm~

3, 3.: Um unsers Unglaubens willen wird Gott nicht fehlen. So reden wir auch jetzt nicht, wer den Schlüsseln glaubt oder nicht; wissen fast wohl, dass wenig glauben.; sondern wir reden davon, was die Schlüssel thun und geben. Wers nicht annimmt, der hat freilich nichts; der Schlüssel fehlet darum nicht. Viel gläuben dem Evangelio nicht, aber das Evangelium fehlet und lüget darum nicht. Ein König gibt dir ein Schloss: nimmst du es nicht an, so hat der König darum nicht gelogen noch gefehlet, sondern du hast dich betrogen und ist deine Schuld, der König hats gewiss gegeben. . . Denn es ist Gottes Befehl und Wort, das jener spricht und dieser hört; sind beide schuldig, bei ihrer Seelen Seligkeit, solches so gewiss und fest zu gläuben, als alle andere Artikel des Glaubens.“ (Schrift von den Schlüsseln. 1530. XIX, 1172—1177.) §

9. Causa impulsiva minus principalis a est fides b in Christum.c Quae quidem Deum movet ad hominem justificandum, verum non sua propria dignitate, vi aut valore, sed virtute ac dignitate objecti, quod apprehendit.

In Solida Declar. Form. Cone, hoc sic exprimitur: Fidem non justificare, quod ipsa tam bonum opus tamque praeclara virtus sit, sed quia in promissione evangelii meritum Christi apprehendit et amplectitur, de Justif. Fid. p. m. 684.


### On Justification: Others say that faith relates to justification instrumentally or organically

Others say that faith relates to justification instrumentally or organically; others, relatively; which, as far as the matter pertains, agree with the opinion concerning the less principal impulsive cause; yet this latter declares the present matter most conveniently.

For those who speak of an instrumental cause, if they understand a physically efficient cause, do not so much express the relation of faith to the act of justification itself (which it is certain is not an act really produced, much less one that is produced by a physical instrumental cause), as the relation of habitual faith to the actual apprehension of the merit or righteousness of Christ (for faith, taken for the act of believing itself, is not the cause of the apprehension, but is the apprehension of the merit of Christ itself); where, however, it must further be confessed that faith, taken for the habit of believing, is rather the principal cause of its acts than the instrumental (just as other supernatural habits are the physically efficient and principal causes of their acts), so that, when faith is called the instrumental cause of the apprehension of the merit of Christ, it seems it must be accepted in the sense in which any principle by which something is done is called an instrument; just as faith, apprehending the merit of Christ and the grace of God offered in the evangelical promises, is commonly compared to a hand extended to apprehend alms.

But if they call faith an instrumental cause in relation to the act of justification itself, it is necessary that it be understood as a morally moving cause, and that not by its own dignity, goodness, or merit, but by the goodness, dignity, and merit of another principal cause; in this way, however, an instrumental cause in the category of morals is the same as a less principal impulsive cause. See the blessed Musaeus, *Dissert. de Aet. Elect. Decr.* cap. II. § 67. sqq. p. 48. sqq.

Those, however, who say that faith justifies relatively or correlatively, certainly understand that faith, by the power of its correlative, which is the merit of Christ, contributes something to our justification, and indeed morally. PART. III. CAP. V.

by] moving the will of God, by virtue of the merit of Christ, toward our justification. Whence, again, the rationale under which faith concurs toward our justification cannot be other than that which befits an impulsive cause. Confer, blessed Musaeus, 1. c. § 78. p. 54, 55.

That some of our own [theologians] refused to call faith an impulsive cause came about because they were persuaded that every external impulsive cause imports a certain merit, or at least a goodness, dignity, and proper perfection, by which the will of the efficient cause might be moved to act; for the distinction of cause into principal and less principal was not found to be inculcated in the doctrine of the impulsive cause as it was in the doctrine of the efficient cause among the ancient metaphysicians. See blessed Musaeus, 1. c. § 62, 63. p. 43, 44.

Quenstedtius: "The mediate cause is on one side of God and δοτική (giving), on the other side of man and ληκτική (receiving). The δοτικά on the part of God are the Word and the Sacraments; for through them the justifying and saving obedience of Christ is offered to be apprehended by the faith conferred in regeneration and is applied to the believer, Luke 24:47; 2 Cor. 3:9; 5:18. Note: The ὄργανα δοτικά and προσφερόμενα, or the datival and offering [instruments] on the part of God, are the Word and the Sacraments, and indeed 1) regarding the announcement and oblation of the justice of Christ and the remission of sins, Luke 24:47; 2) regarding the application; and 3) regarding the generation, confirmation, and augmentation of faith. Hence we say in the thesis that the justifying and saving obedience of Christ is first offered through these means to be apprehended by faith, and then applied to the believer. And therefore the preaching of the Gospel is called διακονία τῆς δικαιοσύνης, the ministry of righteousness, 2 Cor. 3:9, and διακονία τῆς καταλλαγῆς, the ministry of reconciliation, 2 Cor. 5:18.

The ληκτική on the part of man is faith leaning upon the merit of Christ, Rom. 3:22, 25; Phil. 3:9; Col. 1:23; 2:7; Gal. 3:7, 8, 9, 11, 12, and indeed faith alone, Rom. 3:28; Gal. 2:16; Eph. 2:8, 9.

Note: The instrumental cause on the part of the man receiving justification, or the organon ληκτικόν and καταληκτικόν or receptive [instrument], by means of which we receive and embrace Christ with His benefits, is faith, Rom. 3:22: 'But the righteousness of God διά πίστεως, through faith, of Jesus Christ,' etc.; v. 25: 'Whom God set forth as a propitiation διά τῆς πίστεως, through faith, in His blood.' Faith, however, speaks formally, and insofar as it justifies, of the appropriative apprehension of the most perfect obedience of Christ, which is its proper object, insinuated by the words ἐν τῷ αὐτοῦ αἵματι, in His blood.

This blood denotes (for it is not the case that, leaving aside the proper signification, we should take the word αἵματος metonymically for the doctrine sanctioned by blood, as Grotius does) by a synecdoche customary in Scripture the whole bloody sacrifice of Christ, not excluding the remaining obedience rendered to the heavenly Father by acting and suffering throughout the whole course of His life. The particle διά, through, indicates the organic cause by which, on our part, the blood of the ἀπολυτρώσεως καὶ ἱλαστηρίου is applied.

Hence we are also said to be justified, to receive grace, and to live in Christ πίστει, Acts 26:18; ἐκ πίστεως, Rom. 3:30; Gal. 3:7, 8, 9, 11, 12; διά τῆς πίστεως, ibid. and v. 31; μετὰ πίστεως, with faith, 1 Tim. 1:14; ἐπὶ τῇ πίστει, Phil. 3:9; ἐν πίστει, in faith, 1 Tim. 3:13; Col. 1:23; 2:7; κατὰ πίστιν, according to faith, Heb. 11:13...

There is, therefore, in the act of justification a causality of faith entirely its own, yet it is none other than organic, insofar as it justifies by apprehending the merit of Christ; the rationale of causing, the justifying power, is competent to faith not in itself and insofar as it is an apprehension and our act, or in itself and its own nature, or having some dignity, whether small or great, from the liberal estimation or acceptance of God, but solely from the justifying object apprehended, Rom. 3:25.

Note: One must well distinguish the causality of faith in the act of justification and the rationale of causing; the causality of faith consists in apprehending and receiving, i.e., it is none other than organic and instrumental, for by apprehending or rather receiving the grace of God..."

The merit of Christ, when apprehended and applied and appropriated to oneself individually, justifies. The Holy Scriptures designate this apprehension with the words λαμβάνειν (John 1:12; 17:8; Rom. 5:17; Gal. 3:14), καταλαμβάνειν (John 1:5), παραλαμβάνειν (5:11, ibid.), επιλαμβάνειν (Gal. 4:12), δέχεσθαι (Luke 8:13; Acts 8:14; James 1:21), and αποδέχεσθαι (Acts 2:41; 1 Tim. 1:15). The pronouns of application and possession—"my," "me," "to me," etc.—insinuate this appropriation, as in Job 19:25, Isa. 45:24, Cant. 2:16, John 20:28, and Gal. 2:20 sq.

The reason for the causality, or the justifying power, does not belong to faith in itself and in its own nature, or insofar as it is an apprehension; for it could apprehend imaginary merits of one’s own or human righteousness, and yet it would not justify in that way. Nor does it belong to it by a liberal estimation or acceptilation of God, as if God esteemed faith so highly that He bestowed upon it the dignity and value of justifying; but it belongs to it solely from the justifying object apprehended, or by reason of the object, insofar as it apprehends the merit of Christ. St. Paul indicates this expressly in Rom. 3:25, namely, that the entire justifying power depends upon the thing apprehended—that is, upon the bloody merit of Christ, which is the proper object of justifying faith as such.

Just as, for example, when the hand of a starving man apprehends bread that has been offered, that apprehension as such does not satisfy the man—for he could apprehend mud or a stone or other things by which he could not be satisfied—but the entire satisfaction depends upon the object apprehended and eaten, namely, the bread; and just as when one who is thirsty draws water from elsewhere, namely from a fountain, by means of a bucket, that drawing as such does not quench the thirst—for he could draw sand or blood through the bucket; but it quenches the thirst because the drink which he draws has the power to quench thirst: so he who hungers or thirsts for righteousness (Matt. 5:6) does indeed apprehend by faith, as with a begging hand, the bread which descends from heaven (John 4:50, 51), and with this bucket draws for the thirsty soul the water springing up into eternal life (John 4:14). Yet that apprehension and drawing as such neither drives away spiritual hunger nor quenches such thirst; for such a man could apprehend something else heterogeneous—which does not possess this divine efficacy, for example, imaginary merits of one’s own and the satisfactions which the Roman synagogue invents, or those of the saints—but the entire power of the apprehension depends upon the thing apprehended through faith, namely, the απολύτρωσις and the blood of Jesus Christ, in which the Apostle expressly hints that it is founded (Rom. 3:25). (L. c. s. 1. th. 8—11. f. 742. sqq.)

The same [Quenstedtius]: "When faith is called an instrument by us (because it justifies not by its own power, but by another’s), we do not cling so strictly to the word 'instrument,' as to whether faith is an instrument in the most famous sense of the term. For we do not wish to contend with anyone about that matter, provided it remains certain that through faith we receive solely the remission of sins, and that faith is the medium apprehending the grace of God and the merit of Christ. For we take 'instrumental cause' or 'instrument' in a broader sense, for any medium whatsoever that receives and contains something. Therefore, faith is said to justify ὀργανικῶς, not because faith remits sins or absolves from sins, not because it imputes to us the righteousness of Christ instrumentally, as God does this principally, but because faith apprehends the remission of sins and the absolution which God offers and wills to confer upon us through the Word and Sacraments, and because it accepts the righteousness of Christ and applies the same to us." (L. c. s. 2. q. 2. f. 794.)

Carpzovius: "We significantly say that faith is an apprehensive instrument. For instruments or organs are not all of one kind. For some instruments are operative, which cooperate with the principal cause or which work the effect with their agent, just as a saw is an instrument in cutting wood; some, however, are dative, through which something provided by another is exhibited, or which offer to others an effect produced by another, just as the hand of a rich man distributes alms to a poor man; some, indeed, are apprehensive, by which the offered thing is received and converted into our own possession, just as the hand of the poor man takes the alms. And faith is of this last kind of instrument, because it relates correlatively to its object, namely, to the obedience of Christ, who is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes, Rom. 10:4, which it receives unto itself, whence it is called ἀποδοχή, reception, 1 Tim. 1:15, and is explained by the words λαμβάνειν, καταλαμβάνειν, John 1:5, 11, 12. For faith cannot be referred to the second kind, because in this way it would be confused with the Gospel and the Sacraments, which are the organs offering and exhibiting the righteousness of Christ; much less, indeed, to the first. For faith contributes nothing nor cooperates toward justification, but only apprehends the righteousness imputable for salvation, nor is it required and employed for any other end than that the obedience offered through the Gospel may also become ours by imputation, just as the hand, by which a beggar apprehends alms, contributes nothing to the alms itself, e.g., the coin or the bread, which have already obtained their being from the minter or the baker, and just as a bucket is not the cause of the quenching of thirst, but the water, and is employed for no other end than that the water may also become ours. Hence it may be doubted whether faith can rightly be called the instrumental cause of our justification, since it is not an operative instrument of our justification." (Isagog. in lib. symbol. p. 206.)

Latin:

Alii dicunt, fidem instrumentaliter aut organice, alii, relative se habere ad justificationem, quae quidem, quantum ad rem attinet, cum sententia de causa impulsiva minus principali conveniunt; haec vero rem praesentem commodissime declarat.

Nam qui instrumentalem causam dicunt, si causam physice efficientem intelligant, non tam exprimunt habitudinem fidei ad ipsum actum justificationis (quem non esse actum realiter productum, nedum talem, qui per causam instrumentalem physicam producatur, certum est), quam habitudinem fidei habitualis ad.actualem apprehensionem meriti seu justitiae Christi (fides enim, pro ipso actu credendi accepta, non est causa apprehensionis, sed ipsa apprehensio meriti Christi); ubi tamen porro fatendum est, fidem, pro habitu credendi acceptam, esse potius causam principalem suorum actuum, quam instrumentalem (prout alii habitus supernaturales suorum actuum causae physice efficientes ac principales sunt), ut adeo, quando fides dicitur causa instrumentalis apprehensionis meriti Christi, id eo sensu accipiendum videatur, quo instrumentum dicitur quodlibet principium quo; prout etiam vulgo fides, meritum Christi et gratiam Dei in promissionibus evangelicis oblatam apprehendens, cum manu ad apprehendendam eleemosynam extensa comparatur.

Quod si fidem in ordine ad ipsum actum justificationis causam instrumentalem dicant, necesse est, intelligi causam moraliter moventem, idque non sua dignitate, bonitate aut merito, sed bonitate, dignitate ac merito alterius causae principalis; ita vero causa Instrumentalis in genere morum idem est, quod causa impulsiva minus principalis. Vid. b. Mus. Dissert. de Aet. Elect. Decr. cap. II. § 67. sqq. p. 48. sqq.

Qui autem fidem dicunt justificare relative aut correlative, intelligunt utique, fidem vi correlati sui, quod meritum Christi est, ad nostri justificationem aliquid conferre, et quidem mora PART. III. CAP. y.

liter, movendo voluntatem Dei, vi meriti Christi, ad nostri justificationem. Unde iterum ratio, sub qua fides ad nostri justificationem concurrit, non alia esse potest, quam quae causae impulsivae convenit. Confer, b. Mus. 1. c. § 78. p. 54. 55.

Quod autem nostrates aliqui fidem causam impulsivam dicere recusarunt, inde factum est, quod persuasum haberent, causam impulsivam externam omnem importare meritum quoddam, vel certe bonitatem, dignitatem et perfectionem propriam,״ qua voluntas causae efficientis ad agendum moveatur; quippe quod distinctio causae in principalem et minus principalem in doctrina de causa impulsiva non ita, ut in doctrina de causa efficiente apud veteres metaphysicos inculcata reperiretur. Vid. b. Mus. 1. c. § 62. 63. p. 43. 44.

Quenstedtius: ,,Causa media alia ex parte Dei et δοτική, alia ex parte hominis et ληκτική est. Δοτική ex parte Dei sunt verbum et sacramenta; per ea enim fidei in regeneratione collatae apprehendenda offertur et credenti applicatur obedientia Christi justifica et salvifica, Luc. 24, 47. 2 Cor. 3, 9. 5, 18. Nota: v0pyava δοτικά et κροσψερόμενα seu dativa et offerentia a parte Dei sunt verbum et sacramenta, et quidem 1.) quoad annunciationem et oblationem justitiae Christi et remissionis peccatorum, Luc. 24, 47., 2.) quoad applicationem et 3.) quoad fidei generationem, confirmationem et augmentationem. Hinc dicimus in thesi, quod obedientia Christi justifica et salvifica per haec media primum fidei apprehendenda offeratur, deinde credenti applicetur. Et propterea evangelii praedicatio vocatur διακονία τής δικαιοσύνης, ministerium justitiae, 2 Cor. 3, 9., διακονία τής καταλλα^ής, ministerium reconciliationis, 2 Cor. 5, 18. Δηκτική

ex parte hominis est fides innixa Christi merito, Rom. 3, 22. 25. Phil. 3, 9. Coi. 1, 23. 2, 7. Gal. 3, 7. 8. 9. 11. 12., et quidem sola, Rom. 3, 28. Gal. 2, 16. Eph. 2, 8. 9.

Nota: Causa instrumentalis a parte hominis justificationis recipientis sive organon ληκτικόν et καραληκτικόν sive receptivum, quo mediante Christum cum suis beneflciis recipimus et amplectimur, est fides, Rom. 3, 22.: ,Justitia autem Dei διά κίστεως, per fidem, Jesu Christi‘, etc.; v. 25.: ,Quem proposuit Deus propitiationem διά τής πίστεως, per fidem, in ipsius sanguine.‘ Dicit autem fides formaliter, et qua justificat, apprehensionem appropriativam perfectissimae Christi obedientiae, quae proprium illius objectum est, insinuata per verba εν τφ αντον αίματι, in ipsius sanguine.

Notat autem sanguis hic (neque enim est, ut relicta propria significatione vocem αίματος metonymice pro doctrina per sanguinem sancita cum Grotio accipiamus) per synecdochen Scripturae usitatam totum Christi cruentum sacrificium, non exclusa reliqua obedientia agendo et patiendo per omnem vitae cursum Patri coelesti praestita. Particula διά, per, indicat causam organicam, qua ex parte nostri sanguis ακολντρύσεως καί ιλαστηρίου applicatur.

Hinc dicimur quoque justificari, gratiam percipere et vivere in Christo κίστει Act. 26, 18., έκ κίστεως Rom. 3, 30. Gal. 3, 7. 8. 9. 11. 12., διά τής κίστεως ibid. et v. 31., μετά κίστεως, cum fide 1 Tim. 1, 14., έκϊ τη κίστει Phil. 3, 9., εν κίστει, in fide 1 Tim. 3, 13. Coi. 1, 23. 2, 7., κατά κίστιν, secundum fidem Hebr. 11, 13. . .

Est itaque fidei in actu justificationis omnino sua causalitas, non tamen alia, quam organica, quatenus sc. apprehendendo Christi meritum justificat, ratio causandi, vis justifica est, competens fidei non in se et quatenus est apprehensio et actus noster, sive in se et sua natura, sive ex liberali Dei aestimatione seu acceptatione, dignitatem aliquam, sive parvam sive magnam, habens, sed unice ex objecto justifico apprehenso, Rom. 3, 25.

Nota: Bene distinguenda est fidei in actu justificationis causalitas et ratio causandi; causalitas fidei consistit in apprehendendo et recipiendo, h. e., non est alia, quam organica et instrumentalis, apprehendendo enim seu potius recipiendo Dei gratiam et

Christi meritum apprehensumque sibi in individuo applicando et appropriando justificat. Apprehensionem designant sacrae literae verbis λαμβάνειν Joh. 1, 12. 17, 8. Rom. 5, 17. Gal. 3, 14., καταλαμβάνειν Joh. 1, 5., παραλαμβάνειν 5, 11. ibid., επιλάμβάνειν Gal. 4, 12., δέχεσθαι Luc. 8, 13. Act. 8, 14. Jac. 1, 21., αποδεχεσθαι Act. 2, 41. 1 Tim. 1, 15. Appro־ priationem insinuant pronomina applicativa et possessiva,meus‘, ,me‘, ,mihi‘ etc.,· ut Jobi 19, 25. Esa. 45, 24. Cant. 2, 16. Joh. 20, 28. Gal. 2, 20. sq.

Ratio causandi seu vis justifica competit fidei non in se et in sua natura, sive quatenus est apprehensio; posset enim apprehendere merita propria imaginaria vel justitiam humanam, neque tamen sic justificaret, nec competit ipsi ex liberali Dei aestimatione seu acceptilatione, quasi Deus tanti fidem aestimet, ut justificandi dignitatem et valorem ipsi tribuat, sed unice ex objecto justifico apprehenso sive ratione objecti, quatenus scii, apprehendit meritum Christi. Hoc S. Paulus expresse indicat Rom. 3, 25., scii, totam vim justificam dependere a re apprehensa, videlicet a cruento Christi merito, quod fidei justificantis, qua talis, objectum proprium est.
