out, that one might therefore neglect Baptism or that it might be sufficient; that someone might want to pretend that he has faith and does not need Baptism: for whoever becomes a Christian and believes will certainly also gladly accept such a sign, so that he may have both—such divine testimony and confirmation of his salvation—with him, and may strengthen and comfort himself with it throughout his whole life, and that he may also publicly confess this before all the world. Just as both parts belong to a Christian, as Paul says in Romans 10:10: "With the heart one believes before God and in himself, and with the mouth one confesses before the world."

Although it can happen that one may also believe even if he is not baptized, and conversely, some receive Baptism who yet do not truly believe.

Therefore, one must understand this text in such a way that Baptism is hereby commanded and confirmed as that which one should not despise, but use, as has been said, and yet not draw the lines so tightly that someone should be damned for that reason who could not come to Baptism.

And in sum, these four propositions arise from this text: 1. That some believe and are baptized; which is generally the command of Christ and the rule that one should teach and keep. 2. Some believe and are not baptized. 3. Some do not believe and yet are baptized. 4. Some do not believe and are not baptized.

The text itself provides such a distinction. And it has always been held unanimously that if someone were to believe and yet die unbaptized, he would not be damned for that reason, for the case may perhaps occur that one believes and, although he desires Baptism, is overtaken by death (as can sometimes happen with young children, before, or in, or even after their birth, who are nevertheless previously offered and commended to Christ through the faith and prayer of their parents or others, whom He also, according to His words: "Let the little children come to me," etc., undoubtedly accepts)." (Ev. Kirchenpostille. Opp. Hai. XI, 1332. sqq.)

Dannhauerus: "How great the necessity of Baptism is, the Savior Himself teaches by a clear assertion: 'Unless one is born again of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God,' which exception is resolved into this expository statement: 'No αβάπτιστος [unbaptized person] shall enter the kingdom of heaven.' I say αβάπτιστος, privatively, who, although he could and ought to be baptized, nevertheless spurns the counsel of God against himself.

For that it should be taken negatively and infinitely of every unbaptized person simply, the following do not permit: 1. The general scope of the evangelical Scripture, which is consolation. 2. The particular scope of Christ’s colloquy, which is the refutation of the Pharisaism that despises the counsel of God concerning Baptism. For He is dealing with a ruler of the Pharisees, as if He were saying: You and those like you despise the baptism of John, but I say that no αβάπτιστος [unbaptized] despiser shall enter the kingdom of heaven.

Therefore, Christ is speaking of those who ought to be, and who can be, baptized, but who despise it...

7. The abundance of instances, drawn from the converted thief. He undoubtedly entered paradise αβάπτιστος; for he would have been baptized either before the cross, or on it, or after it: not before, because no one ought to be baptized without the repentance of adults; not after the cross, because he was then dead; not on the cross, because, as to what some have opined concerning the water poured from the side of Christ, Suarez himself refutes it: 'It is,' he says, 'scarcely credible that the water issued from the side with such force that it reached the thief, especially if it is true that this thief held the right side of Christ, while the water flowed from the left side of Christ.'

What Gretserus trifles concerning the baptism of blood, that is both foreign and blasphemous; 'for that thief,' these are the words of Augustine, 'was not crucified for the name of Christ, but for the merits of his own crimes; nor did he suffer because he believed, but while he was suffering, he believed.'

You will say with Augustine: In the thief, the will to receive was not lacking, but the necessity of not receiving was present. You may say the same of unbaptized infants, that the will is not lacking in them, namely, as the schools distinguish, a virtual one." (Hodosoph. p. 504. sqq.) PART III. CHAP. X.

Carpzovius on the words of the Augsburg Confession, Art. 9: "They (the Anabaptists) affirm that infants are saved without baptism," he adds: "That is, by the ordinary reason and way destined for the salvation of infants. Otherwise, it is not denied regarding an extraordinary mode of regeneration. For it is one thing to say that one cannot be saved without faith; it is another to say that one cannot be saved without baptism. The former is absolutely true; the latter, however, holds only regarding the ordinary reason and mode, which God has established not for Himself, but for men." (Isagog. p. 335.)

ANTITHESIS. Quenstedtius: "Antithesis: 1. Of certain ancient Fathers, who formerly commonly judged that those who expired before receiving baptism were excluded from the kingdom of heaven. The voice of many was: 'They are not crowned if they are not initiated.' Augustine, T. 3, l. de fide ad Petr. Diac., c. 27, writes: 'Hold most firmly and doubt not at all, that not only men who are already using their reason, but also infants, who either begin to live in their mothers' wombs and die there, or who, when born from their mothers, pass from this world without the sacrament of holy baptism, which is given in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, are to be punished with the everlasting torment of eternal fire.' Sometimes, however, Augustine assigns a most mild and light damnation to unbaptized (αβαπτίστοις) infants, as in l. 1 de peccator. merit. c. 15 and l. 5 c. Jul. Pelagianum c. 8. Athanasius, T. 2, in Qu. ad Antioch. qu. 90, after citing the dictum of Christ in John 3:5, adds: 'It is manifest that no one unbaptized shall enter into that (kingdom of heaven).' From Cyprian it is clear that those catechumens who had undergone martyrdom before they were washed were excepted from that strict censure. For the holy martyr says in Epist. 73 to Jubaianus: 'They are not deprived of the sacrament of baptism, inasmuch as they are baptized with the most glorious and greatest baptism of blood.' The same is affirmed by Gennadius, l. 1 de eccles. dogmatibus (which is wrongly ascribed to Augustine), c. 74. Theophylact also, in c. 16 of Mark, pronounces that 'catechumens,' even if they believe, are not yet saved 'unless they are also baptized.'

2. Of the Scholastics, who establish that unbaptized infants perish. Thus Lombard, l. 4 sent. dist. 1, lit. L, says: 'If, however, it is asked concerning infants who died before the eighth day, before which circumcision was not performed according to the law, whether they were saved or not, the same can be answered as is felt concerning infants who died before baptism, whom it is certain perish.' Thomas, P. 3, q. 65, a. 4, teaches: 'that baptism is absolutely necessary for salvation.' P. 3, qu. 68, he says: 'They can in no way be saved who have received the sacrament of baptism neither in reality nor in desire.' It is, however, the opinion of Thomas concerning infants who died without having received baptism, that they are damned in the underworld with eternal death, but yet are punished by the lack of the vision of God, which is called the penalty of loss, in such a way that they suffer no pain at all, neither internal nor external; see his own Quaest. 5 de malo, a. 1, 2, 3.

3. Of the Papists, who also defend this harsh opinion. Bellarmine, l. 1 de baptismi sacr. c. 4: 'The Church has always believed that infants perish if they depart from this life without baptism.' And at the end of that chapter he sets forth this gnome: 'All who die in infancy, if they are predestined, are without doubt baptized, and conversely, if they are reprobate, they are not baptized.' They imagine, however, such a torment for unbaptized infants, by which the penalty of loss, not of sense, is inflicted upon them, i.e., they establish that they are deprived of the vision and sight of God, but that they feel no torments at all." (L. c. s. 2, q. 10, f. 1166 sq.)

For we cannot equally conceive a hope of salvation concerning these from divine revelation. Cf. what was added above to P. I, c. 7, § 12, Vol. II, p. 213 sqq. Namely, when these children ought to be returned to their parents, and it should be permitted that they themselves educate them, who without doubt are going to educate them in their idolatry, it is to be feared that, in the meantime, by baptizing those children, holy things might be cast to the dogs. Otherwise, however, if the infants of infidels have come into the power of Christians in a legitimate manner, and thus can be justly preserved and educated in the true religion and faith, just as it can be conferred upon those who are educated and instructed and thus converted and requesting baptism, so it is permitted to baptize them in their very infancy if the danger of death is imminent.

Hartmannus: "God certainly did not will that the faith be propagated and the sacraments administered to anyone with injury to parental right, seeing that otherwise a great disturbance of affairs would follow and the Gospel, together with the sacraments, would be rendered hateful to the nations; whence the apostles never snatched children away against the will of their parents. If, however, an infant were by chance, shipwreck, or some other way removed from the power of the parents, and the parents were either entirely ignorant of or despaired of their restoration, then the infant is by all means to be baptized." (Pastorale ev. p. 640.)

Latin:

Sic autem etiam b. Gerhardus 1. c.: De infantibus in ecclesia natis, ait, melius speramus. Et paulo post: Infantes illos, qui vel in utero materno, vel repentino quodam casu ante baptismi susceptionem extinguuntur, temere damnare nec possumus, nec debemus; quin potius statuimus, preces piorum parentum, vel, si parentes in hac parte negligentes fuerunt, preces ecclesiae ad Deum pro his infantibus fusas clementer exaudiri eosdemque in gratiam et vitam a Deo recipi. At<que hanc in rem quidem argumenta plura adducit § 238. 239. Determinatum modum agendi autem, quo Deus utatur per gratiam extra,ordinariam, non aeque tangit.

Lutherus: ,,Es lässt Christus daran genug sein, dass er im ersten Stück dieses Spruchs sagt: ,Wer da gläubet und getauft wird‘; und im andern: ,Wer aber nicht gläubet‘ u. s. w., die Taufe nicht wiederholet; freilich darum, dass es mit dem ersten genug angezeiget und anderswo weiter davon befohlen, als Matth. 28, 19.: ,Lehret alle Heiden und taufet sie im Namen des Vaters‘ u. s. w. Und folgt nicht

daraus, dass man darum die Taufe nachlassen möge oder genug sei; dass jemand wollte fürgeben, er hätte den Glauben und dürfte der Taufe nicht: denn wer ein Christ wird und gläubet, der wird gewisslich auch solch Zeichen gerne annehmen, auf dass er beide, solch göttlich Zeugniss und Bestätigung seiner Seligkeit, bei ihm habe und sich des stärken und trösten möge in seinem ganzen Leben und dass er auch solches vor aller Welt öffentlich bekenne. Wie denn zu einem Christen beide Stücke gehören, als Paulus Röm. 10, 10. sagt: ,Mit dem Herzen vor Gott und bei ihm selbst gläuben und mit dem Munde vor der Welt bekennen.‘

Wiewohl es kann geschehen, dass einer auch mag gläuben, ob er gleich nicht getauft, und wiederum etliche die Taufe nehmen, die doch nicht wahrhaftig gläuben.

Darum muss man diesen Text also verstehen, dass hiemit die Taufe befohlen und bestätigt, als die man nicht soll verachten, sondern brauchen, wie gesagt ist, und doch darum nicht so gar enge spannen, dass darum sollte jemand verdammt sein, der zur Taufe nicht kommen könnte.

Und Summa, aus diesem Text gehen diese vier Sprüche: 1. Dass etliche gläuben und werden getauft; welches ist insgemein der Befehl Christi und die Regel, so man lehren und halten soll. 2. Etliche gläuben und werden nicht getauft. 3. Etliche gläuben nicht und werden doch getauft. 4. Etliche gläuben nicht, werden auch nicht getauft.

Solchen Unterschied gibt der Text selbst. Und ist allezeit einträchtiglich gehalten, dass, ob jemand gläubte und doch ungetauft stürbe, der würde darum nicht verdammt, denn es mag etwa der Fall vorfallen, dass einer gläubet und, ob er wohl der Taufe begehret, durch den Tod übereilet würde (wie es zuweilen mit jungen Kindern geschehen kann, vor, oder in, oder auch nach ihrer Geburt, welche doch zuvor durch ihrer Eltern oder anderer Glauben und Gebet Christo geopfert und ihm befohlen sind, welche er auch, laut seiner Worte: ,Lasset die Kindlein zu mir kommen‘ u. s. w., ohne Zweifel annimmt).“ (Ev. Kirchenpostille. Opp. Hai. XI, 1332. sqq.)

Dannhauerus: ,,Quanta sit necessitas baptismi, Salvator docet ipse clara assertione: ,Nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua et Spiritu, non potest introire in regnum Dei‘, quae exceptiva in hanc exponentem resolvitur: ,Nullus αβάπτιστος introibit in regnum coelorum.‘ ’Αβάπτιστος, inquam, privative, qui cum posset ac deberet baptizari, tamen consilium Dei adversus semet ipsum aspernatur.

Nam ut negative accipiatur ac infinite de omni non baptizato simpliciter, id non permittit: 1. Scopus Scripturae evangelicae generalis, qui est consolatio. 2. Scopus particularis colloquii Christi, qui est elenchticus Pharisaeismi contemnentis consilium Dei de baptismo. Agit enim cum principe Pharisaeorum, quasi dicat: Tu tuique similes baptismum Johannis contemnitis, ego vero dico, nullum άβάπτιστον contemptorem introiturum regnum coelorum.

Igitur de illis loquitur Christus, qui debent, et qui possunt, qui contemnunt baptizari. . .

7. Instantiarum copia, depromptarum a latrone converso. Is sine dubio introivit in paradisum άβάπ· τιστός; baptizatus enim esset vel ante crucem, vel in hac, vel post hanc: non ante, quia sine poenitentia adultorum nemo debuit baptizari; non post crucem, quia tum fuit mortuus; non in cruce, quia, quod de effusa aqua a latere Christi quidam opinati sunt, refellit ipse Suarez: ,Vix‘, inquiens, ,credibile est, aquam tanto impetu e latere exiliisse, ut latronem attingeret, praesertim si verum est, hunc latronem dextram Christi tenuisse, aquam vero de latere Christi sinistro manasse.‘

Quod de baptismo sanguinis nugatur Gretserus, id et alienum est, et blasphemum; ,neque enim latro ille‘, verba sunt Augustini, ,pro nomine Christi crucifixus est, sed pro meritis facinorum suorum; nec quia credidit, passus est, sed dum patitur, credit.‘

Dices cum Augustino: In latrone non defuisse accipiendi voluntatem, sed adfuisse non accipiendi necessitatem. Idem dicas licet de infantibus non baptizatis, non deesse illis voluntatem, scilicet, ut distinguunt scholae, virtualem.u (Hodosoph. p. 504. sqq.) PART. III. CAP. X.

Carpzovius ad verba A. Conf. art. 9.: ״Affirmant (Anabaptistae)r pueros sine baptismo salvari“, addit: ״Scilicet ordinaria ratione ac via, saluti infantum destinata. Alias de extraordinario regenerationis modo non negatur. Aliud enim est, sine fide salvari non posse; aliud,, sine baptismo salvari non posse. Priuk absolute verum est; posterius vero nonnisi de ordinaria ratione ac modo, quem Deus non sibi, sed hominibus constituit, valet.“ (Isagog. p. 335.)

ANTITHESIS. Quenstedtius: ״Antithesis: 1. Antiquorum Patrum quorundam, communiter olim illi, qui ante susceptum baptismum expirabant, extorres esse regni coelorum judicabantur. Multorum vox erat: ,Non coronantur, si non initiantur‘; Augustinus T. 3.1. de fide ad Petr. Diae, c. 27. scribit: ,Firmissime tene et nullatenus dubites, non solum hornines jam ratione utentes, verum etiam parvulos, qui sive in uteris matrum vivere incipiunt et ibi moriuntur, sive cum de matribus nati sine sacramento sancti baptismatis, quod datur in nomine Patris, Filii et Spiritus S., de hoc saeculo transeunt, ignis aeterni sempiterno supplicio puniendos.‘ Interdum tamen αβαπτίστοις infantibus mitissimam et levissimam damnationem assignat August., ut 1. 1. de peccator, merit. c. 15. et 1. 5. c. Jul. Pelagianum c. 8. Athanasius T. 2. in Qu. ad Antioch. qu. 90. post citatum Christi dictum Joh. 3, 5. addit: ,Manifestum, quod nemo non-baptizatus in illud (regnum coelorum) ingressurus sit.‘ Ex Cypriano liquet, a stricta illa censura exceptos fuisse illos catechumenos, qui martyrium subiissent, antequam tincti essent. Dicit enim S. Martyr Epist. 73. ad Jubajan.: ,Non privari eos baptismi sacramento, utpote qui baptizentur gloriosissimo et maximo sanguinis baptismo.‘ Idem Gennadius 1. de eccles. dogmatibus (qui perperam Augustino adseribitur) c. 74. affirmat. . . Theophylactus etiam in c. 16. Marci, ,Catechumenos‘, etiamsi credant, nondum tamen salvatos pronunciat, ,nisi quoque sint baptizati.‘

2. Scholasticorum, qui non-baptizatos infantes perire statuunt. Sic Lombardus 1. 4. sent. dist. 1. Iit. L. ait: ,Si vero quaeritur de parvulis, qui ante diem octavum moriebantur, ante quem non fiebat circumcisio ex lege, utrum salvarentur, vel non, idem potest responderi, quod sentitur de parvulis ante baptismum defunctis, quos perire constat.‘ Thomas P. 3. q. 65. a. 4. docet: ,baptismum ad salutem absolute esse necessarium.‘ P. 3. qu. 68. inquit: ,Minime salvari possunt, qui nec re, nec voto baptismi sacramentum susceperint.‘ Est autem Thomae sententia de infantibus sine baptismo percepto demortuis, quod apud inferos damnentur aeterna morte, sed tamen sic puniantur carentia visionis Dei, quae dicitur poena damni, ut nullum omnino patiantur dolorem, neque internum, neque externum; vide ipsius Quaest. 5. de malo, a. 1. 2. 3. . .

3. Pontificiorum, qui etiam immitem hanc sententiam defendunt. . . Bellarminus 1. de baptismi sacr. c. 4.: ,Semper ecclesia credidit, infantes perire, si absque baptismo de hac vita recedant.‘ Et in fine istius capitis hanc gnomam ponit: ,Omnes, qui in infantia moriuntur, si praedestinati sint, sine dubio baptizantur, et contra, si reprobi sint, non baptizantur.‘ . . Fingunt autem tale supplicium infantum non baptizatorum, quo poena damni, non sensus illis inferatur, h. e., statuunt, illos privari visione et conspectu Dei, nullos autem sentire cruciatus.“ (L. c. s. 2. q. 10. f. 1166. sq.)

De his enim spem salutis aeque concipere ex revelatione divina non possumus. Cf., quae supra addita sunt ad P. I. c. 7. § 12. Vol. II. p. 213. sqq. Nempe, quando liberi isti parentibus reddi debent, ac permitti, ut ipsi eos educent, qui procul dubio in idololatria sua illos sunt educaturi, verendum est, ne interim, liberos illos baptizando, sacra canibus· projiciantur.· Alias autem, si infantes infidelium modo legitimo in potestatem Christianorum pervenerint adeoque juste servari atque in religione et fide vera educari possunt, sicut illis educatis et informatis atque adeo conversis et baptismum petentibus conferri is potest, sic in ipsa infantia, si mortis periculum immineat, baptizare eos licet.

Hartmannus: ,,Noluit sane Deus, fidem propagari et sacramenta cuiquam administrari laeso jure paterno, cernens, alioquin magnam rerum perturbationem secuturam et evangelium una cum sacramentis invisum gentibus redditum iri; unde apostoli nunquam invitis parentibus liberos eripuerunt. Sicubi vero infans casu, naufragio aut alio modo potestati parentum eximeretur et parentes vel prorsus ignorarent aut desperarent de eorum restitutione, tum omnino infans est baptizandus.“ (Pastorale ev. p. 640.)


### On Baptism: Huelsemannus: "It is false, 1

Huelsemannus: "It is false, 1. that to baptize a little one against the contradiction of the parents is not an injury to paternal power; for it is entirely injurious, by virtue of the apostolic saying 1 Cor. 5:12... For there is and remains on the part of the one snatching an άλλοτριοεπισκοπία, 1 Pet. 4:15. There is and remains in all parents, without condition of status, the faculty of disposing of the religion and salvation of their children, even if it be erroneous, which is evident from collating Gal. 3:28 with Eph. 6:1. False, 3. that in the article of death, against the will of the parents, even if they are not our subjects, it is permitted to snatch an infant for baptism." (Praelect. Form. Conc. p. 485.)

Kromayerus: "However much all men (πάντα τα έθνη) may have some mediate right to the sacrament of initiation, yet the children of Christians, who ought not first to become catechumens, but are to be admitted to baptism immediately upon being born into this light, enjoy it by an immediate right, in preference to the children of the Gentiles, Turks, and Jews." (Th. posit. pol. II, 430 sq.)

Dannhauerus: "Those who are born outside the boundaries of the church to non-Christian parents are not indeed excluded from this benefit by any decretory rejection; yet they do not yet have a right to the thing; they are 'outside,' 'alien from the commonwealth of Israel and strangers to the covenants,' they are 'unclean' (a phrase borrowed from Levitical cleanness), 1 Cor. 5:12, Eph. 2:12, 1 Cor. 7:14. But those who are born within the camp of Israel to Christian parents, to them this benefit pertains by a certain right, in respect of which right they are ennobled by the Holy Spirit with the name of holiness—not internal, but external and Levitical, corresponding to it in 1 Cor. 7:14—and therefore they are not properly to be called Gentiles or 'Heiden.' Those born from one Christian parent and one pagan parent enjoy the same right; those born from parents who were recently Jews, now converted; those claimed by a Christian master by any just title of purchase, donation, war, or adoption. For this promise of the new covenant is not only for those who are children of the covenant, Acts 3:25, but also for τοῖς μακρὰν οὖσιν, Acts 2:39, that is, the Gentiles, whom the Lord has called on any occasion." (Hodosoph. Phaenom. X. p. 526.)

Gerhardus: "Although some of Christian parents are worse than the heathens on account of the impiety of their lives, yet in the meantime they received baptism in their infant age, through which they were received into the covenant of God, and they still profess the Christian faith; therefore they are still to be held as external members of the church. Although, however, on account of impenitence and unbelief they do not actually enjoy the benefits promised and conferred in the covenant of baptism itself, yet on the part of God the covenant remains valid and firm, so that through true repentance a return to it is always open to them, so that they are in need of no other baptism or other covenant; hence also PART III. CHAP. X.

their children still enjoy this prerogative, that the way to baptism is open to them, whereas, on the contrary, the children of infidels do not have it, being altogether aliens from the covenants of promise, Eph. 2:11.” (L. c. § 204.)

The same: “It appears that the children of those heretics who openly protest that they will educate the children left to them under their paternal authority in that heresy are not to be baptized. For 1. they walk in equal step with the infants of infidels, since their parents are likewise outside the church, from which they have made a wicked divorce. 2. The baptized renounce the devil and all his works, among which heresy does not hold the last place. Add that the sacraments are symbols of confession and doctrine. 3. There exists no command to baptize such an infant; nay, rather, a contrary command is annexed to the institution of baptism. Matt. 28:20: ‘Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you.’ And with baptism, true repentance and faith are joined in the apostolic sermons, Matt. 3:1; Acts 2:38; Eph. 4:5. 4. To say nothing in the meantime of the abuse of pious prayers, and thus of baptism itself, of the scandal to the weak, of the perpetual doubt of the baptizing minister whether he is doing right or otherwise, etc.” (L. c. § 200.)

Dannhauerus: “But what if parents who are Christians (in name) openly violate the covenant of God, and fall away to Judaism or Turkism? What if they are held in contumacy under the rod of excommunication? Do their children lose the right to the benefits of the church? Amesius indeed thinks so in lib. 4, cas. consc. c. 27, yet he thinks that they can be assisted through the intervention of sponsors. But truly, not even apostates and the excommunicated are absolutely excluded from a return to the divine covenant; why, therefore, their children? ... The intention of the sponsors is accidental; for what would have become of those who were born of apostate parents before the custom of sponsors obtained in the church?” (Hodosoph. Phaenom. X. p. 527.) §

9. The end of which, from whom, and the effect of baptism, is, proximately, the regeneration or renewal of those being baptized; the ultimate end is the eternal salvation of the same. To which baptism, by the intention of the author, has the nature of a means. For baptism is an efficacious means and a cause of obtaining the end, as will soon appear. This is what is meant when we are said to be born of water and the Spirit, John 3:5, where by water is understood true and properly so-called baptismal water.

Regeneration, however (which is not baptism itself, which is therefore said to consist of water and the Spirit as a double matter, but is an action which is perfected by God and, by appropriation, by the Holy Spirit through baptism as a divinely instituted organ), is said to proceed ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ πνεύματος, of water and the Spirit, as efficient causes, the less principal and the principal joined together. Conf. Aegid. Hunnius de Bapt. T. I. Op. fol. 1021. Similarly, at Titus 3:5, baptism is called the washing of regeneration, a denomination taken from the effect. Apology of the Augsburg Confession: “Nor can any letter be brought forward from the ancient writers that supports the scholastics in this matter. Nay, Augustine says the contrary, that the faith of the sacrament, not the sacrament, justifies. And there is the well-known sentence of Paul (Rom. 10:10): ‘With the heart one believes unto righteousness.’”

Luther: "But as for what Peter says in 1 Pet. 3, that we are saved by baptism, who does not see that nothing is built up against me from this, as if it were false that we are justified by faith alone? Certainly, baptism does not justify without faith, but faith justifies without baptism; therefore, no part of justification can be attributed to baptism. Otherwise, if it justified in any part, it would not be permitted to deny that baptism justifies without faith. But since it is denied to it, it is rightly left to faith alone. Peter therefore intends that by baptism, as an external sign, faith is provoked and exercised, which saves, just as the Word itself—which far prevails over the visible sign—nevertheless justifies no one by itself, except the believer. Thus the Epistle to the Hebrews, Heb. 3, says: 'The word heard did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in those who heard it.' But if there are any among the fathers who felt that the sacrament justifies by its own power—even if it were Augustine, as Cochlaeus contends—I do not care; these are the sayings of men, who often contradict themselves and teach many things according to human sense outside the Scriptures. We follow the most certain Scripture, which says that without faith neither the Word nor the sign profits." (Adversus Cocleum. 1523. See Opp. lat. ad ref. hist. pert. Francof. ad M. 1873. Vol. VII, 54.)

Carpzovius: "It is not said by the Augsburg Confession that the sacraments do not have efficacy without faith, but that they do not profit without faith. For the sacraments are in themselves not only effective in the first act, but they also act in a certain way without faith in men, by offering, namely, the justifying good for justification and the powers of renewal for the continuation of renewal. Meanwhile, he who uses the sacraments has no benefit without faith, even though he cannot prevent the sacraments from offering; yet he does prevent them from conferring that which is offered. When, therefore, it is said in catechisms and here and there by the orthodox that the sacraments do not have efficacy without faith, nor do they work, this must be understood only in the composite sense and regarding the saving effect on the part of the man using the sacraments." (Isagog. in lib. symb. p. 408.)

Quenstedtius: "The water of baptism regenerates not in itself and of itself, or through itself and by its own virtue, but insofar as it has the Word joined to it, whence baptism is called the washing of water by the Word, Eph. 5:26. We do not, therefore, ascribe the power of baptism to naked water, 'a handful of water,' as the Calvinists say, but to the Word of God working alongside and through the water and together with the water."

(L. c. s. 2. q. 7. f. 1135.) Augustine: "Whence comes such great power of water, that it touches the body and cleanses the heart, if not by the Word acting?

Not because it is spoken, but because it is believed." (Tract. in Joh. 80.) Smalcald Articles: "Baptism is nothing else than God's Word in the water, commanded by His institution, or, as St. Paul says in Eph. 5: 'the washing of water by the Word'; as also Augustine says: 'Let the Word be added to the element, and it becomes a sacrament.' And therefore we do not hold with Thomas and the Dominican monks, who forget the Word (God's institution) and say that God has placed a spiritual power into the water, which washes away sin through the water; nor with Scotus and the Franciscan monks, who teach that baptism washes away sin by the assistance of the divine will, so that this washing happens solely through God's will, not at all through the Word or water." (P. III. art. 5. § 1—3. p. 320.)

Calovius: "Universally (Gal. 3:27) the apostle's statement sounds: 'As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ,' namely, with regard to the saving intention of God, who willed this sacrament to be a medium for the putting on of Christ, and with regard to the efficacy of baptism conferred upon it by God—not with regard to the earthly matter alone, because it is not naked water, but water comprehended by the Word of God and the washing of water by the Word, Eph. 5, but as the whole sacrament, inasmuch as it is a medium of regeneration, Tit. 3:5, John 3:6, and has efficacy among all..." PART III. CHAP.

Latin:

Huelsemannus: ,,Falsum est, 1. quod baptizare parvulum contradicentibus parentibus non sit injuria in potestatem patriam; est enim omnino injurium, vi dicti apostolici 1 Cor. 5,12. . . Est quippe et manet ex parte rapientis άλλοτριοεπισκοπία, 1 Pet. 4, 16. Est et manet in parentibus omnibus sine conditione status facultas disponendi de religione et salute filiorum suorum, etsi erronea sit, quod patet ex coli. Gal. 3, 28. cum Eph. 6, 1. Falsum, 3. quod in articulo mortis invitis parentibus, etiam non subditis nostris, liceat rapere infantem ad baptismum.“ (Praelect. Form. Cone. p. 485.)

Kromayerus: ,,Quantumvis omnes homines (πάντα τα εΰνη) jus aliquod mediatum ad sacramentum initiationis habeant, immediato tamen jure Christianorum liberi^ qui non prius fieri debent catechumeni, sed statim in hanc lucem nati ad baptismum admittendi sunt, prae gentium, Turearum, Judaeorum liberis gaudent.“ (Th. posit.pol. II, 430. sq.)

Dannhauerus: ,,Qui extra ecclesiae pomoeria a parentibus non Christianis nascuntur, illi non quidem decretoria aliqua rejectione sunt exclusi ab hoc beneficio; nondum tamen habent jus ad rem; ,foris‘ sunt, ,alieni a republica Israelis et hospites testamentorum‘, sunt,immundi‘ (phrasi e munditie levitica mutuo petita), 1 Cor. 5, 12. Eph. 2,12. 1 Cor. 7,14. Qui vero intra castra Israelis a Christianis parentibus nascuntur, ad illos jure quodam hoc beneficium pertinet, cujus juris respectu a Spiritu Sancto sanctitatis nomine, non internae, sed externae et leviticae illi respondenti 1 Cor. 7, 14., nobilitantur, ac ideo gentiles vel,Heiden‘ proprie non sunt vocandi. Gaudent eodem jure nati ex alterutro parente christiano, altero pagano; nati ex parentibus nuper Judaeis, nunc conversis; asserti christiano domino quovis justo emtionis, donationis, belli, adoptionis titulo. Est enim haec nova foederis promissio non tantum eorum, qui sunt filii foederis, Act. 3, 23., sed et των μακράν δντων, Act. 2, 39., hoc est, gentilium, quos Dominus qualibet occasione advocarit.“ (Hodosoph. Phaenom. X. p. 526.)

Gerhardus: ״Quamvis quidam Christianorum parentum ethnicis sint deteriores propter vitae impietatem, interim tamen in aetate infantili susceperunt baptismum, per quem in foedus Dei sunt recepti, ac profitentur adhuc fidem Christianam; ideoque pro externis ecclesiae membris adhuc habendi sunt. Quamvis vero propter impoenitentiam et incredulitatem actu non fruantur beneficiis in foedere baptismi ipsismet promissis ac collatis, tamen ex parte Dei foedus manet ratum ac firmum, ut per veram poenitentiam ad illud perpetuo ipsis pateat reditus, ut nullo alio baptismo vel alio foedere indigeant; inde etiam PART. III. CAP. X.

liberi illorum gaudent adhuc ista praerogativa, quod ad baptismum ipsis pateat aditus, cum contra infidelium liberi eam non habeant, utpote alieni omnino a testamentis promissionis, Eph. 2,11.“ (L. c. § 204.)

Idem: ,,Apparet, non esse baptizandos liberos illorum haereticorum, qui palam protestantur, se liberos, in potestate patria sibi relictos, in haeresi illa educaturos esse. Nam 1. pari passu ambulant cum infantibus infidelium, cum parentes ipsorum itidem sint extra ecclesiam, a qua nefarium fecere divortium. 2. Baptizati renunciant diabolo et omnibus ejus operibus, inter quae haeresis non postremum obtinet locum. Adde, quod sacramenta sint symbola confessionis et doctrinae. 3. Nullum exstat mandatum de baptizando tali infante, quin imo contrarium mandatum institutioni baptismi est annexum. Matth. 28, 20.: ,Docete eos servare, quaecunque praecepi vobis.‘ Et cum baptismo vera poenitentia et fides in concionibus apostolicis conjunguntur Matth. 3, 1. Actor. 2, 38. Eph. 4, 5. 4. Ut nihil interim dicatur de abusu piarum precum, adeoque ipsius baptismi, de scandalo infirmorum, de perpetua baptizantis ministri dubitatione, rectene an secus faciat etc.“ (L. c. § 200.)

Dannhauerus: ,,Quid vero, si parentes (titulo) Christiani foedus Dei aperte violant, dejiciunt ad Judaismum, Turcismum f Quid, si sub excommunicationis ferula contumaces detineantur? Num jus ad beneflcia ecclesiae eorum liberi amittunt? Ita quidem sentit Amesius lib. 4.. cas. consc. c. 27., putat tamen, iisdem subveniri posse interventu sponsorum. At vero ne apostatae quidem ac excommunicati a reditu ad foedus divinum sunt absolute exclusi, qui igitur eorum liberi? ... Sponsorum intentio accidentaria est; quid enim futurum fuisset de iis, qui, antequam sponsorum mos in ecclesia obtinuit, a parentibus apostatis fuerunt geniti?“ (Hodosoph. Phaenom. X. p. 527.) §

9. Finis cujus, a qui et ejfectus b baptismi, proximus est regeneratio c aut renovatio d baptizandorum; ultimus est salus aeterna e eorundem. Ad quem baptismus, ex intentione auctoris, medii rationem habet. Est enim baptismus medium efficax et causa consequendi finis ut mox patebit. Hoc est, quod dicimur nasci ex aqua et Spiritu, Joh. 3, 5., ubi per aquam aqua baptismalis vera et proprie dicta intelligitur.

Regeneratio autem (quae non est baptismus ipse, qui propterea ex aqua et Spiritu, tanquam duplici materia, constare dicatur, sed est actio, quae a Deo et per appropriationem a Spiritu S. per baptismum, tanquam organon divinitus institutum, perficitur) dicitur έξ υδατος χα\ πνεύματος, ex aqua et Spiritu, tanquam causis efficientibus, minus principali et principali conjunctis, proficisci. Couf. b. Aegid. Hunnius de Bapt. T. I. Op. fol. 1021. Similiter ad Tit. 3, 5. baptismus dicitur lavacrum regenerationis, denominatione ab effectu petita. Apologia Aug. Conf.: ״Neque ulla litera ex veteribus scriptoribus proferri potest, quae patrocinetur hac in re scholasticis. Imo contrarium ait Augustinus, quod fides sacramenti, non sacramentum justificet. Et est nota Pauli sententia (Rom. 10, 10.): ,Corde creditur ad justitiam.“‘

Lutherus: ״Quod autem Petrus 1 Pet. 3. dicit, nos per baptismum salvari, quis non videt, hinc nihil contra me strui, quasi hinc falsum sit, sola fide justificari? Certe baptismus sine fide non justificat, fides autem sine baptismo justificat; ideo non potest ulla pars justificationis tribui baptismo; alioqui si ulla parte justificaret, non liceret negare, baptismum sine fide justificare. Cum autem ei denegetur, soli fidei recte relinquitur. Vult ergo Petrus per baptismum ceu signum externum fidem provocari et exerceri, quae salvet, sicut nec verbum ipsum, quod longe praevalet signo visibili, nullum tamen per sese justificat, nisi credentem. Sic epistola Ebraeorum Ebr. 3. dicit: ,Nihil profuit eis sermo auditus non admixtus fidei in his, quae dicebantur.‘ Quod si qui sunt ex patribus, qui senserunt, sacramentum sua virtute justificare, esto etiam Augustinus, ut Cocleus contendit, nihil moror; hominum sunt dicta, sibi ipsis saepius pugnantium et pleraque humano sensu extra Scripturas docentium. Nos certissimam Scripturam sequimur, quae sine fide nec verbum nec signum prodesse dicit.“ (Adversus Cocleum. 1523. Vid. Opp. lat. ad ref. hist. pert. Francof. ad M. 1873. Vol. VII, 54.)

Carpzovius: ״Non dicitur ab Aug. Conf., quod sacramenta non habeant efficaciam absque fide, sed quod non prosint absque fide. Omnino enim sacramenta in se non tantum efficacia sunt actu prhno, sed etiam certo modo agunt absque fide in hominibus, offerendo scii, bonum justificum ad justificationem et vires renovationis ad renovationis continuationem. Interea nihil commodi absque fide habet is, qui utitur sacramentis, utut impedire nequeat, quod sacramenta offerant; impedit tamen, ut non conferant id, quod offertur. Quando igitur in libellis catecheticis et passim ab orthodoxis dicitur, sacramenta non habere efficaciam absque fide, nec operari; tunc non nisi in sensu composito id intelligi debet et de salutari effectu ex parte hominis usurpantis sacramenta.“ (Isagog. in lib. symb. p. 408.)

Quenstedtius: ״Regenerat aqua baptismi non in se et ex se, aut per se et virtute sua, sed quatenus conjunctum habet verbum, unde dicitur baptismus lavacrum aquae in verbo Eph. 5, 26. Non itaque adscribimus vim baptismi nudae aquae, ,einer Handvoll Wasser‘, ut dieunt Calviniani, sed verbo Dei juxta et per aquam et una cum aqua operanti.“ (L. c. s. 2. q. 7. f. 1135.)

Augustinus: ״Unde ista tanta virtus aquae, ut corpus tangat et cor abluat, nisi faciente verbo? Non quia dicitur, sed quia creditur.“ (Tract. in Joh. 80.)

Articuli Smalcald.: ״Die Taufe ist nichts anders denn Gottes Wort im Wasser, durch seine Einsetzung befolflen, oder, wie St. Paulus sagt Eph. 5.: lavacrum in verbo; wie auch Augustinus sagt: Accedat verbum ad elementum, et fit sacramentum. Und darum halten wirs nicht mit Thoma und den Predigermönchen, die des Worts (Gottes Einsetzung) vergessen, und sagen, Gott habe eine geistliche Kraft ins Wasser gelegt, welche die Sünde durchs Wasser abwasche; auch nicht mit Scoto und den Barfüssermönchen, die da lehren, dass die Taufe die Sünde abwasche aus Beistehen göttliches Willens, also, dass diese Abwaschung geschieht allein durch Gottes Willen, gar nicht durchs Wort oder Wasser.“ (P. III. art. 5. § 1—3. p. 320.)

Calovius: ״Universaliter (Gal. 3, 27.) sonat apostoli sententia: ,Quotquot baptizati estis in Christum, induistis Christum‘, scilicet quod ad intentionem Dei salutiferam, qui sacramentum hoc voluit esse medium ad induitionem Christi, et quod ad efficaciam baptismi a Deo ipsi collatam, non quantum ad materiam tantum terrenam, quia non est nuda aqua, sed aqua verbo Dei comprehensa et lavacrum aquae in verbo, Eph. 5., sed qua totum sacramentum, utpote quod medium est regenerationis, Tit. 3, 5. Joh. 3, 6., et penes omnes efficaciam habet PART. ΙΠ. CAP. X.


### On Baptism: X. from the gracious intention of God, using the same, provided they do not…

X. from the gracious intention of God, using the same, provided they do not resist grace and impede the operation of the Holy Spirit. Since this does not happen in infants, we do not doubt that they are all regenerated through baptism and have put on Christ. There is, therefore, no objection to be made regarding Simon Magus, inasmuch as he resisted saving grace and thus did not put on Christ, concerning which Jerome says: "If anyone receives only this bodily washing, which is seen by the eyes of the flesh, he has not put on the Lord Jesus Christ. For even that Simon Magus had received the washing of water, but because he did not have the Holy Spirit, he had not put on Christ."

(Bibi, illustr. on Gal. 3:27.) Brentius: "Although these Gentiles (Acts 10:47) did not now have a need to be baptized in order to be regenerated and renewed by the Holy Spirit, it was nevertheless necessary to obey the ordinance of God, who had commanded the apostles to baptize all nations, and had subjected all believers to baptism, saying: 'He who believes and is baptized will be saved.' To this is added that baptism is not only an instrument, but also a symbol, by which believers are openly declared to be the people of God, and by which, when tempted by various afflictions, they are confirmed in the faith of regeneration. It is not, therefore, idle and superfluous that these Gentiles are baptized after regeneration." (In Acts of the Apostles homil.

See homil. 51 on the same passage.) Gerhard: "When those are baptized who have already been regenerated by the Word as spiritual seed, they do not have need of regeneration through baptism, but baptism is for them a confirmation and sealing of regeneration, 'just as in Abraham the righteousness of faith precedes and circumcision follows as the seal of the righteousness of faith, Rom. 4:11, so in Cornelius spiritual sanctification in the gift of the Holy Spirit precedes and the sacrament of regeneration follows in the washing of baptism,' writes Augustine, lib. 4 de baptismo c. 24."

(L. de sacram. § 106.) The same: "The adversaries object 4: 'Sometimes those are baptized who have already been reborn before through the Word and the Holy Spirit, as is evident from the example of the eunuch in Acts 8:38 and those upon whom the Holy Spirit had already fallen before, Acts 10:47; since for them baptism was not a means of regeneration, it should not be said to have this end in others.' Resp. 1: Although these and many others were truly regenerated before the use of baptism, nothing at all is detracted from the efficacy of baptism, whereby it is and is called the 'washing of regeneration.' 2. This can be declared by the example of the divine Word, which is heard by many who have already been regenerated; nevertheless, the Word is that saving medium through which, 'as incorruptible seed, we are reborn,' 1 Pet. 1:23, Jas. 1:18. 3. Therefore, just as faith and the gifts of the Holy Spirit are increased in the reborn through the hearing and meditation of the Word, so also the same is done through baptism; indeed, baptism effectively seals the gift of regeneration in them. 4. Therefore, in the question concerning the use of baptism, one must distinguish between infants and adults. For infants, baptism is primarily the ordinary means of regeneration and cleansing from sins, etc., and secondarily the seal of righteousness and confirmation of faith; for believing adults, baptism primarily provides the use of sealing and testifying concerning the grace of God, υἱοθεσία, and eternal life, but less primarily it increases renewal and the gifts of the Holy Spirit." (L. c. § 123.)

The same: "They object: '2. Trust in salvation is perversely included under a sign.' Resp.: The Word and the sacraments are means of salvation divinely instituted; whoever, therefore, attributes to the Word and the sacraments what God Himself attributes to them does not turn the trust of the heart away from God, but rather renders to Him the due honor and reverence; for one must distinguish between the principal and the instrumental cause of salvation: the principal cause of salvation is to be attributed to God alone, and therefore the trust of the heart is to be placed in Him alone; but the instrumental cause of salvation and spiritual efficacy is nonetheless to be left to the Word and the sacraments, which whoever stubbornly denies,

passes over to the camps of Karlstadt and Schwenckfeld. 3. "The whole Scripture attributes the power of regeneration not to the element, but to the Spirit of God." Resp.: Subordinate things are not to be opposed to one another; the power of regeneration is attributed to the Holy Spirit as the principal cause, but to water as the instrumental cause. (L. c. § 104.)

The same: "They object: 'Many who are baptized in infancy, when they grow up, live very wickedly and become malicious; therefore, they were not regenerated through baptism.' Resp.: 1. Those flagitious sinners show by this reasoning not that they were never regenerated, but that they have fallen away from the grace and benefit of regeneration." (L. c. § 125.) Cf. the notes above on Part III, Chapter 8, § 10. For thus baptism is also called the washing of regeneration, Tit. 3: 5.

Carpzovius: "Baptism is an instrument not only offering and conferring justifying grace with respect to justification, but also an operating medium with respect to regeneration and renewal. In the former way, baptism acts by way of moral action, because it does not work in us something that inheres; in the latter way, however, baptism acts by way of physical action, because it works in us that which inheres. And because this latter mode of operation was not in controversy between the Papists and the Lutherans at that time, the Augsburg Confession wished to mention only the former." (Isag. p. 333.)

C. Dietericus: "The Papists err who assert that baptism removes all sins by the root in such a way that neither punishment, nor guilt, nor liability remains (see Bellarmine, l. 1, de baptis. c. 12 and 13 sqq. T. III. col. 289. c. and col. sq.); since only the liability or guilt of condemnation is removed, but the vice or depravity of nature remains residual even in the regenerate, Rom. 7:17, 24; according to that saying of Augustine de nupt. et concup. c. 6. T. VII. col. 824. D.: 'Sin is removed in baptism, not so that it does not exist, but so that it is not imputed as sin'; for in baptism concupiscence is removed, not so that it does not exist, but so that it does not harm." (Institut. catechet. p. 702.)

Balduinus: "In the formula of prayers which precede baptism, mention is made of sins committed by the one being baptized himself: 'And which he himself has added to it.' The question is asked, whether the minister of the church can omit those words in the baptism of infants, since infants do not appear to sin actually? Resp.: They do not err who use those words in the baptism of infants. For infants are not lacking in every actual sin. But a distinction must be made between an action προαιρετικήν [of choice], which is joined with deliberate purpose, and that which is proper to original sin, which you could call φυσικήν [natural], because it arises from a corrupted nature and flows as a vicious effect from original sin, as from a depraved cause. Actual sin, which is done out of choice and intended purpose, is not in infants, because they are still destitute of the use of reason; for which reason they are also said 'not to understand good and evil, and to be ignorant of the difference between the right hand and the left,' Deut. 1:39, Jonah 4:11. However, it must not be denied that actual sin, such as is wont to be in original sin—the root of which is never idle, but always generates vicious actions—is present in infants, even if they are unaware of it. For the evidence of it is anger, impatience, reluctance in doing good, disgust, and similar depraved motions, to which infants are subject even before the years of discretion. And the ancients looked especially to this, who inserted those words: 'And which he himself has added to it,' into the baptismal prayers. Furthermore, those words also look to the act of choice which follows in adults after baptism. For not only is the remission of original sin effected in baptism, but of all sins with which a man can be polluted during his entire life; therefore baptism is called 'the stipulation of a good conscience toward God,' 1 Pet. 3:21, because there is no sin that can trouble us in conscience for which remission has not been made in baptism. For these reasons, the words of that prayer are to be retained. PART III. CHAPTER X. rather than omit it, it would be better to perform it; but an inveterate custom has prevailed among most people that they be omitted; yet that can make a law for no one.” (Tractat. de cas. consc. p. 1066. sqq.)

Luther: “In short, if God were to command you to pick up a straw or tear off a feather, with such a commandment, order, and promise that you should thereby have the forgiveness of all your sins, His grace, and eternal life, should you not accept that with all joy and gratitude, love it, praise it, and therefore hold that same straw and feather as a higher sanctuary and hold it dearer to you than heaven and earth? For however small the straw or feather is, you nevertheless obtain through it such a good that neither heaven nor earth, indeed, not all the angels, can give you. Why are we such shameful people that we do not also hold the water of Baptism, bread and wine—that is, Christ’s body and blood, the oral Word, the laying on of a man’s hands for forgiveness—as high a sanctuary as we would hold the straw or feather, when yet in these, as we hear and know, God Himself wills to work, and it is to be His water, Word, hand, bread, and wine, through which He wills to sanctify and save you in Christ, who has acquired such for us and given the Holy Spirit from the Father for such a work? Conversely, if you were to go in armor to St. James, or let yourself be murdered by Carthusians, Barefoot Friars, or Preachers through such a strict life, so that you might be saved, and God had neither commanded nor instituted such a thing, what would it help you? He knows nothing of it; rather, the devil and you have devised it, as a special sacrament or priestly estate. And even if you could carry heaven and earth so that you might be saved, it is still all lost, and he who would pick up the straw (where it were commanded) would do more than you, even if you could carry ten worlds. Why that? God wills that one should obey His Word, one should use His Sacraments, one should honor His Church; thus He wills to make it gracious and gentle enough, and more gracious and also gentler than we could desire. For it says in Exodus 20:2, 3: ‘I am your God, you shall have no other gods’; it also says: ‘This one you shall hear’ (Matthew 17:5) and no other.” (Writing on the Councils and the Church. A. 1539. Tom. XVI, 2813. sq.)

Latin:

ex gratiosa Dei intentione, eodem utentes, modo non resistant gratiae et operationem Spiritus S. impediant. Quod quum in infantibus non fiat, eos omnes per baptismum regenerari ac Christum induere non dubitamus. Nulla ergo est instantia de Simone mago, utpote qui gratia salutari restitit, adeoque Christum non induit, quo facit illud Hieronymi: ,Si quis hoc corporeum, quod oculis carnis aspicitur, aquae tantum accipit lavacrum, non est indutus Dominum Jesum Christum. Nam et Simon ille magus acceperat lavacrum aquae, verum quia Spiritum S. non habebat, non erat indutus Christum.‘“ (Bibi, illustr. ad Gal. 3, 27.)

Brentius: ,,Tametsi hae gentes (Act. 10, 47.) nunc non necesse habebant baptizari, ut regenerarentur et renovarentur Sp. Sancto, necessarium tamen erat, ordinationi Dei parere, qui praeceperat apostolis, ut baptizarent omnes gentes, et omnes credentes baptismo subjecerat, dicens: ,Qui crediderit et baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit.‘ Huc accedit, quod baptismus non solum sit organon, sed etiam symbolum, quo credentes palam declarantur esse populus Dei, et quo variis afflictionibus tentati in fide regenerationis confirmantur. Non igitur otiosum et supervacaneum est, quod hae gentes post regenerationem baptizentur.“ (In acta apost. homil. Vid. homil. 51. in 1. c.)

Gerhardus: ,,Quando illi baptizantur, qui per verbum tanquam spirituale semen jamdum regeniti sunt, illi non opus habent regeneratione per baptismum, sed baptismus ipsis est confirmatio et obsignatio regenerationis, ,sicut in Abraham praecedit fidei justitia et accedit circumcisio signaculum justitiae fidei, Rom. 4, 11., ita in Cornelio praecedit sanctificatio spiritualis in dono Spiritus S. et accedit sacramentum regenerationis in lavacro baptismi‘, scribit August, lib. 4. de baptismo c. 24.“ (L. de sacram. § 106.)

Idem: ,,Adversarii objiciunt 4.: ,Quandoque baptizantur illi, qui jam ante sunt per verbum et Spiritum S. renati, ut patet exemplo eunuchi Actor. 8, 38. et eorum, in quos jam ante acciderat Spiritus S., Actor. 10, 47.; illis cum baptismus non fuerit regenerationis medium, nec in reliquis hunc finem habere dicendus fuerit.‘ Resp. 1.: Quamvis hi aliique complures ante baptismi usum vere fuerint regeniti, ex eo tamen baptismi efficaciae nihil quicquam decedit, quo minus sit et dicatur,lavacrum regenerationis‘. 2. Id quod exemplo verbi divini declarari potest, quod a multis auditur, qui jam ante sunt regeniti; nihilo tamen minus verbum est salutare illud medium, per quod, ,tanquam incorruptibile semen, renascimur‘, 1 Pet. 1, 23. Jac. 1,18. 3. Ut ergo fides et dona Spiritus Sancti per auditum et meditationem verbi in renatis augenthr, ita quoque idem fit per baptismum; quin et baptismus donum regenerationis in illis efficaciter obsignat. 4. Proinde in quaestione de usu baptismi distinguendum inter infantes et adultos. Infantibus baptismus principaliter est medium ordinarium regenerationis et mundationis a peccatis etc., secundario autem sigillum justitiae et fidei confirmatio, adultis credentibus baptismus principaliter praestat usum obsignationis ac testificationis de gratia Dei, νίυΰεσία et vita aeterna, sed minus principaliter renovationem et dona Spiritus Sancti auget.“ (L. c. § 123.)

Idem: ,,Objiciunt: ,2. Praepostere salutis fiducia sub signo ineluditur.‘ Resp.: Verbum et sacramenta sunt media salutis divinitus instituta; quisquis ergo id tribuit verbo et sacramentis, quod Deus ipse illis tribuit, non avertit cordis fiduciam a Deo, sed debitum potius honorem et reverentiam ipsi praestat; distinguendum enim inter causam salutis principalem et instrumentalem: principalis causa salutis soli Deo tribuenda, ideoque cordis fiducia in ipsum solum collocanda; Instrumentalis vero causa salutis et efficacia spiritualis verbo et sacramentis nihilominus relinquenda, quod ipsum quisquis praefracte negat,

ad Carolstadii et Swencofeldii castra transit. 3. ,Tota Scriptura non elemento, sed Spiritu Dei regenerationis vim merito tribuit.‘ Resp.: Subordinata non sunt sibi invicem opponenda; Spiritui S. tribuitur vis regenerationis, ut causae principali, aquae vero ut causae instrumentali.“ (L. c. § 104.)

Idem: ,,Objiciunt: ,Multi in infantia baptizati, ubi adolescunt, pessime vivunt et tiunt malitiosi, ergo non fuerunt per baptismum regeniti.‘ Resp.: 1. Flagitiosi illi peccatores hac ratione ostendunt, non, quod nunquam fuerint regenerati, sed quod regenerationis gratia et beneficio exciderint.“ (L. c. § 125.) Cf. annotata supra ad P. III. c. 8. § 10. Sic enim baptismus etiam lavacrum renovationis dicitur Tit. 3, 5.

Carpzovius: ״Baptismus organum est non tantum offerens atque conferens gratiam justificam respectu justificationis, sed etiam medium operans respectu regenerationis et renovationis. Priori modo baptismus habet se per modum actionis moralis, quia non operatur in nobis aliquid, quod inhaereat; posteriori vero modo baptismus sese habet per modum actionis physicae, quia in nobis operatur id, quod inhaereat. Et quia hic posterior modus operationis inter papistas et Lutheranos tunc temporis non in controversiam veniebat, igitur priorem saltem memorare voluit Augustana Confessio.“ (Isag. p. 333.)

C. Dietericus: ״Errant pontificii, qui baptismum peccata omnia radicitus sic tollere asserunt, ut neque poena, neque culpa sive reatus supersint (vid. Beilarm. 1.1. de baptis. c. 12. et 13. sqq. T. III. coi. 289. c. et coi. sq.); cum tollatur tantummodo reatus sive culpa damnationis, vitium autem sive depravatio naturae etiam renatis maneat residua, Rom. 7, 17. 24.; juxta illud Augustini de nupt. et concup. c. 6. T. VII. coi. 824. D.: ,Peccatum tollitur in baptismo, non ut non sit, sed ut in peccatum non imputetur‘; in baptismo enim concupiscentia tollitur, non ut non sit, sed ut non obsit. “ (Institut, catechet. p. 702.)

Balduinus: ״In formula precum, quae baptismo praemittuntur, mentio fit peccatorum ab ipso baptizando perpetratorum: ,Und die er selbst dazu gethan hat.‘ Quaeritur, an minister ecclesiae illa verba in baptismo infantum omittere possit, cum infantes actualiter peccare non videantur? Resp.: Non errant, qui in baptismo infantum istis verbis utuntur. Non enim omni actuali peccato infantes carent. Sed distinguendum est inter actionem προαιρετικήν, quae cum deliberato proposito est conjuncta, et inter eam, quae peccato originis est propria, quam φυσικήν nominare posses, quia a natura corrupta oritur et tanquam effectus vitiosus a peccato originali, tanquam a causa prava, profluit. Actuale peccatum, quod ex proaeresi et destinato proposito fit, non est in infantibus, quia destituuntur adhuc usu rationis; quam ob causam etiam,malum et bonum non intelligere, discrimen dextrae et sinistrae ignorare‘ dicuntur Deuter. 1, 39. Jon. 4, 11. Actuale autem peccatum, quale in peccato originis esse solet, cujus radix nunquam otiosa est, sed semper actiones vitiosas gignit, infantibus, licet insciis, inesse, negari non debet. Ejus enim indicium est ira, impatientia, reluctatio in bono, fastidium et similes pravi motus, quibus infantes etiam ante annos discretionis sunt obnoxii. Et huc respexerunt veteres potissimum, qui verba illa: ,Und er selbst dazu gethan hat‘, precibus baptismalibus inseruerunt. Deinde respiciunt ista verba etiam ad actum proaereticum, qui in adultis post baptismum sequitur. Non enim in baptismo tantum peccati originalis fit remissio, sed omnium, quibus homo omni vitae suae tempore pollutus esse potest, ideo baptismus,stipulatio bonae conscientiae cum Deo‘ appellatur 1 Pet. 3, 21., quia nullum est peccatum, quod nos in conscientia angere possit, cujus remissio non sit facta in baptismo. His de causis verba illius precationis retinere PART. III. CAP. X. potius, quam omittere praestaret, sed obtinuit apud plerosque inveterata consuetudo, ut omittantur; ea vero nemini legem facere potest.“ (Tractat, de cas. consc. p. 1066. sqq.)

Lutherus: ,,Summa, wenn dich Gott hiesse einen Strohhalm aufheben, oder eine Feder reissen, mit solchem Gebot, Befehl und Verheissung, dass du dadurch solltest aller Sünde Vergebung, seine Gnade und ewiges Leben haben, solltest du das nicht mit allen Freuden und Dankbarkeit annehmen, lieben, loben und darum denselben Strohhalm und Feder höher Heiligthum halten und dir lassen lieber sein, weder Himmel und Erden ist? Denn wie geringe der Strohhalm oder Feder ist, dennoch kriegst du dadurch solch Gut, das dir weder Himmel noch Erde, ja alle Engel nicht geben können. Warum sind wir so schändliehe Leute, dass wir der Taufe Wasser, Brod und Wein, das ist, Christi Leib und Blut, mündlich Wort, eines Menschen Hände Auflegen zur Vergebung nicht auch so hoch Heiligthum halten, als wir den Strohhalm oder Feder halten würden, so doch in denselben, wie wir hören und wissen, Gott will selber wirken, und soll sein Wasser, Wort,. Hand, Brot und Wein sein, dadurch er dich wolle heiligen und seligen in Christo, der uns solches erworben und den Heiligen Geist vom Vater zu solchem Werk gegeben hat? Wiederum, wenn du denn gleich geharnischt gingest zu St. Jacob, oder liessest dich von Kartäusern, Barfüssern, Predigern durch so strenge Leben ermorden, damit du selig werden möchtest, und Gott hätte solches nicht geheissen noch gestiftet, was hülfe dichs? Er weiss doch nichts drum, sondern der Teufel und du habens erdacht, als sondere Sacrament oder PriesterStände. Und wenn du gleich Himmel und Erde tragen könntest, damit du selig würdest, noch ists alles verloren, und der, so den Strohhalm (wo es geboten wäre) aufhübe, der thäte mehr denn du, und wenn du zehn Welt tragen könntest. Warum das? Gott will, man solle seinem Wort gehorchen, man solle seine Sacrament brauchen, man solle seine Kirche ehren, so will ers gnädig und sanft gnug machen und gnädiger,, auch sänfter, weder wirs könnten begehren. Denn es heisst 2 Mos. 2, 3.: ,Ich bin dein Gott, du sollt keine andere Götter haben‘; heisst auch: ,Diesen sollt ihr ehren‘ Matth. 17, 5. und keinen andern.“ (Schrift von den Conciliis und Kirchen. A. 1539. Tom. XVI, 2813. sq.)


### On Baptism: Quenstedtius: “Although the Calvinists concede that Baptism is an organ and an…

Quenstedtius: “Although the Calvinists concede that Baptism is an organ and an ordinary medium through which God effectively confers and applies His goods, they are nevertheless only tinkling cymbals of words; for they wish these statements to be understood either only of internal baptism, or also sacramentally, i.e., significatively, of external baptism. . . If God and the minister in conferring Baptism conduct themselves as the principal and instrumental cause, there will not be two baptizers, such that man is only the minister of the external sprinkling, while the internal sprinkling of the blood of Christ is done only by the Holy Spirit; which Beza asserted (P. II. resp. ad acta coll. p. 437); nor will there be two separate actions, such that through one the washing of the filth of the body occurs, and through the other the washing of the heart; but it is a single, undivided action of the principal cause, i.e., the Holy Spirit, the minister, and the sanctified water in the very act of regeneration by the ordinance of God. The action of the water is indeed one thing as to its nature, and the action of the Holy Spirit another, but both, by reason of their inseparable communication, constitute one inseparable act in the very result (which is the regenerative washing).” (L. c. s. 2. q. 7. f. 1135. sq.)

Aeg. Hunnius: “Why does John himself distinguish: ‘I indeed baptize you with water, but He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit’? (Mark 1:8.) Certainly not because that baptism of John was a bare external ceremony, through which God had worked nothing intrinsically in the hearts of men. . . . In the mentioned words of John and Christ, the persons concurring in one and the same action are distinguished, as if John were saying: When I baptize, then I indeed cannot provide more than that I administer the water, but the internal virtue is added and bestowed upon my ministry by...

Christ, who is efficacious through that baptism administered by me. This power and faculty does not reside with me, but with Christ; which He Himself will declare by the visible and miraculous baptism of fire, the illustrious outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost, as an indubitable symbol that this power of baptizing with the Holy Spirit resides with Him, whether invisibly through the baptism of water, or visibly in the baptism of fire. Thus, Peter could use the same phrase and say: I indeed baptize with water, but it is Christ who baptizes with the Holy Spirit. Where the actions of Christ and Peter would not be separated, as if the baptism of water, which Peter administers, were separated from the baptism of the Spirit, but it would only be distinctly indicated what Peter contributes and what Christ contributes in that one and undivided action. Clearly just as Dr. Paul writes concerning the ministry of the Word in 1 Cor. 3:6-7, where, in exactly the same manner, a distinction is made between the ministers of the Word and the author of the ministry, God, so that the increase of the preached Word is attributed neither to Paul nor to Apollos, but to God; and yet, God, who alone gives the increase, does not ordinarily exert His power except through the external ministry and labor of the preachers; just as the apostle adds in the same place: "Who then is Paul? And who is Apollos? But ministers by whom you believed." Whence he calls himself and Apollos God’s fellow workers in the same place. (Article or Locus on the Sacraments. Frankfurt, 1590, pp. 120–123.)

See the aforementioned passages and Mark 16:16. Huelsemann: "The external end of baptism is the coalition of the baptized into one external and visible society, professing the same faith, Eph. 4:5; for which reason the Photinians are condemned by this end in the book *Quod Regni Poloniae etc.*, p. 15, and the Arminians in their *Apology*, ch. 23, as well as in the preface to their *Specimina*, who openly profess that they do not require baptism for the inauguration of their associates and brethren into one faith, but rather condemn those who, on account of the lack of baptism, refuse to acknowledge Anabaptists and Photinians as brethren." (Praelect. F. C., p. 491.)

Luther: "But that Christ adds to the first part, 'he who believes,' and mentions baptism, this refers to the command concerning the external office in Christendom, just as He also summarizes this in both parts in Matt. 28:19: 'Teach all nations and baptize them,' etc. And He shows first that the faith, of which this Gospel preaches, must not remain secret and hidden, as if it were enough that everyone should go away when he hears the Gospel and believe for himself alone and not need to confess his faith before others; but in order that it might be manifest, not only where the Gospel is preached, but also where it is accepted and believed—that is, where the Church and Christ’s kingdom stand in the world—He wills to bring us together and hold us together through this divine sign of baptism. For if it were without this, and we were to be scattered without an external gathering and sign, then Christendom could not be spread, nor preserved until the end. But now He wills to bind us together through such a divine gathering in such a way that the Gospel may go ever further and further, and through our confession others also may be brought in. And thus baptism is a public testimony of the doctrine of the Gospel and of our faith before all the world, by which one may see where and with whom this Lord reigns." (Kirchenpostille. Opp. Hal. XI, 1330 sq.)

ANTITHESIS. Quenstedtius: "Antithesis: 1. Of those who sin in the doctrine concerning the end and effect of baptism *καθ' ὑπερβολήν*, according to excess, such as the Papists, who establish: 1. That sin is entirely taken away through baptism, so that nothing re—" remains in the nature of the reborn man, in that it has the character of sin. 2. That baptism confers grace *ex opere operato*, i.e., by the power of the sacramental action itself, so that faith is excluded from the efficacy of sacramental grace. 3. That it imprints an indelible character upon the soul; see Bellarmine, *De baptismo*, bk. 1, ch. 12, 13, and *De sacramentis*, bk. 2, ch. 18, 19. Bellarmine contends, however, that the sacraments (of the N.T.) "are such instruments to which the power and efficacy of conferring grace essentially inheres, or a certain physical accident, just as heat inheres in fire, and consequently that the sacraments induce grace *ex opere operato*, without the intervention of faith." Thus Gabriel Biel, *Sent.*, bk. 4, dist. 1, q. 3: "A sacrament is said to confer grace *ex opere operato*, in such a way that, beyond the exhibition of the sign externally, no good motion is required in the recipient.". .

2. Of those who in this doctrine "sin *κατ’ ἔλλειψιν*, by defect, placing the power and efficacy of baptism only in signifying, shadowing forth, or representing, but not in exhibiting and conferring heavenly goods," and indeed: α. The Calvinists, who make one baptism "internal," another "external"; the external, which the minister performs by washing us with water; the internal, which Christ Himself performs through the Holy Spirit and fire in the elect alone, as it seems good to Him; all of which they explain in such a way that they wish this double baptism to be separated "in species, time, efficacy, and subject." See Beza in *Coll. Mompelg.*, pp. 453, 470. . .

And the Calvinists teach that "baptism (which they call external) is only a bare sign, symbol, and seal of regeneration, but not a means of the same." And thus they simply strip baptism of the power of regenerating, remitting sins, and saving, placing its entire end and effect in signifying, representing, testifying, etc. Zwingli, in his *Confessio ad Carolum V*, art. 7, writes: "I believe, nay, I know, that all sacraments are so far from conferring grace that they do not even bring or dispense it." The same says in *t. 2*, p. 96: "It (baptism) is an external and ceremonial thing, which, like other external things, the church can use worthily and honestly, or omit and duly remove, insofar as it seems to contribute to the edification and salvation of all." The *Belgic Confession*, p. 96, has it thus: "The water signifies that the blood of Christ through the Holy Spirit performs and effects the same internally in the soul that the water works externally in the bodies.". . Beza, in *Actis Colloq. Mompelgart.*, Part 2, p. 115, calls it "a palpable error, drawn from the foul pits of the Scholastics, if the power of conferring grace is attributed indeed principally to God, but instrumentally to the sacraments." Johannes Grynaeus, in *Theol. Theorem.*, Part 1, in the preface, says: "Remission of sins is attributed to the Gospel, baptism, and the Eucharist for the sake of honoring them." *Admonitio Neostadiens.*, ch. 2, p. 510: "Baptism is only a sign and testimony of regeneration." β.

The Socinians, who maintain that "baptism does not confer the Holy Spirit, nor is it a means of regeneration and salvation, but is a bare, external, human, ecclesiastical ceremony, devoid of all divine operation.". . γ.

The Arminians, who do not think more honorably of the efficacy and use of baptism than the aforementioned Socinians; see their *Confession*, ch. 23, sect. 3; Episcopius, *Disp.* 29, th. 8. For they contend that "baptism on the part of God is only a certain signification of grace, and on our part only a public profession of the name of Christ." For thus Episcopius, in the place already cited: "The effect or end of baptism is not any real conferring of grace, but only a mere signification of divine grace and of our profession." δ.

To those who sin by defect also belong the Papists, who call baptism the first plank after shipwreck, as if that washing were of no benefit to those who have fallen after the regeneration of baptism, but only at that moment in which they are baptized. They wish, therefore, that once the covenant of grace is broken, we need another remedy and another plank, namely, our own contrition and satisfaction, by the help of which we may swim to the harbor of salvation. See *Council of Trent*, can. 20, *de bapt.*, Bellarmine, *de baptis.*, bk. 1, ch. 18. (L. c. s. 2, q. 7, f. 1131 sqq.)

10. Here, however, as far as the proximate end is concerned, a diversity occurs with respect to the different subjects. For to infants, indeed, faith is conferred and sealed equally in all through baptism, by which the merit of Christ is applied to them. But to adults, only to those who have conceived faith from the Word before the reception of baptism, does baptism seal and confirm it. Nor does it profit the faithful only at the time when it is received, but also afterwards, and throughout their whole life, effectively for the confirmation of faith and further renewal. For neither can they, by reason of their age, place an obstacle or maliciously resist divine grace and, consequently, the means of grace established in use; nor, being unimpeded, do they fail to obtain grace immediately. For thus far they are by nature unclean and children of wrath, and not holy before God, as if by right of birth from believing parents. For the federal grace does not extend itself to this.

Latin:

Quenstedtius: ,,Licet concedant Calviniani, baptismum esse organon et ordinarium medium, per quod Deus efficaciter conferat et applicet sua bona, verborum tamen tantum sunt tintinnabula; dicta enim haec volunt vel solum de baptismo interno, vel etiam sacramentaliter h. e. significative de baptismo externo. . . Si Deus et minister in conferendo baptismo se habent ut causa principalis et instrumentalis, non erunt duo baptizatores, ita, ut homo sit tantum externae aspersionis minister, interna autem aspersio sanguinis Christi fiat tantum per Sp. S.; id quod Beza P. II. resp. ad acta coli. p. 437. asseruit; neque erunt duae actiones separatae, ita, ut per unam fiat ablutio sordium corporis, per alteram ablutio cordis; sed est unica indivisa actio causae principalis, h. e. Sp. Sancti, ministri et aquae sanctificatae in ipsa regenerationis actu ex ordinatione Dei. Alia utique quoad naturam est actio aquae, alia Sp. S., sed utraque, ratione inseparabilis communicationis, in ipso apotelesmate (quod est ablutio regenerativa) unum inseparabilem actum constituit.“ (L. c. s. 2. q. 7. f. 1135. sq.)

Aeg. Hunnius: ״Cur Joannes ipse distinguit: ,Ego quidem baptizo vos aqua, ille vero baptizabit vos Spiritu Sanctto? (Marc. 1, 8.) Non certe, quod Joannis baptismus ille nuda sit ceremonia externa, per quam Deus intrinsecus in corde hominum nihil fuerit operatus. . . . Discernuntur in memoratis verbis Joannis et Christi personae in una eademque actione concurrentes, quasi dicat Joannes: Quando ego baptizo, tum ego quidem plus praestare non possum, quam quod aquam ministro, virtutem autem internam ministerio meo adjungit et largitur

Christus, qui per illum baptismum a me dispensatum efficax est. Haec vis et facultas non est penes me, sed penes Christum; quod declarabit ipse visibili et miraculoso baptismo ignis, effusione illustri Sp. Sancti in die pentecostes, tanquam indubitato symbolo, quod penes se resideat illa potestas baptizandi Spiritu S., sive invisibiliter mediante baptismo aquae, sive visibiliter in baptismo ignis. Sic eadem phrasi posset uti Petrus ac dicere: Ego quidem baptizo aqua, Christus autem est, qui baptizat Sp. Sancto. Ubi non distraherentur actiones Christi et Petri, quasi baptismus aquae, quem Petrus administrat, sit a baptismo Spiritus separatus, sed distincte tantum indicaretur, quid in una illa et indivisa actione praestent Petrus, quid Christus. Plane sicut de ministerio verbi scribit D. Paulus 1 Cor. 3, 6. 7., ubi simili prorsus ratione inter ministros verbi et ministerii autorem, Deum, sic discernitur, ut incrementum praedicati verbi nec Paulo, nec Apollo, sed Deo feratur acceptum, atque nihilo minus Deus, qui solus dat incrementum, ordinarie virtutem suam non exserat, nisi per externum ministerium et operam concionatorum; sicut ibidem addit apostolus: ,Quis igitur est Paulus? Quis autem Apollo? nisi ministri, per quos credidistis.‘ Unde se et Apollonem Dei cooperarios ibidem nominat.“ (Artic. sive Locus de sacramentis. Erancof. 1590. p. 120—123.)

Vidd. 11. cc. et Marci 16, 16. Huelsemannus: ,,Externus baptismi finis est coalitio baptizatorum in unam societatem externam et visibilem, profltentium eandem fidem, Eph. 4, 5.; quapropter damnantur per hunc finem Photiniani in libro Quod Regni Poloniae etc. p. 15. et Arminiani Apolog. suae c. 23., nec non in praefatione speciminum suorum, qui aperte profitentur, se non requirere baptismum ad inaugurationem sociorum et fratrum suorum in una fide, sed damnare potius eos, qui propter defectum baptismi Anäbaptistas et Photinianos renuunt agnoscere pro fratribus.“ (Praelect. F. C. p. 491.)

Lutherus: ,,Dass aber Christus zu dem ersten Stück, ,wer da gläubet‘, dazu setzet und meldet von der Taufe, das gehet auf den Befehl von dem äusserlichen Amt in der Christenheit, wie er Matth. 28, 19. solches auch in die beide Stück zusammen fasset: ,Lehret alle Heiden und täufet sie‘ u. s. w. Und zeiget erstlich, dass dennoch der Glaube, davon dies Evangelium prediget, nicht muss heimlich und verborgen bleiben, als wäre es genug, dass ein jeder wollte hingehen, wenn er das Evangelium höret, und für sich allein gläuben und nicht dürfte vor andern seinen Glauben bekennen; sondern auf dass es offenbar wäre, nicht allein, wo das Evangelium geprediget, sondern auch angenommen und gegläubet werde, das ist, wo die Kirche und Christi Reich in der Welt stehe, will er uns zusammen bringen und halten durch dies göttliche Zeichen der Taufe. Denn wo es ohne das wäre, und wir sollten zerstreuet sein ohn äusserliche Sammlung und Zeichen, so könnte die Christenheit nicht ausgebreitet, noch bis ans Ende erhalten werden. Nun aber will er uns durch solche göttliche Sammlung also zusammen binden, dass das Evangelium immer weiter und weiter gehe, und durch unser Bekenntniss auch andere herzu gebracht werden. Und ist also die Taufe ein öffentlich Zeugniss der Lehre des Evangelii und unsere Glaubens vor aller Welt, dabei man sehen könne, wo und bei welchem dieser Herr regieret.“ (Kirchenpostille. Opp. Hai. XI, 1330. sq.)

ANTITHESIS. Quenstedtius: ״Antithesis: 1. JZorum, qui in doctrina de fine et effectu baptismi peccant καΰ1 υπερβολήν, secundum excessum, ut Pontifidi, qui statuunt: 1. Per baptismum penitus tolli peccatum, ut nihil rePART. in. CAP. X. maneat in natura hominis renati, quod peccati rationem habeat. 2. Conferre baptismum gratiam ex opere operato, i. e., ex vi ipsius actionis sacramentalis, ita ut fides ab efficientia gratiae sacramentalis excludatur. 3. Imprimere animae characterem indelebilem; vide Bellarminum 1. 1. de baptismo c. 12. 13. et 1. 2. de sacram, c. 18. 19. Contendit autem Bellarminus, sacramenta (N. T.),esse talia instrumenta, quibus virtus et efficacia conferendi gratiam essentialiter inhaereat, seu physicum quoddam accidens, sicut calor igni inhaeret, ac proinde inducere sacramenta gratiam ex opere operato, non interveniente fide.‘ Sic Gabriel Biel 1.4. sent. dist. 1. q. 3.: ,Sacramentum dicitur conferre gratiam ex opere operato, sic, quod praeter exhibitionem signi foris non requiritur bonus motus in suscipiente.‘ . .

2. Eorum, qui in hac doctrina,peccant κατ’ έλλειψιν, in defectu, collocantes vim et efficaciam baptismi tantum in significando, adumbrando seu repraesentando, non vero in exhibendo et conferendo bona coelestia‘, et quidem a. Calvinianorum, qui baptismum alium faciunt,internum‘, alium,externum‘; externum, quem minister aqua nos abluens peragat; internum, quem Christus ipse per Spiritum S. et ignem in solis electis, prout ipsi visum, perficiat; quae omnia ita explicant, ut duplicem hunc baptismum,specie, tempore, efficacia et subjecto‘ velint distractum. Vide Bezam in Coli. Mompelg. p. 453. 470. . .
