Esto ergo prudens lector, imo contemptor Magistri sententiarum lib. 4. cum omnibus suis scribentibus, qui tantum de materia et forma sacramentorum scribunt, dum optime scribunt, id est, mortuam et occidentem literam sacramentorum tractant, ceterum spiritum, vitam et usum, id est, promissionis divinae veritatem et nostram fidem prorsus intactas relinquunt.

Vide itaque, ne te fallant operum pompae, et humanarum traditionum fallaciae, ut veritati divinae et fidei tuae non facias injuriam.

A fide sacramentorum tibi incipiendum est, sine ullis operibus, si salvus fieri voles, fidem autem ipsa sequentur opera, tantum ne vilem habeas fidem, quae opus est omnium operum excellentissimum et arduissimum, quo solo, etiam si ceteris omnibus carere cogereris, servaberis.

Est enim opus Dei, non hominis, sicut Paulus docet, cetera nobiscum et per nos operatur, hoc unicum in nobis, et sine nobis operatur.“ (

De captivitate Babylonica ecclesiae. A. 1520. Vid. Opp. lat. varii argum. cur. Dr. H. Schmidt. Erancof. ad M. 1868. Vol. V. p. 56. 57—60.)

Lutherus: ,,Es ist klär: es möge niemand zu viel sich auf solch Bad und Wiedergeburt verlassen, es ist noch mehr da.“ (Epistol. Kirchenpostille. Tom. Hai. XII, 193.) §

11. Ad significandam baptismi a efficaciam, qua e potestate satanae b in libertatem spiritualem transferuntur infantes, antiquus c exorcismi d ritus, cum signo crucis e et abdicatione satanae votiva,f indifferens g quidem, recte obServatur, h quemadmodum etiam ad designandum foedus i gratiae, quod baptizati cum Deo ineunt, sponsores k seu patrimi pio ritu adhibentur.

De qua vid. § 9.

Non dico obsessione, praesertim corporali, sed e potestate satanae, quam per peccatum in homines carnaliter habet, juxta Eph. 2, 2. PART. ΙΠ. CAP. X.

Olim quidem, locum habente dono miraculoso ejiciendi daemones ex obsessis. Postea autem servatus non solum in adultorum, sed et infantum quorumvis baptismo, testibus Gregor. Nazianz. Orat. XL., August de Fide et Oper. cap. VI. et Lib. II. contra Pelag. cap. XL. Verbis quidem imperandi mado conceptis, sed precationis ad Deum, cum fiducia atque hinc nata animositate adversus hostem depellendum sensu accipiendis. Habito respectu ad vim meriti Christi crucifixi, unde ipsa baptismi efficacia pendet. Qua baptizandi solenniter et expressis verbis renunciant satanae atque omni pompae ejus. Gerhardus: ,,Ceremonias ac ritus in baptismi administratione usitatos distinguimus in tres classes: 1. Quidam divinitus sunt mandati; 2. quidam ab apostolis libere usurpati; 3. quidam avirisecclesiasticis additi. De singulis tenendae sunt hae regulae:

1. Ritus baptismi divinitus instituti accurate distinguendi sunt a ritibus ab apostolis usurpatis et a viris, ecclesiastici honesti decoris, ordinis et piae commonefactionis ergo additis; illi enim sunt substantiales et necessarii, hi vero accidentales et certo modo liberi. ...

2. Ritus ab apostolis in baptismi administratione libere usurpati, licet non eo gradu necessarii sint, quo prioris generis ritus divinitus instituti, tamen a ritibus mere ecclesiasticis distinguendi ac diligenter sunt servandi. Ex historia apostolorum colligitur, quod in administratione baptismi explicationes doctrinae sacramentorum, exhortationes, preces, gratiarum actiones etc. adhibuerint, Actor. 2, 38. etc. Hos ritus etiam in nostris ecclesiis retinemus, quia sacramenta non sunt nuda et otiosa spectacula, sed instituta sunt, ut et fidem confirment et promissionem clarius explicent; ideo doctrina de substantia, usu et efficacia eorum praesentibus ex verbo Dei lingua ipsis nota proponenda est et explicanda, ut de legitima et salutari sacramentorum susceptione diligenter admoneantur. Notandum tamen, in Scripturis ostendi quidem fundamenta, unde sumi debeant explicationes, exhortationes, preces, gratiarum actiones ex institutione sci. et doctrina de baptismo, sicut in verbo Dei traditur, non tamen praescribi certam formam conceptis verbis, sed hoc pro ratione circumstantiarum ad aedificationem liberum permitti, modo fundamentum servetur.

3. Ritus a viris ecclesiasticis additi sunt adiaphori et indifferentes, proinde non sunt simpliciter repudiandi, nec tamen eo gradu necessarii sunt, quo ritus divinitus mandati.“ (L. de bapt. § 255.) Rudelbachius: ״Was zur kirchlichen Giltigkeit erforderlich ist, begriff die Kirche von jeher unter zwei Stücken, nämlich: Die Entsagung des Teufels (abrenuntiatio) und das Bekenntniss des christlichen Glaubens. ... Es ist wahr, die erste ausdrückliche Erwähnung einer EntsagungsFormel kommt erst bei Tertullian in der bekannten Stelle seiner Schrift de corona militis c. 3. vor. Allein, wenn die ungläubigen Theologen weiter daraus folgern: Also ist die Entsagung bei der Taufe keine apostolische Einrichtung, so würden sie dadurch nur einen gänzliehen Mangel an Urtheilskraft verrathen, wenn man nicht wüsste, dass ein ganz aÄeres Interesse sie triebe, wider diese Formel — ein Zeugniss des lebendigen Christenthums — anzukämpfen. Vergegenwärtigen wir uns den Stand der Sache! Tertullian schrieb seine Schrift de cor. mil. nach seinem Uebergang zum Montanismus im Jahre 201. Er erwähnt der Entsagung bei der Taufe nicht als einer Sache, die weiterer Erklärung bedürfe, sondern die offenkundig vorliege, und woraus man also Schlüsse zu ziehen berechtigt sei. Nun wird man aber wohl nicht behaupten wollen, dass er die Sache erdichtet habe, sondern das, was

gegen das Ende des zweiten Jahrhunderts allgemeine kirchliche Giltigkeit erlangt hatte, musste unstreitig schon im ersten als^apostolische Einrichtung bekannt sein. So stehen wir an der Grenze des apostolisehen Zeitalters, und wie wäre es wohl denkbar, dass irgend ein Kirchenlehrer aus der ersten oder zweiten apostolischen διαδοχή (Folge) solches erfunden hätte, in einer Zeit, wo noch unmittelbare ApostelSchüler (wie Polykarp, der Jünger Johannis) lebten — und diese, ja die ganze Kirche hätte einer solchen Erdichtung oder unkirchliehen Privatmeinung nicht laut und feierlich widersprochen? Nein, im Gegentheil, das Zeugniss Tertullians, wohl erwogen, muss alle, die aus der Geschichte der Kirche den Grund der Kirche selbst untergraben, die Bollwerke des Christenthums niederreissen wollen, auf den Mund schlagen. Aber auch bei noch älteren Kirchenlehrern wird der aufmerksame Beobachter wenigstens Spuren der Entsagung bei der Taufe als einer grundchristlichen Einrichtung finden. Wie wird man, fragen wir, ,das Gelübde eines christlichen Lebens‘ erklären, welches, nach Justinus Martyr, alle Täuflinge in Verbindung mit dem Glaubensbekenntnisse ablegen mussten (Apol. I, c. 61.)? Doch wir brauchen wahrlich dieser Zeugnisse nicht, da die Sache als solche schon durch das Zeugniss der Apostel selbst ins Licht gestellt ist, so dass offenbar weiter nur von der Formel als solcher die Rede sein kann.“ (Die Sakramentworte, p. 25. sqq.)

Non certe mandatus a Christo, sed libere receptus ideoque abrogabilis, si ita res tulerit, aut aliquando citra culpam omittendus.

Gerhardus: ,,Cavendum, 1. ne haec ceremonia (exorcismi) pars baptismi essentialis ac necessaria statuatur; 2. ne de obsessione quadam corporali infantis cogitetur, cum spiritualem ejusdem in regio satanae captivitatem solummodo demonstret. . .; 3. neve usus exorcismi statuatur effectivus, quasi vi verborum istorum infans ex regno satanae liberetur, cum sacramento baptismi hoc sit in solidum tribuendum, sed saltem significativus. . . . Quod igitur rem ipsam per exorcismum adumbratam, itemque explicationem verborum in hac ceremonia adhibitorum attinet, quod videlicet sit commonefactio et testimonium de spirituali captivitate infantis in regno satanae, de miserabili statu, in quem per lapsum primorum parentum redacti sumus, de salutari efficacia baptismi etc., ea cum fidei sit analoga, non potest simpliciter improbari; interim tamen cum verba sint duriora ac, seposita illa explicatione, prae se ferant obsessionem quandam infantis, a qua per illam ipsam ceremoniam fiat liberatio, ideo, ut loquitur D. Chemnitius parte 3. Locor, theol. p. 178., ,habet ecclesia libertatem, ut doctrinam illam de peccato originis, de potestate et regno satanae et de baptismi efficacia aliis verbis, Scripturae magis consentaneis, proponat et explicet.‘ . . . Hanc libertatem abrogandi ceremoniam adiaphoram ut ipso facto ecclesia in exorcismo demonstraret, forte non fuerit inutile propter causas non contemnendas.“ (Loc. de bapt. § 264. sqq.)

Huelsemannus: ״Neque negamus, utilius fore, si totius ecclesiae consensu apostrophe illa imperativa converteretur in epiphonema sive doctrinam de modo et mediis exeundi e potestate satanae.“ (Praelect. Form. Cone. p. 495.)

Admonitionis piae causa de insigni operatione sacramenti ipsius. Unde in gratiam heterodoxorum libertati nostrae insidiantium, aut sanctitatem infantibus christianis, velut haereditariam, qua jam sint in statu gratiae, adseribentium abrogari aut omitti non debet. Vid. § 10. not. c. g. h.

k) Non solum testes baptismi collati, sed et causam baptizandorum, praesertim infantum, velut persona eorum in se suscepta, gerentes. PART. ΠΙ. CAP. X.

B. Meisnerus: ״Quaeritur, num interrogatio patrinorum in ecclesiis nostris recte retineatur? — Retinetur haec ceremonia in nostris ecclesiis utiliter propter suos fines ususque, 1. quod non tam infantes, quam ipsos susceptores sua et infantum vice interrogamus, ut sic patrini fidem suam coram ecclesia profiteantur. 2. Ut sciant, quale testimonium baptizato, cum ad discretionis annos pervenerit, perhibere debeant. 3. Ut agnoscat, qua in fide baptizatus instituendus sit. Inter reliqua nonnulli illam rejiciunt formulam,credis?^ ,credo!' abrenuncias?‘ ,abrenuncio‘, putantes, ceremoniam hanc a baptismo adultorum ad paedobaptismum perperam esse translatam....

Menzerus autem, altius hanc rem considerans, his utitur verbis: Quia servator disertis verbis testatus est, parvulos credere Matth. 18, 6. et illorum esse regnum Dei Mare. 10, 14. et adultos debere ipsis fieri similes, ut vitam aeternam consequantur Matth. 18, 3., proinde susceptores sive patrini sub responsione hoc ipsum repetunt apud baptismum infantis, quod Christus tanquam os infantum pro ipsis clare testatus est. Atque huc refert dictum Augustini, quod allegatur de consecrat, dist. 4. c. 139.: ,Mater ecclesia os maternum parvulis praestat, ut sacris mysteriis imbuantur, nimirum repetendo et applicando illud, quod ipse Christus pro infantibus expresse testatus est et confirmavit.‘ “ (Colleg. adiaphorist. disp. VI. § 79—81. 83. 84.) §

12. Baptismus juxta institutionem· Christi a semel collatus b iterari circa idem subjectum c non debet.d

Scilicet, ut in substantialibus nihil fuerit mutatum, verum illa conformia institutioni fuerint. Alias enim non fuerit verus baptismus.

Etiamsi ab haeretico, aut improbo, modo recte administratum fuisse constat.

Licet per abnegationem apertam vel alia scelera defecerit a Deo et foedus gratiae violaverit. ,

Non solum enim nullum pro iterando baptismo extat mandatum aut exemplum, sed nec alias necessitas aut ratio solida apparet. Imo sacramenti initiationis ratio ipsa excludit magis iterationem, quam postulat. §

13. Definiri potest baptismus, quod sit actio sacra a a Christo b instituta, in qua homines c sine sexus atque aetatis discrimine abluuntur aqua d in nomine e Patris, et Filii, et Spiritus Sancti, ut sic f regenerentur ac renoventur, salutis aeternae consequendae causa. Ita forma baptismi significatur, vid. § 6. Haec pertinent ad finem cujus, juxta § 9.


## 26 Of the Holy Supper

PART III. CHAP. XI. Chapter XI. OF THE SACRED SUPPER. § 1. To Baptism succeeds the other sacrament of the N. T., which we call the Lord’s Supper. Not as if the former were abrogated, but as a sacrament of confirmation, to be conferred only upon those who have already been initiated. With Paul leading the way, 1 Cor. 11:20. Moreover, many other names have been received: e.g., the Lord’s table, according to 1 Cor. 10:21; the Eucharist, with regard to the peculiar act occurring therein, see Mark 14:23, Luke 22:19, 1 Cor. 11:24; communion, from 1 Cor. 10:16; synaxis (σύναξις), with regard to the sacred assemblies in which it is accustomed to be celebrated, cf. 1 Cor. 11:20; mass, either from the rite of sending away things or gifts, or from the formula of dismissing the people; the sacrament of the altar, not indeed with a view to a sacrifice properly so called, but with regard to the sacred table where the gifts were deposited. Quenstedtius: "It (the s. s.) is further called κοινωνία or communication of the body and blood of Christ, 1 Cor. 10:16, since the essence of this sacrament consists in this. For the sacramental bread, when taken and eaten, is the κοινωνία of the body of Christ, or the organ or medium by whose intervention the partakers are made participants of the body of Christ. This appellation is also customary among the fathers... Hence κοινωνεῖν among the ancients is to admit to the s. supper or to become a participant of it. Likewise καινὴ διαθήκη, new testament, in the very words of institution, Luke 22:20 and 1 Cor. 11:25: 'This cup is the N. T. in my blood.' For the testator here is Christ, sealing the testament with His death; the heirs are all believers; the witnesses are the apostles; the notaries are the evangelists and Paul; the good legacy is the golden key to the kingdom of heaven and the heavenly treasures, namely, the very remission of sins; the seal is the body of Christ in the bread, the blood in the wine. The s. supper is indeed both an instrument and a seal of the executing of the N. Testament, and yet it is also the testament itself, the new testamentary table instituted, as the blessed Dannhawer teaches in *Mysteriosophia*, s. 2, a. 4, § 64, and in *Hodosophia*, p. 1128. In the words of Christ, however: 'This cup is the N. T.' etc., the word 'cup' is taken metonymically for that which is within the cup, so that the sense is: the cup, or that which is drunk from the cup, is the new testament, i.e., the cause, foundation, and basis of the N. T., constituted and sanctioned in my blood or through my blood." (Th. did.-polem. P. IV. c. 6. s. 1. th. 2. p. 1182 sq.) The seat of doctrine is held to be Matt. 26:26 sqq., Mark 14:22 sqq., Luke 22:19 sqq., 1 Cor. 11:23 sqq. Calovius: "That the words of Christ’s institution are the proper seat of this article, which are read in Matt. 26:26 sqq., Mark 14:22 sqq., Luke 22:19 sqq., and are repeated from the mouth of Christ by the apostle Paul in 1 Cor. 11:23 sqq. and declared in 1 Cor. 10:16, 17, it is a wonder that anyone should call into doubt. But the Calvinists do not so much deny that these are the seat of this doctrine as they altogether reject them from proof and hold them in contempt. Thus the Calvinists..." PART III. CHAP. XI. The considerers are warned, and Whitaker does not want the words of Christ to be alleged as proof any longer, because they are το κρινόμενον [the matter to be judged]. Bullinger and the Tigurines (in *Lib. contr. J. Andr.*, fol. 40) refuse to admit the words of the Supper, "because these, and their meaning, are in controversy." Lavater (in *Hist. sacr.*, p. 16) denies that "from the words: 'This is my body,' the real presence of the body of Christ in the Eucharist can be proven, for it is a *petitio principii* [begging the question]." Others indeed admit the words of institution, but only secondarily, nor do they want them to be held as the principal foundation; this is done not only by all those who attempt to elicit the true sense of Christ’s words from the 6th chapter of John—and therefore abuse a foreign passage to corrupt the proper seat of the doctrine—but also by those who look primarily to other articles of faith, such as the truth of the human nature in Christ, the ascension of Christ into heaven, the return for judgment, etc., and only after they have established from other passages of Scripture what they wish to believe concerning the Lord’s Supper do they then approach the words of institution. And then, this is the task, this is the labor: that a sentiment conceived elsewhere be forced into the words of institution by some figurative and violent interpretation. Therefore, among those arguments which they accumulate to establish and confirm their opinion concerning the Supper, the words of institution do not properly have a place; but when, in refutation, those things which seem to oppose the established opinion must be removed, only then do these words resound: "This is my body," so that, namely, they do not signify what they sound like, but are compelled to serve an opinion presumed from elsewhere, as the blessed Chemnitz teaches (c. 2, *de fundam. coen.*). (System. Tom. IX, 288, 289, sq.) Hutter: "That the discourse of Christ held in John 6 to the Capernaites is not the proper seat of the sacrament of the Eucharist, however much mention is made in it of eating the flesh of Christ and drinking His blood, is evident from these arguments: The discourse of Christ in John 6 was held at least an entire year before Christ was delivered to death. But, as the evangelical history teaches, the sacrament of the Supper was sanctioned on that night in which Christ was delivered to death. From this, therefore, it is clearly gathered: either the sacrament of the Eucharist was founded before it was instituted by Christ, or the seat of this doctrine is to be located in its very institution. But the former is by far most absurd, etc. ... The three earlier evangelists and the Apostle describe such an eating of the body of Christ and drinking of His blood with which eternal damnation can coexist, namely among those who eat and drink unworthily and thus to judgment, 1 Cor. 11:29. But the discourse of Christ in John speaks of such an eating and drinking which cannot be unworthy and is thus always salutary, John 6:54, 56. ... Therefore, sacramental eating and drinking is not delivered in this 6th chapter. — The discourse of Christ in John 6 treats of such an eating which is necessary for all who are to be saved, i.e., without which no one ever was or will be saved, since it is performed by faith alone. But sacramental eating is not necessary except for those who can examine themselves, namely adults, 1 Cor. 11:28. Therefore. Sacramental eating requires an external element for its truth and essence. But that which is described in John 6 has absolutely nothing to do with any external sign or visible element, since the bread there is understood not as elemental, but metaphorical. Therefore." (Loc. theol. fol. 685, sq.) The same: "What the blessed Luther argued with great spirit against Zwingli in his Large Confession, the Sacramentarians variously agitate as *ἀλλότρια* [alien] and having nothing to do with the matter; crying out, 'by this method two articles are confused, that concerning the person of Christ and that concerning the Supper of the Lord, nor is it right that foundations be sought from the former for the confirmation of the latter.' But this cavil is spineless. For if they fear so greatly that some confusion of the articles of faith might arise, why, I ask, have they not imposed this law upon themselves, but, having transgressed it in many ways, have even sought arguments from the sole article concerning the person of Christ for asserting the *ἀπουσία* [absence] of the body and blood in the Supper, for the reason that their presence conflicts with

properties of a true and natural human body, with the ascension, with the sitting at the right hand of the Father, with the return to judgment. Here, therefore, Luther, provoked by his adversaries, wished—nay, indeed, was bound—to seek the foundations of purer doctrine from that same article.

But this also must be noted in this place, that in this Eucharistic controversy, not one, but two distinct questions are agitated:

one of which concerns the will and intention of Christ, namely, whether He truly wills to exhibit His body to be eaten and His blood to be drunk in the Supper, and thus to be most present with His body and blood to the Eucharistic bread and wine? Where, indeed, Luther determined—and we with him determine—that the decision of this question is to be sought nowhere else than from the article of the Lord’s Supper alone.

The other question concerns the power of Christ: namely, whether He is able to be present with His body and blood in all places where this sacrament is dispensed? Or whether the flesh of Christ, when thus eaten, can provide life for us? Where, indeed, he would be a fool who would determine that the decision of these questions is to be sought anywhere else than from the article concerning the person of Christ.

Therefore, the blessed Luther is free from all reproach, who wished to explain and illustrate these two questions from their own proper seats, and to assert them against the φλυαρίας [babblings] of the Sacramentarians.” (Loc. comm. th. Witteb. 1619. f. 716.) §

2. The principal efficient cause of this sacrament is Christ, who instituted this sacrament and commanded it to be frequented, and who even today causes the action concerning the external symbols, administered according to His prescription, to have the nature and power of a sacrament. And He determined each and every thing that pertains to the substance or to the form of the sacramental act. See the 11th chapters of Matthew, Mark, Luke, and Paul. So that He is the cause also regarding the exercise of the act, insofar as He commanded it to be celebrated until His return to judgment, as Paul interprets in 1 Cor. 11:26. For He Himself also joins His body and blood with the blessed symbols, so that they may be received simultaneously, and thus He confirms and increases faith; as we shall see below.

Quenstedtius: “And indeed Christ is θεάνθρωπος, that is, He is the author and cause of the institution of the Holy Supper not only according to His divine, but also according to His human nature. For to institute the sacraments of the New Testament is a mediatorial work; it pertains to the office of Christ, which belongs to Christ according to both natures; and He was indeed at that time in the state, not of humiliation, but of majesty, and He displayed the splendor of His majesty most clearly.” (L. c. s. 1. th. 4. f. 1183.)

Gerhardus: “Since Christ, who instituted this Holy Supper, is true God, it is right that we should admire, not pry into; venerate, not scrutinize, the divine institution of this sacrament. Since He is our mediator, savior, redeemer, king, and priest, it is right that we should hold His testamentary disposition in the highest regard, adding nothing to it nor taking anything away from it, Gal. 3:15. Since He is of the same power and essence as the Father and the Holy Spirit, it is right that we should firmly establish that whatever He ordained, instituted, and promised, He is able to perform, provided that PART III. CAP. XI.

DE SACRA COJSNA. proprietatibus veri et naturalis corporis humani, cum ascensione, cum sessione ad dextram Patris, cum reditu ad judicium. Hic ergo Lutherus, ab adversariis provocatus, ex eodem articulo purioris doctrinae firmamenta petere voluit, imo vero debuit.

Sed et illud hoc loco animadvertendum est, quod in controversia hac euchar. non una, sed duae diversae agitantur quaestiones:

quarum una est de voluntate et intentione Christi, an nimirum corpus suum in coena manducandum et sanguinem bibendum exhibere et sic corpore et sanguine suo pani et vino euchar. praesentissime adesse velit? Ubi sane quaestionis hujus decisionem non aliunde, quam ex solo articulo coenae Dom., petendam esse, statuit Lutherus, statuimus et nos cum ipso.

Altera quaestio est de potentia Christi: an nimirum possit corpore suo et sanguine praesens adesse in omnibus locis, quibus sacramentum hoc dispensatur? an caro Christi sic manducata vitam nobis praestare possit? Ubi sane bardus fuerit, qui aliunde, quam ex articulo de persona Christi, quaestionum istarum decisionem petendam esse statuerit.

(L. c. s. 1. th. 4. f. 1183.)
