Isagog. Carpzov. p. 1681.)

B. Meisnerus: ״Notetur, quod per κοινοποίησιν de toto coetu loquatur apostolus (Eph. 1, 4.), cum tamen epitheta ista solis conveniant electis, in coetu vocatorum existentibus.“ (Anthropol. Disp. XVI. D. 4. b.) ״Recurrit hic (1 Tim. 1, 9.) eadem synecdoche, quam alii vocant κονοποίησιν, cum ad multos sermo dirigitur, id tamen, quod dicitur, non omnibus accommodatur.“ (L. c. Disp. XVII. 1. 3.) Calovius: ״Utut crediderit (apostolus), non omnes inter eos electos esse ad aeternam vitam, a potiori ac meliori parte tamen eo libentius omnes denominabat, quo ardentius omnes in electorum numero inveniri exoptabat; quemadmodum hodieque pro concionibus publicis auditores omnes communiter gratiosissimo electorum in Christo Jesu nomine compellantur, quod inter ipsos tales esse sperentur, omnesque tales esse exoptentur. Recte Augustinus 1. de unit. eccl. c. 12.: ,Prophetae et apostoli sic arguere solent reprehensibiles in aliquo populo, quasi omnes arguantur, et sic alloqui laudabiles, quasi omnes ibi laudentur.‘ “ (Consider. Arminian. p. 434.) ANTITHESIS.

Quenstedtius: ״Antithesis: Sebastiani Castalionis, qui in dialogo suo de elect. erroris de electione universali architectus est, eumque adversus Calvinum et Bezam publice defendit; eum secutus est Samuel Huberus, Helvetius, theologiae professor in acad. Witteb. sub finem superioris saeculi (A. 1593.), qui absurde statuit: ,Electionem esse universalem; Deum elegisse omnes homines vere, proprie et univoce ad salutem.“‘ (L. c. s. 2. q. 6. f. 72. sq.) Formula Concordiae: ״Es muss aber mit sonderm Eleiss Unterschied gehalten werden zwischen dem, was in Gottes Wort ausdrücklieh hievon offenbaret oder nicht geoffenbaret ist; denn über das, davon bisher gesagt, so hievon in Christo offenbaret, hat Gott von diesem Geheimniss noch viel verschwiegen und verborgen, und allein seiner Weisheit und Erkenntniss Vorbehalten, welches wir nicht erforschen, noch unsern Gedanken hierinnen folgen, schliessen oder grübeln, sondern uns an das geoffenbarte Wort halten sollen; welche Erinnerung zum höchsten vonnöthen. Denn damit hat unser Vorwitz immer viel mehr Lust sich zu bekümmern, als mit dem, das Gott uns in seinem Wort davon offenbaret hat, weil wirs nicht zusammenreimen können, welches uns auch zu thun nicht befohlen ist. Also ist daran kein Zweifel, dass Gott gar wohl und ·יaufs allergewisseste vor der Zeit der Welt zuvor ersehen habe und noch wisse, welche von denen, so berufen werden, glauben oder nicht glauben werden; item, welche von den Bekehrten beständig, welche nicht bestän4ig bleiben werden; welche nach dem Fall wiederkehren, welche in VerStockung fallen werden. So ist auch die Zahl, wie viel derselben beiderseits sein werden, Gott ohne allen Zweifel bewusst und bekannt. Weil aber solches Geheimniss Gott seiner Weisheit Vorbehalten und uns im Wort nichts davon offenbaret, viel weniger solches durch unsere Ge«danken zu erforschen uns befohlen, sondern ernstlich davon abgehaiten hat, Röm. 11, 33. f.: sollen wir mit unsern Gedanken nicht folgern, schliessen, noch darinnen grübeln, sondern uns an sein geoffenbartes Wort, darauf er uns weiset, halten. Also weiss auch Gott ohne allen Zweifel und hat einem jeden Zeit und Stunde seines Berufs, Bekehrung bestimmet; weil aber uns solches nicht geoffenbaret, haben wir Befehl, PART. III. CAP. XII. dass wir immer mit dem Wort anhalten, die Zeit aber und Stunde Gott befehlen sollen, Act. 1, 7. Gleichfalls, wenn wir sehen, dass Gott sein Wort an einem Ort gibt, am andern nicht gibt, von einem Ort hinwegnimmet, am andern bleiben lässt; item, einer wird verstockt, verblendet, in verkehrten Sinn gegeben, em anderer, so wohl in gleicher Schuld, wd wiederum bekehret'etc.: in diesen und dergleichen Fragen setzt uns Paulus ein gewisses Ziel, wie fern wir gehen sollen, nämlich dass wir bei einem 7%eil erkennen sollen Gottes Gericht; denn es sind wohlverdiente Strafen der Sünden, wenn Gott an einem Lande oder Volk die Verachtung seines Worts also straft, dass es auch über die Nachkommen gehet, wie an den Juden zu sehen; dadurch Gott den Seinen an etlichen Landen und Personen seinen Ernst zeiget, was wir alle wohl verdienet hätten, würdig und werth wären, weil wir uns gegen Gottes Wort übel.verhalten und den Heiligen Geist oft schwerlich betrüben; auf dass wir in Gottes Furcht leben, und Gottes Güte ohne und wider unser Verdienst, an und bei uns, denen er sein Wort gibt und lässt, die er nicht verstockt und verwirft, erkennen und preisen. Denn weil unsere Natur durch die Sünde verderbt, Gottes Zorn und der Verdammniss würdig und schuldig, so ist uns Gott weder Wort, Geist oder Gnade schuldig, und wenn ers aus Gnaden gibt, so stossen wir es oft von uns und machen uns unwürdig des ewigen Lebens, Act. 13, 46. Und solch sein gerechtes wohlverschuldtes Gericht lässt er schauen an etlichen Landern, Völkern und Personen, auf dass wir, wenn wir gegen ihnen gehalten und mit ihnen verglichen, desto fleissiger Gottes lautere unverdiente Gnade an den Gefässen der Barmherzigkeit erkennen und preisen lernen. Denn denen geschieht nicht Unrecht, so gestraft werden und ihrer Sünden Sold empfangen; an den andern aber, da Gott sein Wort gibt und erhält und dadurch die Leute erleuchtet, bekehret und erhalten werden, preiset Gott seine lautere Gnade und Barmherzigkeit ohne ihren Verdienst. Wenn wir sofern in diesem Artikel gehen, so bleiben wir auf der rechten Bahn, wie geschrieben steht Hos. 13, 9.: ,Israel, dass du verdirbest, die Schuld ist dein; dass dir aber geholfen wird, das ist lauter meine Gnade.‘ Was aber in dieser Disputation zu hoch und aus diesen Schranken laufen will, da sollen wir mit Paulo den Finger auf den Mund legen, gedenken und sagen: , Wer bist du, Mensch, der du mit Gott rechten willst?1 Denn dass wir in diesem Artikel nicht alles ausforschen und ausgründen können noch sollen, bezeugt der hohe Apostel Paulus, welcher, da er von diesem Artikel aus dem offenbarten Wort Gottes viel disputirt, so bald er dahin kommt, dass er anzeigt, was Gott von diesem Geheimniss seiner verborgenen Weisheit vorbehalten, drückt ers nieder und schneidets ab mit nachfolgenden Worten: , 0 welch eine Tiefe des Beichthums, beide der Weisheit und Erkenntniss Gottes! Wie gar unbegreiflich sind seine Gerichte und unerforschlich seine Wege! Denn wer hat des Herrn Sinn erkannt?‘ nämlich ausser und über dem, was er in seinem Wort uns offenbaret hat.“ (Concordia, p. 715—717.) Cf. supra citata P. III. c. 1. §7. p,16.sq. c.3. §10. p. 153. sq. 154. Lutherus: ,,Da hebt sich ein sonderlich Unglück, dass jedermann aus schändlichem und schädlichem Fürwitz will am ersten anheben mit der Versehung dieses und jenes. Weil Gott alle Dinge gewusst: warum er des Menschen Fall nicht Vorkommen habe? warum er noch in der Welt zu sehe und lasse sie ihre eigne Verdammniss fördern, so er doch wohl dafür sein und sie bekehren könnte, dass sie müsste fromm sein? u. s. w. Wer mit solchen Fragen will anheben, Gott zu erkennen, der wird eigentlich den Hals brechen, denn das ist Lucifers Fall, der wollte auch oben hinaus und nirgend an. Aber es thuts nicht.“ (Hai. Tom. XIII, 332. sq.)

Idem: ״Tria mihi lumina pone, lumen naturae, lumen gratiae, lumen gloriae, ut habet vulgata et bona distinctio. In lumine naturae est infeolubile, hoc esse justum, quod bonus affligatur et malus bene

habeat. At hoc dissolvit lumen gratiae. In lumine gratiae est insolubile, quomodo Deus damnet eum, qui non potest ullis suis viribus aliud facere, quam peccare et reus esse; hic tam lumen naturae, quam lumen gratiae dictant, culpam esse non miseri hominis, sed iniqui Dei, nec enim aliud judicare possunt de Deo, qui hominem impium gratis sine meritis coronat et alium non coronat, sed damnat, forte minus vel saltem non magis impium. At lumen gloriae aliud dictat et Deum, cujus modo est judicium incomprehensibilis justitiae, tunc ostendet, esse justissimae et mauifestissimae justitiae tantum, ut interim id credamus, moniti et confirmati exemplo luminis gratiae, quod simile miraculum in naturali lumine implet.“ (De servo arbitrio. 1525. Vid. Opp. lat. var. argum. Francof. ad M. 1873. Vol. VII, 365. sq.)


### On Predestination and Reprobation: J. Andreae: “The faith by which we receive this grace offered universally to…

J. Andreae: “The faith by which we receive this grace offered universally to all, promised in 2 Thess. 3, is a gratuitous gift of God; given by the mere mercy of God without any regard for our works; as it is written: ‘To you it has been granted in Christ, not only to believe in him, but also to suffer for him,’ Phil. 1. But that this grace or this gift of faith is not given by God to all, although he calls all to himself and indeed calls them seriously for his infinite goodness: ‘Come to the wedding, all things are ready,’ is a secret, known to God alone, a mystery to be trembled at and adored, not investigable by any human reason, as it is written: ‘O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God, how incomprehensible are his judgments and his ways past finding out!’ Rom. 11. And Christ gives thanks to God the Father that he has hidden these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them to little ones, Matth. 11. Meanwhile, let afflicted consciences not be offended by this hidden reason of God’s divine will, but look to the will of God revealed in Christ, who calls all sinners to himself. Nor indeed is God to be said to will sin, while he does not always hinder the sinner’s will and way, but permits them to persevere in sins; for God truly hates sin, whose author is the devil, who did not remain in the truth, Rom. 8. For God, because he is horribly angry at sin, forbids it and threatens his wrath to all transgressors of his law. ‘You are not a God who wills iniquity; you hate all who work iniquity,’ Ps. 5. But such is the goodness of God that he can use the evil, which he permits, for the good of the glory of his name, as it is written: ‘For this I have raised you up, that I may show my power in you and that my name may be announced in all the earth,’ Rom. 9. Exod. 9. The same happens when he punishes sin with sin. Rom. 1.” (Form. Conc. Argentoratens. A. 1563. See Historia motuum Loescheri. II, 287. sq.)

N. Selneccerus: “Why is it written: ‘As many as were ordained to eternal life believed’? This is written because the matter is so. For God knows his own from eternity, and those whom he predestines to eternal life, he endows with faith and justifies through the word which they hear. But that he does not predestine all and endow them with faith, the fault is of men, not of God. For many men hear the word in vain and reject the grace of God offered in the word. And although God could make the willing out of all the unwilling, yet he does not do this, and why he does not do it, he has his own most just and most wise reasons, which it is not for us to wish to inquire into. Rather, we ought to give thanks with our whole heart that he has called us through the preaching of the gospel to the participation of eternal life and has illuminated our hearts with faith.” (In omnes epp. D. Pauli commentar. I, 213.)

The same: “Does not God himself blind and harden the impious, as Scripture speaks? Entirely. For when the grace of God is absent, then God is always said to blind and harden men, left, that is, to themselves and going according to the desires of their heart in their own inventions. This is a punishment and judgment of God upon the contemners of evangelical grace... This blinding and hardening is, i.e., the removal of grace, not indeed an efficacious operation done by the purpose and decree of the divine will toward the evil of fault, but a punishment of the contempt of the word of God, by which God dismisses or permits (as Ps. 81 speaks), the ungrateful and impious to be carried by the impulse of their own flesh, nature, and reason, which causes them to precipitate themselves from sin into sin by their own fault and into destruction. But God is said to blind, harden, precipitate, and deceive them (Ezech. 14.) by reason of most just punishment and wrath. For where grace through and because of Christ is not, there it is necessary for place to be given to hardening and blinding. Esa. 6. Joh. 12.” (In omnes epp. D. Pauli commentar. I, 214.)

Cornerus: “Rom. 9, 22. 23. This is a reason from final causes, so that the justice and equity of God may be defended, either in the destruction of the reprobate or in the salvation of the elect. But Paul does not expressly explain the cause why God receives some, but rejects many. For this pertains to the mysteries and secret counsels of God, which we cannot attain in this darkness of life and judgment. For it is not to be said that God acts unjustly if he does anything for the sake of either mercy or the declaration of his power; but the justice of God is to be defended, not blamed; for he does nothing without a cause, although we sometimes are ignorant of it.” (In ep. ad Rom. comment. p. 124.)

Kirchnerus: “Is God then the cause that some are damned? By no means; for he swears and speaks himself, that he does not want the death of the sinner, but that he be converted and live, Ezech. 18. Therefore we should not say that the rejection of the godless is God’s will or order, but rather confess that sin is a cause of the same, for the wages of sin is death. Rom. 6. —

But could he not well convert them all together? There is no doubt about that, if he wanted to use his omnipotence; that he does not do it, we are not to question him about that. Paul writes in Rom. 9: He shows wrath and makes known his power and bears with great patience the vessels of wrath, etc. In those whom he thus lets remain in their unbelief, he shows his justice and wrath against sin. He owes nothing to any of us, but what he gives and does, he does out of pure grace, for Jesus Christ’s sake, to whom we have everything to thank and attribute. —

Since then faith in Christ is a special gift of God, why does he not give it to all? The resolution of this question we should save for eternal life, meanwhile being content that God does not want us to investigate his secret judgments. Rom. 9: ‘O the depth of the riches, both of the wisdom and knowledge of God; how incomprehensible are his judgments!’ —

But it has the appearance as if God were unjust, that he does not give his knowledge and faith to all men, Turks, heathens, and the impenitent? Answer: How can he be unjust, since he owes nothing to any man? Matth. 20., and could well have let them all die in their sins. Therefore also the Apostle says in Rom. 9: ‘Dear man, who are you that you want to argue with God?’ etc. It also seems that God is unjust in that he lets it go badly for the pious here on earth and mostly well for the wicked, and reason cannot adapt itself to this at all. But the Gospel shows the cause why God lays various crosses upon his own here and saves the glory for there. Thus it also seems to us here that God is unjust in that he does not give his word and faith in Christ to all men, and our reason cannot find its way out of this in this life. But when we come there into that life, then we will see and understand that God is not unjust, even if he does not give the word and faith to all men. Lumen gloriae will then solve this question finely and easily; which solution we cannot entirely see in lumine gratiae, God’s punishments and judgment upon sin must be recognized just as much as his grace. The nature of all men is corrupted by sin. Therefore God owes us nothing but damnation. Since he also

God] sometimes gives His Word and grace, [yet] we thrust them away and make ourselves unworthy of eternal life, as is written of the Jews in Acts 13. Therefore, no injustice can justly be attributed to God the Lord in this matter. — "Nevertheless, I would gladly know what the cause of this might be." To this I answer with Augustine, *De verbis apostoli*, serm. 20: "Let no one seek from me the reason for hidden things. He says, 'His judgments are inscrutable,' and have you come to scrutinize them? He says, 'His ways are unsearchable,' and have you come to search them out? If you have come to scrutinize the inscrutable and to search out the unsearchable, believe me, you have already perished. It is the same thing to wish to scrutinize the inscrutable and to search out the unsearchable as it is to wish to see the invisible and to speak the ineffable. Therefore, the house is being built; when it reaches its dedication, then you will find the most manifest reason for these hidden things." In sum, in this life we can say no more than what stands in Romans 9: "That God might make known the riches of His glory on the vessels of mercy, but show His wrath on those who are condemned." We ought to let it rest there. (Enchiridion. 1583. p. 142. b. sqq.)

Heerbrandus: "Since faith is a peculiar gift of God, why is it given to one, but not to another? — God has reserved many things to Himself in this dispute which He has not revealed to us. Therefore, let us not indulge our own thoughts, but let us set a limit, so that we do not inquire further than what has been revealed to us in the Word. God does whatever He can for the sake of our salvation. For He sent and gave His Son as the Savior of the world. He instituted the ministry of His Word, through which He wills that the Son be heard. And through the hearing of the Word, He works faith, through the mediation of the Holy Spirit. Since men do not wish to hear this, as was said above, it is not at all surprising that they are also neglected by the Holy Spirit and thus do not believe, nor are they saved. For it is not for us to judge who hears with a mind to learn. And yet the Apostle rightly says that it is not of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy. For the blindness and stupor of the human mind is too great for it to be able to grasp those mysteries of the kingdom of God by itself. Therefore, even if a man runs, wills, and hears for a long time, yet neither can the teacher give faith, nor can the hearer excite it in himself; but it is necessary that the motion of the Holy Spirit be added, without whom there is nothing—neither he who waters or plants, nor he who hears, but God who gives the increase; who nevertheless requires that external obedience of running, willing, and hearing, through which He Himself works faith.

But if the reason for the diversity is sought, why He gives faith to one and does not give it to another, it certainly cannot be found in God, who is equally disposed toward all men. For He receives into grace all who believe in the Son and condemns all who are unbelieving, according to His own words: 'That whoever believes in the Son should not perish, but have eternal life'; and the Baptist in the same place: 'He who believes in the Son has eternal life. But he who is unbelieving toward the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him.' Therefore, we have nothing else to answer here, except that it ought not to be otherwise. Because He owes nothing to anyone, but has mercy on whom He wills. And that there is no injustice with Him. And let us say with the Apostle: 'O man, who are you to reply against God? Will the thing formed say to him who formed it, "Why have you made me like this?" Does not the potter have power over the clay, from the same lump to make one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?' And let us exclaim with the same: 'O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments and His ways past finding out! For who has first given to Him and it shall be repaid to him?' Likewise: 'Is it not lawful for me to do what I wish with my own things?' Matt. 20:15. —

Latin:

J. Andreae: ״Fides, qua oblatam hanc gratiam, universaliter omnibus 2 Thess. 3. promissam, accipimus, gratuitum Dei donum est; mera Dei misericordia nullo operum nostrorum respectu data; sicut scriptum est: ,Vobis donatum est in Christo, non solum ut in eum credatis, sed ut etiam pro illo patiamini‘, Phil. 1. Quod autem haec gratia sive hoc donum fidei non omnibus a Deo datur, cum omnes ad sevocat et quidem pro sua infinita bonitate serio vocet: ,Venite ad nuptias, omnia parata sunt‘, arcanum est, soli Deo notum, nulla ratione humana pervestigabile mysterium tremendum et adorandum, sicut scriptum est: ,0 altitudo divitiarum sapientiae et scientiae Dei, quam incomprehensibilia sunt judicia ejus et inpervestigabiles viae ejus!‘ Rom. 11. Et Christus agit gratias Deo Patri, quod haec absconderit a sapientibus et prudentibus et revelarit ea parvulis, Matth. 11. Interim afflictae conscientiae hac Dei abscondita divinae voluntatis ratione non offendantur, sed voluntatem Dei in Christo revelatam respiciant, qui omnes peccatores ad se vocat. Neque vero propterea dicendus est Deus peccatum velle, dum peccatoris voluntatem et viam non semper impedit, sed permittat eos in peccatis perseverare; vere enim Deus odit peccatum, cujus auctor est diabolus, qui in veritate non permansit, Rom. 8. Deus enim, quia horribiliter peccato irascitur, prohibet illud et iram suam omnibus transgressoribus legis suae minatur. ,Non es Deus volens iniquitatem; odisti omnes, qui operantur iniquitatem‘, Ps. 5. Ea autem est Dei bonitas, ut malo, quod permittit, bene ad nominis sui gloriam uti possit, sicut scriptum est: ,In hoc excitavi te, ut ostendam in te virtutem meam et ut annuncietur nomen meum in universa terra‘, Rom. 9. Exod. 9. Idem fit, quando peccat.um peccato punit. Rom. 1.“ (Form. Cone. Argentoratens. A. 1563. Vid. Historia motuum Loescheri. II, 287. sq.)

N. Selneccerus: ״Cur scriptum est: ,Crediderunt, quotquot erant ordinati ad vitam aeternam‘ ? Hoc ideo scriptum est, quia sic se res habet. Novit enim Deus suos ab aeterno et quos praedestinat ad vitam aeternam, eos per verbum, quod audiunt, fide donat et justificat. Quod autem non omnes praedestinat et fide donat, culpa est hominum, non Dei. Homines enim multi frustra audiunt verbum et respuunt gratiam Dei in verbo oblatam. Etsi vero Deus ex omnibus nolentibus facere posset volentes, tamen hoc non facit, et cur non faciat, suas habet justissimas et sapientissimas rationes, quas inquirere velle, nostrum non est. Gratias potius toto pectore agere debemus, qtlod nos per praedicationem evangelii ad participationem vitae aeternae vocaverit et fide corda nostra illuminaverit.“ (In omnes epp. D. Pauli commentar. 1,213.)

Idem: ״Annon Deus ipse excaecat et indurat impios, ut Scriptura loquitur? Omnino. Quando enim gratia Dei abest, tunc semper Deus excaecare et indurare homines dicitur, relictos sc. sibi et secundum desideria cordis sui euntes in adinventionibus suis. Haec poena est et judicium Dei in contemtores gratiae evangelicae. . . Haec excaecatio et induratio est, h. e, remotio gratiae, non vero effleax operatio et proposito et decreto voluntatis divinae facta ad malum culpae, sed poena contemtus verbi Dei, qua Deus dimittit seu permittit (ut Ps. 81. PART. ΙΠ. CAP. XII. loquitur), ingratos et impios ferri suae carnis, naturae et rationis impetu, qui fit, ut de peccato in peccatum ipsi suamet culpa et in exitium se ipsos praecipitent. Dicitur autem Deus eos excaecare, indurare, praecipitare et decipere (Ezech. 14.) ratione justissimae poenae et irae. Ubi enim gratia per et propter Christum non est, ibi necesse est locum dari indurationi et excaecationi. Esa. 6. Joh. 12.“ (In omnes epp. D. Pauli commentar. I, 214.)

Cornerus: ,,Rom. 9, 22. 23. Est haec ratio ex causis finalibus, ut defendatur justitia et aequitas Dei, vel in reproborum interitu, vel in electorum salute. Non autem Paulus expresse explicat causam, quare Deus nonnullos recipiat, multos vero rejiciat. Hoc enim ad mysteria et arcana consilia Dei pertinet, quod nos in hac caligine vitae et judicii assequi non possumus. Non est enim dicendum, Deum injuste agere, si quid vel misericordiae, vel declarandae potentiae suae causa agit; sed justitia Dei est defendenda, non culpanda; nihil enim facit sine causa, quamvis illam nos interdum ignoramus.“ (In ep. ad Rom. comment. p. 124.)

Kirchnerus: ״Ist denn Gott die Ursache, dass etliche verdammt werden? Keineswegs; denn er schwört und spricht selbst, er wolle nicht den Tod des Sünders, sondern dass er bekehret werde und lebe, Ezech. 18. Darum sollen wir nicht sagen, dass die Verwerfung der Gottlosen Gottes Wille oder Ordnung sei, sondern vielmehr bekennen, dass Sünde ein Ursach derselben sei, denn der Sünden Sold ist der Tod. Röm. 6. —

Er könnte sie aber wohl alle mit einander bekehren? Da ist kein Zweifel an, wenn er seine Allmächtigkeit brauchen wollte; dass ers aber nicht thut, haben wir ihn nicht darum zu besprechen. Paulus Röm. 9. schreibt: Er erzeige Zorn und thue kund seine Macht und trage mit grösser Geduld die Gefässe des Zorns u. s. w. In denen, die er also in ihrem Unglauben bleiben lässt, erzeigt er seine Gerechtigkeit und Zorn wider die Sünde. Er ist ja unser keinem nichts schuldig, sondern was er gibt und thut, das thut er aus lauter Gnaden, um Jesu Christi willen, dem haben wir alles zu danken und zuzuschreiben. —

Weil denn der Glaube an Christum ein sonderliche Gabe Gottes ist, warum gibt er ihn nicht allen? Dieser Frage Erörterung sollen wir ins ewige Leben sparen, unterdess uns daran genügen lassen, dass Gott nicht will, dass wir seine heimlichen Gerichte erforschen sollen. Röm. 9.: ,0 welch eine Tiefe des Reichthums, beide der Weisheit und Erkenntniss Gottes; wie gar unbegreiflich sind seine Gerichte! ‘ —

Es hat aber das Ansehn, als sei Gott ungerecht, dass er nicht allen Mensehen, Türken, Heiden und Unbussfertigen sein Erkenntniss und Glauben gibt? Antwort: Wie kann er ungerecht sein, weil er keinem Mensehen nichts schuldig ist? Matth. 20., und hätte sie wohl alle in ihren Sünden können sterben lassen. Darum auch der Apostel Röm. 9. spricht: ,Lieber Mensch, wer bist du, dass du mit Gott rechten willst? u. s. w. Es scheinet auch Gott in dem ungerecht sein, dass ers hie auf Erden den Frommen übel und den Bösen mehrertheils lässt wohlgehen, und kann sich die Vernunft hierein gar nicht schicken. Das Evangelium aber zeigt Ursach an, warum Gott den Seinen hie mancherlei Kreuz auflegt und die Herrlichkeit dorthin sparet. Also dünket uns auch hie, Gott »ei ungerecht in dem, dass er nicht allen Menschen sein Wort und den Glauben an Christum gibt, und vermag sich unsere Vernunft hieraus in diesem Leben nicht zu finden. Wenn wir aber dorthin in jenes Leben kommen werden, alsdann werden wir sehen und verstehen, dass Gott nicht ungerecht ist, ob er wohl nicht allen Mensehen das Wort und den Glauben gibt. Lumen gloriae wird diese Frage alsdann fein und leichtlich auf lösen; welche Auflösung wir in lumine gratiae nicht allerdings sehen können, Gottes Strafen und Gerieht über die Sünde müssen ebensowohl erkannt werden, als seine Gnade. Aller Menschen Natur ist durch die Sünde verderbt. Derwegen ist uns Gott nichts als die Verdammniss schuldig. Da er auch

gleich zuweilen sein Wort und Gnaden gibt, stossen wir dieselbige aus und machen uns des ewigen Lebens unwürdig, wie Act. 13. von den Juden steht. Darum kann Gott, dem Herrn, diesfalls keine Ungerechtigkeit billig zugemessen werden. — Dennoch wollte ich gern wissen, was dieses doch für Ursach hätte. Hierauf antworte ich mit Augustino de verbis apostoli, serm. 20.: ,Nemo quaerat a me occultorum rationem. Ille dicit, inscrutabilia sunt judicia ejus, et tu scrutari venisti? Ille dicit, investigabiles sunt viae ejus, et tu investigare venisti? Si inscrutabilia scrutari venisti et investigabilia vestigare venisti, crede, jam periisti. Tale est velle scrutari inscrutabilia et investigabilia investigare, quale est velle invisibilia videre et ineffabilia fari. Ergo aedificatur domus, cum pervenerit ad dedicationem, tunc invenies istorum occultorum apertissimam rationem.‘ Summa, in diesem Leben können wir nicht mehr sagen, denn wie zun Römern 9. stehet: ,Dass Gott wolle kund machen den Reichthum seiner Herrlichkeit an den Gefässen der Barmherzigkeit, seinen Zorn aber an denen, die verdammt werden, erweisen.‘ Dabei sollen wir es bleiben lassen.“ (Enchiridion. 1583. p. 142. b. sqq.)

Heerbrandus: ,,Cum fides peculiare Dei donum sit, cur hoc uni datur, alii vero non? — Deus multa sibi in hac disputatione reservavit, quae nobis non patefecit. Ideo nostris cogitationibus non indulgeamus, sed metam ponamus, ne ultra inquiramus, quam nobis est revelatum in verbo. Facit Deus, quicquid potest, salutis nostrae causa. Misit enim et donavit Filium suum mundi salvatorem. Instituit verbi sui ministerium, per quod Filium vult audiri. Et per verbi auditum, fidem, median te Spiritu S., operatur. Hoc cum homines audire nolint, ut supra dictum est, mirum est minime, quod etiam a Sp. S. negligantur et sic non credant, nec salventur. Qui enim animo discendi audiat, nostrum non est, judicare. Et tamen recte apostolus dicit, non esse currentis, sed miserentis Dei. Major enim est humanae mentis caecitas et stupor, quam ut possit ex sese mysteria illa regni Dei capere. Igitur etsi diu homo currat, velit, audiat, tamen nec doctor fidem dare potest, nec auditor eam in se excitare; sed motus Sp. S. accedat necesse est, absque quo nihil est, qui rigat aut plantat, ita nec, qui audit, sed qui dat incrementum, Deus; qui tamen externam illam requirit obedientiam currendi, volendi, audiendi, per quae ipse fidem operatur.

Quodsi diversitatis ratio quaeratur, cur uni det fidem, alteri non det, certe in Deo reperiri non potest, qui aequaliter erga homines est affectus. Recipit enim in gratiam omnes credentes in Filium et damnat omnes incredulos, juxta illud ipsiusmet: ,Ut omnis, qui credit in Filium, non pereat, sed habeat vitam aeternam‘? et baptista ibidem: ,Qui credit in Filium, habet vitam aeternam. Qui autem incredulus est Filio, non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super eum.‘ Ideo hic quid respondeamus, aliud non habemus, nisi quod aliter fieri non debeat. Quia nemini quicquam debet, sed quorum vult, miseretur. Et non esse injustitiam apud eum. Et cum apostolo dicamus: ,0 homo, tu quis es, qui ex adverso respondes Deo? Num dicit figmentum fictori suo, cur me ad hunc finxisti modum? An non habet potestatem figulus luti, ut ex eadem massa fingat aliud quidem vas in honorem, aliud vero in ignominiam?‘ Et exclamemus cum eodem: ,0 profunditatem divitiarum sapientiae et cognitionis Dei, quam inscrutabilia sunt judicia ejus et impervestigabiles viae ejus? Nemini quicquam debet. Aut quis prior dedit illi et retribuitur ei?‘ Item: ,An non habeo potestatem de meo dandi et faciendi, quod vojk)?‘ Matth. 20,15. —


### On Predestination and Reprobation: But why does God do this

But why does God do this? — To declare the riches of His mercy toward the elect, and His justice toward the reprobate. Rom. 9: 'What if God, wanting to show His wrath and to make His power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath prepared for destruction, and that He might make known the riches of His glory on the vessels of mercy, which He had prepared beforehand for glory.' God does not make, but finds, the vessels of wrath; but He does not find the vessels of grace, He makes them." (Compend. th. 1578, p. 499 ff.)

PART III. CHAP. XII. P. Piscator: "Forty years ago, a certain learned theologian, most well-versed in the writings of Luther, expressed this sentiment: 'But that some should put forth such childish and utterly boorish things and dare to say: If it depends solely on God’s sheer grace and election and not also in part on man’s will, or if it rests solely with God that a man becomes a believer and accepts salvation in the Word, and not with man’s free choice, then God is a respecter of persons, *cum non aequalibus aequalia dividat* [since He does not distribute equal things to equals], because He does not give the faith for it to one as well as to the other. (Puccius does the same with the synergists.) One ought to beat such rags with rods for accusing our Lord God of unfairness because His incomprehensible judgments do not rhyme with their foolish reason.'" (Commentar. in E.C. 1610, p. 577.)

Quenstedtius: "What is said—that the cause, as some believe, is not in men but in God, who grants faith to them according to His good pleasure—is consistent with the Word in Eph. 2:8 and Phil. 2: 13. But what is inferred—namely, that the cause why others persevere in unbelief is likewise in God—is not only contrary to Holy Scripture (1 Tim. 2:4; 2 Pet. 3:9, etc.), but it does not follow from the antecedent. For the defect of faith is from man alone, who, by stubborn resistance and the rejection of the means, hinders God from producing it in the will of man. Therefore, the cause why some do not believe resides not in God, but in the unbelieving men themselves.

They urge again: 'God is omnipotent; therefore, He is able to remove the malicious stubbornness of those who are reprobate and thus ensure that they no longer resist; yet, since He does not do this, He Himself is the cause that the reprobate persevere in unbelief and do not cease to resist the Holy Spirit.' Resp.: Although God, by His omnipotence, could remove the stubbornness of the reprobate and thus ensure that they no longer resist, He is not, however, bound to do so. For He who has decreed to work in the hearts of men through ordinary means according to His most free will is not bound by any right to remove the unbelief of those who stubbornly reject those means, or to infuse faith into them by His omnipotence." (L. c. s. 2. q. 4. f. 59. sq.)

The Theological Faculty of Wittenberg: "Beyond all this, we know very well that this great mystery of the eternal election of grace of God is so deeply hidden in the abyss of divine wisdom that we cannot grasp or fathom it with our human understanding and reason. Hence it also comes about that, until now, little and sparingly has been written about this article in our churches and schools, and that people have applied themselves much more to Christian simplicity than to high and sharp disputation." (Gründl. Widerlegung. 1596. Vid. Consil. Witteb. I, 550.)

Huelsemannus: "It must be confessed that there are certain mysteries in the economy and means of calling, or in the administration of the means of salvation, which must be left to the hidden judgment of God, and we must exclaim with the Apostle: 'O the depth!' from Rom. 11: 33. Not as if the decree of absolute reprobation were inscrutable, as every Calvinist explains (for it is false that the Apostle applies this saying to the non-evidence of the causes of reprobation; the connection shows that it is applied to the non-evidence of the causes of the vocation sent to the Gentiles, who were just as unworthy as the Jews were, v. 30, 31, 32, 33, sqq.), but because, while the evident will of God to save all stands, and the common intercession of Christ and the Church for the unconverted stands, the dispensation of the means of salvation among equals is nevertheless so unequal that, on the part of man, we can detect the proximate and infallible cause neither a priori nor a posteriori. This is what the entire chorus of the Fathers has ingenuously confessed. Jerome on ch. 40 of Isaiah; Ambrose, Book 4, De Fide, ch. 6; Blessed Augustine especially, who shields himself with this saying of the Apostle as if with an aegis, not to clothe an absolute decree of reprobation, but to defend the disparity of grace bestowed upon those who are equal and established in the same perdition... Book 4, Contra duas ep. Pelag., in the middle: 'But why those...'

makes some men sheep and does not make others so? This is the very question which pertains to that height which the Apostle, wishing to discern, in a certain way shuddered at and exclaimed: ‘O the depth of the riches, etc.’” (De auxiliis gratiae, p. 156 sq.)

Thomasius: “We have arrived at one of the greatest, perhaps even insoluble, difficulties: on the one side, the eternal will of love of God in Christ, that all without exception be helped; on the other side, the fact that this will is not attained in all; in the middle, the determination that its realization in the individual has as a condition the corresponding God-willed conduct of the same. This problem is, to be sure, easily solved if one assumes with Augustine and Calvin a twofold absolute decree, an (absolute) decree of election and of reprobation, or if one lets the eternal counsel of grace be conditioned by divine foreknowledge and the good conduct of human freedom, as with Pelagius. Both are just as simple and easy—as they are contrary to Scripture.” (Christi Person und Werk. Second ed. I, 456.)

Or irrevocable, yet in such a way that an absolute immutability is not to be asserted, but only a hypothetical one. For those who are elected in view of final faith foreseen, just as they could have not believed finally, so they could have not been saved, but reprobated. However, when they are foreseen by God as those who will believe finally and are thus elected, just as they cannot simultaneously be those who believe finally and those who do not believe finally, so, since they are elected, by hypothetical necessity they cannot be non-elected. And because of the immutability of the divine will, when the object is not changed, and God has foreseen that it will not be changed, it comes to pass that the elect are necessarily saved, although, speaking absolutely, they could fall from salvation. Whence, although the elect can not only fall from the grace of God, but sometimes do fall, yet no one of the elect falls from it finally.

Formula of Concord: “But the eternal election of God does not only foresee and foreknow the salvation of the elect, but is also, out of the gracious will and good pleasure of God in Christ Jesus, a cause which creates, works, helps, and promotes our salvation and what pertains to it; upon which our salvation is also so founded that the gates of hell shall not be able to prevail against it; as it is written: ‘No one shall snatch my sheep out of my hand’; and again: ‘And as many as were ordained to eternal life believed.’ (Matt. 16:18; John 10:28; Acts 13:48.)” (Concordia, p. 705 sq.)

The same: “Thus this doctrine also gives the beautiful, glorious comfort that God has taken the conversion, righteousness, and salvation of every Christian so much to heart and meant it so faithfully, that before the foundation of the world was laid, He held counsel concerning it and ordained in His purpose how He would bring me to it and preserve me therein; likewise, that He wanted to secure my salvation so well and certainly—because through the weakness and wickedness of our flesh it could easily be lost from our hands, or be snatched and taken away by the cunning and power of the devil and the world—that He ordained the same in His eternal purpose, which cannot fail or be overturned, and has placed it for safekeeping into the almighty hand of our Savior Jesus Christ, out of which no one can snatch us, John 10:28. Therefore Paul also says in Rom. 8:28, 39: ‘Since we are called according to the purpose of God, who then shall separate us from the love of God in Christ?’” (L. c. p. 714.)

PART III. CHAP. XII. The same: “This article also gives a glorious testimony that the Church of God will be and remain against all the gates of hell.” (L. c. p. 715.)

Hollazius: "When the decree of predestination is said not to be absolute, it is not thereby to be established as conditional. For the opinion is not that God chose this or that person for salvation from eternity if he were to believe in Christ and depart in true faith, but because he was going to believe and persevere." (Exam. P. III. s. 1. c. 2. q. 12. p. 632.)

The same: "The decree is called non-absolute [or respective] on account of the respect to external impulsive causes, in consideration of which it was formed by God; e.g., 'God chose us in Christ before the foundations of the world were laid,' Eph. 1:4. There are some theologians who do not admit a conditional decree (since he is properly said to decree who, having considered all circumstances, wills something simply and without condition)... If the absolute is spoken of in opposition to the conditional, we fearlessly maintain that the decree of election is absolute or unconditional, nor do we deny that it is absolute in any other sense than that in which it is called absolute to exclude the respect of an impulsive cause outside of God or external." (L. c. P. I. c. 6. q. 9. p. 431. sq.)

Luther: "Furthermore, if one must speak according to the divine grasp (as far as the immutability of God is concerned), let the judgment be firm: he whom God chose before the world was created cannot perish: 'For no one shall snatch the sheep from the hand of the shepherd.' But he whom He has rejected cannot be saved, even if he had performed all the works of the saints. So immutable is the judgment of God. You, therefore, look only to the majesty of the Lord who chooses, so that you may attain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ. Augustine is correct: 'The predestination of God, even if it is obscured among us, who dwell amidst the present dangers of life, nevertheless remains immutable with Him who made the things that are to be, nor does He blind those whom He has illuminated, nor destroy what He has built, nor uproot what He has planted. For the gifts and the calling of God are without repentance (Rom. 11), and the firm foundation stands, having this seal: The Lord knows those who are His (2 Tim. 2).'" (Briefe etc., collected by de Wette. Part VI, collected by Seidemann, p. 428.)

Latin:

Sed cur id facit Deus? — Ut divitias misericordiae suae declaret erga electos, et justitiam suam erga reprobos. Rom. 9.: ,Quod si Deus volens ostendere iram et notam facere potentiam suam, sustinuit in multa patientia vasa irae, apparata in interitum, et ut notas faceret divitias gloriae suae erga vasa misericordiae, quae praeparavit ad gloriam.‘ Deus non facit, sed invenit vasa irae; vasa gratiae vere non invenit, sed facit.“ (Compend. th. 1578. p. 499. sqq.)

PART. III. CAP. XII. P. Piscator: ,,Hunc in sensum ante annos XL eruditus quidam et in scriptis Lutheri theologus versatissimus: ,Dass aber etliche solch kindisch und gar bachantisch Ding fürgeben und sagen dürfen: Wenn es allein an Gottes blosser Gnade und Erwählung und nicht auch zum Theil an des Menschen Willen gelegen sei, oder wenn es allein bei Gott stehe, dass der Mensch gläubig werde und die Seligkeit im Wort anuehme, und nicht bei des Menschen freier Willkür, so sei Gott ein Anseher der Person, cum non aequalibus aequalia dividat, weil er nicht einem sowohl als dem andern den Glauben dazu gibt. (Idem facit Puccius cum synergistis.) Darauf sollte man solche Lappen mit Ruthen hauen, dass sie unsern Herrn Gott darum der Unbilligkeit zeihen, weil sich seine unbegreifliche Gerichte nicht mit ihrer närrischen Vernunft reimen.‘ “ (Commentar, in E.C. 1610. p. 577.)

Quenstedtius: ״Quod dicitur, causam, quod quidam credunt, non esse in hominibus, sed in Deo, fidem pro beneplacito suo iis largiente, id verbo est consentaneum Eph. 2, 8. Phil. 2, 13. Quod vero infertur, causam sc., cur alii in incredulitate perseverent, similiter in Deo esse, id, sicut S. Scripturae 1 Tim. 2, 4. 2 Petr. 3, 9. etc. contrarium, ita nec ex antecedente sequitur. Defectus enim fidei est a solo homine, qui contumaci repugnantia et mediorum rejectione.impedit, quominus eam in voluntate hominis Deus producat. Causa igitur, quod aliqui non credunt, non in Deo, sed in ipsis hominibus iucredulis residet.

Instant iterum: ,Deum esse omnipotentem, ergo posse illorum, qui reprobi sunt, malitiosam contumaciam tollere et sic facere, ne repugnent amplius; dum autem hoc non facit, ipse in causa est, quod in incredulitate reprobi perseverant, nec Spiritui S. repugnare desinunt.‘ Resp.: Licet Deus possit omnipotentia sua reproborum contumaciam tollere et sic efficere, fie repugnent amplius; non tamen tenetur. Qui enim per ordinaria media in cordibus hominum operari pro liberrima voluntate sua decrevit, is nullo jure tenetur, ut iis, qui media illa contumaciter rejiciunt, per omnipotentiam suam vel incredulitatem adimat vel fldem infundat.“ (L. c. s. 2. q. 4. f. 59. sq.)

Facultas theologica Wittebergensis: ,,Ueber das alles wissen wir sehr wohl, dass dieses grosse Geheimniss von der ewigen Gnadenwähl Gottes in dem Abgrund der göttlichen Weisheit so tief verborgen, dass wir es mit unserm menschlichen Verstand und Vernunft nicht ergreifen und erforschen können. Dannher es auch kommen, dass man bis anher in unsern Kirchen und Schulen sparsam und wenig von diesem Artikel geschrieben und sich vielmehr der christlichen Einfalt, denn des hohen und scharfen Disputirens, beflissen hat.“ (Gründl. Widerlegung. 1596. Vid. Consil. Witteb. I, 550.)

Huelsemannus: ,,Confitendum est, esse in oeconomia et mediis vocandi seu administratione mediorum salutis arcana quaedam, occulto Dei judicio permittenda et exclamandum cum apostolo: ,0 altitudo!‘ ex Rom. 11, 33. Non quasi absolutae reprobationis decretum sit inscrutabile, uti nemo non Calvinistarum exponit (falsum est enim, apostolum applicare hoc dictum ad inevidentiam causarum reprobationis; connexio ostendit, illud applicari ad inevidentiam causarum vocationis missae gentilibus, aeque indignis ac Judaei erant, v. 30.31.32.33. sqq.), sed quia stante evidenti voluntate Dei de salvandis omnibus, stante Christi et ecclesiae communi intercessione pro non conversis, dispensatio tamen mediorum salutis inter aequales tam inaequalis est, ut ex parte hominis neque a priori, neque a״posteriori causam proximam et infallibilem deprehendere possimus. Id quod universus patrum chorus ingenue confessus est. Hieron. in c. 40. Jes., Ambros. 4. de fide c. 6. B. Augustinus imprimis, qui hoc dicto apostoli velut aegide se tegit, non ad absolutum reprobationis decretum vestiendum, sed ad defendendam imparitatem gratiae paribus in eadem perditione constitutis coilatae. . . Libr. 4. contra duas ep. Pelag. in medio: ,Sed quare illos

homines oves facit et istos non facit? Ipsa est quaestio, quae ad eam pertinet altitudinem, quam perspicere volens apostolus, quodammodo expavit et exclamavit: O altitudo divitiarum etc.“ (De auxiliis gratiae, p. 156. sq.)

Thomasius: ,,Wir sind an einer der grössten, vielleicht gar nicht zu lösenden Schwierigkeit angekommen: Auf der einen Seite der ewige Liebeswille Gottes in Christo, dass allen ohne Ausnahme geholfen werde, auf der andern Seite die Thatsache, dass dieser Wille nicht an allen erreicht wird, in der Mitte die Bestimmung, dass seine Verwirklichung an den Einzelnen das entsprechende gottgewollte Verhalten derselben zur Bedingung hat. Dieses Problem ist freilich leicht gelöst, wenn man mit Augustin und Calvin einen zwiefachen absoluten Rathschluss annimmt, einen (absoluten) Rathschluss der Erwählung und der Verwerfung, oder wenn man mit Pelagius den ewigen Gnadenrath durch das göttliche Vorherwissen und das Wohlverhalten der menschliehen Freiheit bedingt sein lässt. Beides ist eben so einfach und leicht — als schriftwidrig.“ (Christi Person und Werk. Zweite Aufl. I, 456.)

Seu irrevocabile, ita tamen, ut non sit asserenda immutabilitas absoluta, sed tantum hypothetica.Nam, qui electi sunt intuitu fidei finalis praevisae, sicut poterant non credere flnaliter, ita poterant non salvari, sed reprobari. Quando autem, tanquam flnaliter credituri, a Deo praevisi et sic electi sunt, sicut non possunt simul esse credentes flnaliter et non credentes flnaliter, ita, cum electi sunt, necessitate hypothetica non possunt esse non electi. Et propter immutabilitatem voluntatis divinae, quando objectum non mutatur, Deus autem praevidit, illud non iri mutatum, fit, ut electi necessario salventur, quamvis absolute loquendo possent excidere salute. Unde licet electi non.solum possint gratia Dei excidere, sed et excidant aliquando, non tamen flnaliter ea excidit quisquam electorum.

Formula Concordiae: ,,Die ewige Wahl Gottes aber siehet und weiss nicht allein zuvor der Auserwählten Seligkeit, sondern ist auch aus gnädigem Willen und Wohlgefallen Gottes in Christo Jesu eine Ursache, so da unsere Seligkeit, und was zu derselben gehöret, schaffet, wirket, hilft und befördert; darauf auch unsere Seligkeit also gegründet ist, dass die Pforten der Höllen nichts dawider vermögen sollen; wie geschrieben stehet: ,Meine Schafe wird mir niemand aus meiner Hand reissen'; und abermals: , Und es wurden gläubig, so viel ihrer zum ewigen Leben verordnet waren.' (Matth. 16, 18. Joh. 10, 28. Act. 13, 48.)“ (Concordia, p. 705. sq.)

Eadem: ,,Es gibt auch also diese Lehre den schönen herrlichen Trost, dass Gott eines jedes Christen Bekehrung, Gerechtigkeit und Seligkeit so hoch ihm angelegen sein lassen und es so treulich damit gemeinet, dass er, ehe der Welt Grund gelegt, darüber Rath gehalten und in seinem Vorsatz verordnet hat, wie er mich dazu bringen und darinnen erhalten wolle; item, dass er meine Seligkeit so wohl und gewiss habe verwahren wollen, weil sie durch Schwachheit und Bosheit unsers Fleisches aus unsern Händen leichtlich könnte verloren oder durch List und Gewalt des Teufels und der Welt daraus gerissen und genommen werden, dass er dieselbige in seinem ewigen Vorsatz, welcher nicht fehlen oder umgestossen werden kann, verordnet, und in die allmächtige Hand unsers Heilandes Jesu Christi,, daraus uns niemand reissen kann, zu bewahren gelegt hat, Joh. 10, 28. Daher auch Paulus sagt Röm. 8, 28. 39: ,Weil wir nach dem Vorsatz Gottes berufen sind, wer will uns denn scheiden von der Liebe Gottes in Christo?‘ “ (L. c. p. 714.).

PART. III. CAP. XII. Eadem: ,,Es gibt auch dieser Artikel ein herrlich Zeugniss, dass die Kirche Gottes wider alle Pforten der Hölle sein und bleiben werde.“ (L. c. p. 715.)

Hollazius: ,,Quando decretum praedestinationis haud dicitur absolutum, eo ipso non statuendum est conditionatum. Neque enim sententia est, quod hunc vel illum ad salutem ab aeterno elegerit Deus, si is in Christum crediturus esset, inque fide vera hinc decessurus, sed quia (?) crediturus et perseveraturus erat.“ (Exam. P. III. s. 1. c. 2. q. 12. p. 632.)

Idem: ,,Decretum non-absolutum dicitur respectivum ob respectum causarum impulsivarum externarum, quarum intuitu a Deo formatum est; v. g. ,Deqs elegit nos in Christo ante jacta mundi fundamenta‘, Eph. 1, 4. Sunt nonnulli theologi, qui non admittunt decretum conditionatum (quum decernere proprie dicatur, qui consideratis omnibus circumstantiis aliquid simpliciter et sine conditione vult)... Si tö absolutum dicatur in oppositione ad το conditionatum, decretum electionis absolutum sive inconditionatum esse, intrepide statuimus, nec alio sensu id absolutum esse negamus, quam quo absolutum dicitur ad excludendum respectum causae impulsivae extra Deum sive externae.“ (L. c. P. I. c. 6. q. 9. p. 431. sq.)

Lutherus: ,,Caeterum, si divino captu (quantum ad immutabilitatem Dei attinet) loquendum fuerit, firma sit sententia: quem Dem ante conditum mundum elegerit, eum non posse perire: ,Nemo enim rapiet oves de manu pastoris.‘ Quem vero rejecerit, eum non posse salvari, etiamsi omnia opera sanctorum fecerit. Usque adeo immutabilis est sententia Dei. Tu igitur et in solam Domini eligentis majestatem respice, ut salutem per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum assequaris. Recte Augustinus: ,Praedestinatio Dei, etsi apud nos, qui dum in praesentibus vitae periculis versamur, victa est, tamen apud illum, qui fecit, quae futüra sunt, immutabilis permanet, nec quae illuminavit, occoecat, nec, quae aedificavit, destruit, nec, quae plantavit, evellit. Dona enim et vocatio Dei sunt sine poenitentia (Rom. 11.) et firmum fundamentum stat, habens signaculum hoc: Dominus novit suos (2 Tim. 2.).“ (Briefe etc., gesammelt von de Wette. VI. Theil, ges. von Seidemann, p. 428.)


### On Predestination and Reprobation: The same: "Even if we grant that some elect in Matt

The same: "Even if we grant that some elect in Matt. 24 are held in error for their whole life, yet it is necessary that they return to the way before death, because Christ says in John 10: 'No one shall snatch them from my hand.'" (De servo arb. 1525. Opp. lat. var. argum. VII, 172.)

The same: "Matt. 24:24. Here He admonishes us that it will happen in the future, not that the elect might not err, but that they shall not be led into error. That is as much as to say: error will not rule over them, nor will it be able to hold them finally, but they must be delivered from it, even if it should happen only in death and dying." (Offenb. des Antichrists. 1521. XVIII, 1932.)

The same: "It is truly quite possible that the elect are led astray, just as I truly was led astray in the Papacy up to my ears. How is it then possible? They can be led astray, but finally they come out again, before they depart from this vale of tears; as I often like to use the example of Saint Bernard. He also held that the Pope was God, but when he was about to die, he turned his eyes from the Pope, from his cowl and monkery, and turned to Christ, his Savior, and forgot the Pope and his strict order entirely and said: I have lived wickedly, but I know that my Lord Christ has a twofold right to the kingdom of heaven, first by nature, as the only-begotten Son of the Father, then..."

he has heaven from eternity; secondly, he has heaven as Mary’s Son, and there he has acquired heaven with his bitter suffering and dying and bestowed it upon me. He does not boast of his papist vow, but says: Christ has obtained heaven by inheritance and by purchase through his blood. Thus we also preach. He was in error and yet came out of it.” (Sermon on Matt. 18–24. A.D. 1539. Erlangen Ed. Vol. XLV, 148 sqq.) The same: “Thus I also believe that our dear God preserved many of our ancestors in the great darkness of the Papacy. For in that same blindness and darkness it nevertheless remained that the crucifix was held before the dying, and that some laypeople said to them: Look upon Jesus, who died for you on the cross. Through this, many a dying person turned back to Christ, even though he had previously believed in the false signs and wonders and clung to idolatry. These were the elect, who were also led into the prison of error and would have remained therein, had it been possible. Thus we can take comfort regarding those who died in the Papacy, that God finally gave them grace so that, through the remembrance of the crucifix, they departed and passed on to Christ. These same people were also stuck in error, but it was not possible that they should remain therein.” (XIII, 2313 sqq.) The same: “The elect will not be led into error; not that they would not err; indeed, the danger will (rather) be so great that they will err with the godless: but they will not persist nor remain therein, although they will escape only with difficulty, with toil and labor.” (XIX, 1384.) The same: “We let Jonah here (Jon. 1:5) have committed a great, grievous sin, through which he would have been eternally damned, had he not been written in the number of the elect in the Book of Life.” (Ad Jon. 1:5. VI, 2607.) Chemnitius: “From this it is certain that no elect person finally remains and persists in impenitence and unbelief.” (Handbüchlein, etc., 1574. See Frank: Die Theologie der Concordienformel IV, 338.) The same: “It is clear and certain from the foundation of Scripture that those who are elected to eternal life will all be saved, for God’s providence cannot fail, and the eternal election of grace of God is unchangeable, cannot be altered or overturned, as can be sufficiently proven from Scripture.” (A.D. 1576. Answer to Duke Wolfgang of Braunschweig-Lüneburg regarding a dispute that occurred at Osterode: “whether predestination and election is to be understood universally or particularly.” See Rehtmeyer, Braunschweig. Kirchenhist. III. Appendices p. 240.) Württemberg Theologians: “Holy Scripture speaks clearly of such an election that properly concerns only the chosen children of God, whom God will make eternally blessed, as the following clear passages testify. Rom. 8 (29, 30), Paul writes: ‘For whom he did foreknow,’ etc. In which clear passage the Apostle teaches that the elect are to be sought only among the crowd of those who are called, and shows that those who are ordained or elected are also justified and glorified, that is, made eternally blessed.” (1594. Acta Huberiana I, 266. See Frank: Theologie der Concordienformel IV, 285.) Wittenberg Theological Faculty: “Scripture holds throughout as one: those whom God elects to life, and those who finally grasp such life and come to heaven; in view of the fact that the election does not remain stuck, but is carried out unto salvation and glorification (Rom. 8:29, 30), as Paul says: ‘The PART III. CAP. XII. election hath obtained it’ (Rom. 11:7), namely, the salvation of the soul.” (Bescheidentliche Antwort auf das Bekenntnis Huberi. 1595. See Consil. Witteberg. I, 547.) B. Meisnerus: "By mutability, however, nothing else is understood than the possibility of evacuation, since one can fall away from election and from an elect person become a reprobate. For then, with respect to us, predestination is changed in such a way that he who was previously inscribed in the catalog of the elect through faith is erased from it on account of sins; but if he performs repentance, he is inscribed in turn, and thus, by alternating turns, according to the ratio of either faith or impenitence, he is now a reprobate, now elect. Whether such a reciprocal change ought to be granted, or whether it has a place in the decree of election, is called into controversy. But what ought to be answered will not be so obscure if the *Concordia* is consulted. For thus it is read in the *Epitome*, Art. 2, p. 618, Leipzig edition, year 1606: 'Predestination or the eternal election of God pertains only to the good and beloved children of God, and this is the cause of their salvation; for it procures salvation and disposes those things which pertain to it. Our salvation is so founded upon this predestination of God that the gates of hell cannot overthrow it.' Again in the *Solida Declaratio*, p. 799: 'The eternal election or predestination of God to salvation does not pertain at the same time to the good and to the bad, but only to the children of God, who have been elected and ordained to obtain eternal life.' A little later: 'In that divine eternal predestination our salvation is so founded that even the gates of hell cannot prevail against it, for it is written: No one shall snatch my sheep from my hand.' And p. 803: 'He himself in his eternal counsel decreed that those whom he elected, called, and justified, he wills to make safe in that other eternal life and to adorn with eternal glory.' Shortly below: 'He decreed that in that way (which we have already recited) he wills to make them participants of eternal salvation through his grace, gifts, and efficacy, to help them, to promote their salvation, and to confirm and preserve them.' From these words of the *Concordia* we deduce the following aphorisms:

1. That election properly so called pertains only to the faithful, not to all the called in general, much less to all men.

2. That all the elect are certainly saved, because it is said: 1) that election is the cause of salvation and procures it; 2) that the gates of hell cannot overthrow it; 3) that it was made for the obtaining of life; 4) so that the elect sheep cannot be snatched from the hand of God, i.e., cannot finally fall from grace and be damned; 5) because God certainly wills to save his elect and therefore preserves them in faith until the end of life. Therefore, those who are not preserved, who do not persevere, and thus are not saved, cannot truly and properly be called elect according to the phraseology of Scripture and the explanation of the *Concordia*.

3 That predestination is immutable, so that an elect person does not become a reprobate, or vice versa. For if all the predestined are preserved and certainly saved, then surely he who is damned was never predestined, even if he believed for a time and perceived the grace of God." The Witteberg theologians hold the same opinion in *Explicatio brevis contra Huberum*, A. 3, fac. 2; B. 2, fac. 1; B. 3, fac. 1 and 2; D. 3, fac. 2; E. 4, fac. 2; E. 1, fac. 2; the Tübingen theologians, P. I, *Act. Huber.*, p. 38, 182, 195, 200, 266, 270, 303, 304; P. II, *Act.*, p. 33, 36, 107, 217, sqq.; Chemnitius in *Enchiridion*, p. 266 Hunnius *de praedest.*, p. 357, 358, sqq., Frankfurt edition, 1603; Tom. 1, disp. 10, Marp., th. 88; Gesnerus, *disp. ult. in Dan.*, th. 142; Gerlachius, *disp. de aeterna salvandorum electione*, th. 11; Bungius, *disp. 10 in ep. ad Rom.*, p. 179; Dn. D. Hutterus in *Form. Conc.*, p. 1121, 1163, 1124, 1177; and Dn. D. Menzerus, Tom. 1, *disp. Giess.*, disp. 14, th. 10, 40, 78, 109, 129, 131, 171, 192, sqq. All these teach and confess: 1 That the decree of election, as it is eternal, so it is immutable and certain. For those things which God has once decreed to do, he certainly executes, and if he did not do them, he would be frustrated in his end, and his truth, wisdom, and omnipotence would be detracted from. Therefore, whom he has elected, i.e., decreed to save, him he certainly saves, and vice versa. 2 From this it follows that an elect person always remains elect, and never becomes a reprobate, or vice versa, i.e., that election cannot be rendered void or evacuated. 3. Although

Therefore, although some of the elect may sin mortally, at that very time they truly are and can be called elect on account of the divine decree and the certain number of the elect, in which they always remain included in the eternal foreknowledge. 4. In the same way, although some truly believe for a time, yet if they are not inscribed in the eternal book of life on account of foreseen final unbelief, at that very time of faith, by virtue of the divine decree, they truly are and can be called reprobate in the divine foreknowledge. 5. There is, therefore, a great difference between the regenerate and the elect, so much so that they cannot be held as synonyms, since they are distinguished as the broader and the narrower, for while all the elect are indeed regenerate—if not at every time, yet at the time of death—not all the regenerate are conversely elect, namely those who lose their faith and depart with final impenitence.” (Anthropologia, Disp. XVI. A. 2. b. — A. 3. b.) The same: “Matt. 24:24; Mark 13:22: ‘False Christs and false prophets will arise and will give great signs and wonders, so as to lead into error, εἰ δυνατόν, if it were possible or could be done, even the elect.’ From this we infer as follows: if it were possible for an elect person to become a reprobate, then it would simultaneously be possible for the elect to be finally seduced; but according to Christ’s assertion, it is not possible for the elect to be finally seduced; therefore, it will not be possible for an elect person to become a reprobate. Nor is the exception valid that by ‘impossibility’ one must understand ‘difficulty,’ on the grounds that ‘impossible’ is often the same as ‘difficult.’ For, to say nothing of the fact that this explanation is a begging of the question and proceeds from mere particulars, I would wish that this one thing alone be studiously considered: that Christ does not say, ‘It is impossible for the elect to be seduced,’ but forms the style thus: ‘They will perform signs so great that even the elect would be led into error, if it were possible,’ by which words He certainly intends to be understood not merely a difficulty, but an altogether absolute impossibility of seduction. For even he who is seduced with difficulty is still seduced. Christ, however, denies altogether that any elect person will be seduced, because this is not possible. What kind of absurd paraphrase would it be: ‘Even the elect would be led into error on account of signs and wonders, if it were possible, i.e., unless it were difficult.’ Indeed, it could be inverted: ‘Although it is difficult, yet they could be led into error, since even those things which happen with difficulty nevertheless sometimes happen and can happen.’ Unless, therefore, one chooses to invert the words of Christ entirely, it is necessary that we confess that Christ spoke of the impossibility, rather than the difficulty, of seduction. Here, however, the question arises: is an absolute decree established in this way, or can another cause for the impossibility be assigned? We distinguish between ‘absolute’ and ‘infallible’; maintaining that the elect are not preserved and saved by an absolute and fatal necessity, as if it were simply impossible for them to perish, whatever they might do; but we intend only infallibility. Their own condition is indeed such that they can sin and perish; yet this never happens or can happen, because they are preserved infallibly. And thus we constitute the cause of that infallibility not as a Calvinistic fatal decree, nor as the supreme perfection of the elect, but rather: 1. the power of God, guarding the elect in faith unto salvation, 1 Pet. 1:5; 2. the efficacious prayer of Christ for the perseverance and salvation of the elect, John 17:11; 3. the power of Christ, from whose hands no one can snatch the sheep, John 10:28; 4. the firmness of the divine decree, 2 Tim. 2:19; and finally 5. the infallibility of foreknowledge.” (Anthropologia, Disp. XVI. C. 1. b. sq.) The same: "2 Tim. 2:18 and 19, 'Hymenaeus and Philetus have fallen away from the truth, saying that the resurrection has already taken place; but the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal: The Lord knows those who are His.' In this statement, that antithesis between those who fall away and those who are known by the Lord as His own must be most diligently observed. For because Hymenaeus and Philetus had indeed believed for a time, but afterwards had fallen away from the faith, the apostle immediately adds, lest anyone be offended as if the elect could also finally fall away and perish: 'But the firm foundation stands,' i.e., do not be offended that these two, who were first believers, have become apostates, nor think that the elect can also perish, since these men, although PART III. CHAP. XII. they believed for a time, were nevertheless not truly elect, which the outcome teaches, since 'the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal: The Lord knows those who are His.'" (Anthrop. Disp. XVI. B. 1.) The same: "We maintain that someone can be less edified and confirmed regarding election if its mutability is defended. For if someone believed himself to be elect, and yet doubted his perseverance and salvation because he heard that many of the elect fall away and perish eternally, I do not know whether this scruple could be sufficiently removed from him while the opinion of others stands. For he would urge thus: not every elect person perseveres and is saved, but many finally fall away from election and are damned. Even if, therefore, I am now elect, I cannot firmly conclude the certainty of perseverance and salvation from this election for the stated reason. Conversely, however, if the ἀμεταμέλητον [irrevocability] of election is established, one can invincibly conclude: every elect person is preserved by God and cannot be led into final error, but will certainly be saved and glorified. But I believe, and the Holy Spirit bears witness, that I am elect. Therefore, I am certain and firmly believe that God will preserve me, preserve me from all evil, and finally infallibly save and glorify me. Thus we see how great a πληροφορία [full assurance] and certainty of faith arises and is deduced from the immutability of election; if this is denied, that [certainty] must necessarily be, if not denied, at least in great part undermined." (Anthrop. Disp. XVI. D. 2. a. b.) Gerhard: "By hypothesis and supposition, it is most correctly said that the number of the elect can neither be increased nor diminished; for there the number is considered as it is in act; but everything that is, by the very fact that it is, is impossible not to be or to be otherwise, according to the rule of Boethius." (L. de elect. § 213.) Calovius: "If the elect could perish, the foreknowledge of God would be false and election mutable; since God, on the contrary, cannot be deceived in His foreknowledge. If election were uncertain and mutable, it would not have been made from eternity; for what is from eternity is not mutable. But it was made from eternity, Matt. 25:34, Eph. 1:4, 2 Tim. 1:9, Rev. 17:8, etc." (Socinism. proflig. p. 744.) B. Menzer: "It is certainly true that the faith of the elect cannot be finally overturned. Otherwise, they would not be elect. For all and only those who persevere in faith to the end are elect, and all and only the elect persevere in faith to the end." (Disp. th. in academ. Giessen, hab. Tom. VII, 499.) S. Schmidt: "This must be certain to us, that it is of mere divine grace in Christ that the elect cannot be seduced. It is proven because the elect, with the grace of election abstracted, can be seduced; indeed, it would certainly come to pass that they would be seduced, as our text (Matt. 24:24) clearly signifies. But that they can be seduced excludes all their merit, all their powers, to such an extent that they cannot make themselves unseducible. For imagine that they were such by their merits that God could not permit them to be seduced, but was compelled to make them unseducible; surely, considered in themselves and placed outside of election, they would be unseducible. But our passage suspends unseducibility upon election. It is necessary, therefore, that election be gratuitous and that the unseducibility arising from it be of mere grace." (Colleg. bibl. poster. Ed. 3. p. 242.) Scherzer: "The Socinians object: 1 Cor. 9, last verse: 'I bring my body into subjection, lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway [reprobus].' From this statement it is most clearly evident that Paul, who had been elected to eternal life, could have become a castaway. But if Paul himself could become a castaway, how much more so others? Slichting, after Socinus, *Questions against Meisner*, fol. 40. Response: The issue here is not reprobation as opposed to election, but as opposed to approval. ’Αδόκιμος is from δοκιμάζω, to approve, and denotes one who is useless, sometimes for a time, as in 2 Cor. 13:7. But we concede that one elected can be useless for a time, or even harmful to the church (such as Paul himself was before his conversion). From this it does not follow that any elected person is eternally reprobated."

Latin:

Idem: ,,Si etiam donemus, aliquos electos Matth. 24. in errore teneri in tota vita, tamen ante mortem necesse est ut redeant in viam, quia Christus dicit Joh. 10.: ,Nemo rapiet eos de manu mea.‘ “ (De servo arb. 1525. Opp. lat. var. argum. VII, 172.)

Idem: ״Matth. 24, 24. Hier ermahnet er uns, es werde künftig sein, nicht dass die Auserwählten nicht irren möchten, sondern dasa sie nicht verführet sollen werden in den Irrthum. Das ist so viel geredt, als, der Irrthum wird nicht herrschen über sie, wird sie auch endlieh nicht halten mögen, sondern sie müssen daraus erlediget werden und wenn es schon erst im Tode und Sterben geschähe.“ (Offenb. dea Antichrists. 1521. XVIII, 1932.)

Idem: ״Es ist wahrlich wohl möglich, dass die Auserwählten verführet werden, wie ich denn wahrlich im Pabstthum bis über die Ohren bin verführet gewesen. Wie ists denn nun möglich? Sie können verführet werden, aber endlich kommen sie doch wieder heraus, eher denn sie noch abscheiden aus diesem Jammerthal; wie ich denn oft das Exempel von Sanct Bernhardo pflege zu gebrauchen. Der hält auch dafür, dass der Pabst Gott wäre, aber do er itz sterben sollte, do wendet er die Augen vom Pabst, von seiner Kappen und Möncherei und kehret sich zu Christo, seinem Heiland, und vergass des Pabsts und seines gestrengen Ordens gar und sprach: Ich habe böslich gelebet, aber ich weiss, dass mein Herr Christus zweierlei Recht zum Himmelreich hat, erstlich von Natur, als der eingeborne Sohn vom Vater, do·

hat er den Himmel von Ewigkeit; zum andern, so hat er den Himmel als Marien Sohn, und do hat er den Himmel mit seinem bittern Leiden und Sterben erworben und mir geschenkt. Er rühmet sich nicht seines päbstisch Gelübde, sondern spricht: Christus hat den Himmel erblich und käuflich durch sein Blut erlangt. Also predigen wir auch. Er ist im Irrthum gewesen und dennochs herauskommen.“ (Predigt über Matth. 18—24. A. 1539. Ed. Erlang. P. XLV, 148. sq.) Idem: ,,Also gläube ich auch, dass unser lieber Gott in der grossen Einsterniss des Pabsthums viel unserer Vorfahren erhalten hat. Denn in derselben Blindheit und Ein sterniss ist dennoch überblieben, dass man den Sterbenden vorgehalten hat das Crucifix und dass etliche Laien ihnen vorgesagt haben: Siehe an Jesum, der für dich am Kreuz gestorben ist. Dadurch hat sich mancher Sterbender wieder zu Christo gekehret, ob er schon zuvor den falschen Wunderzeichen auch geglaubt hat und der Abgötterei angehangen ist. Das sind Auserwählte gewestf welche auch sind mitgeführet worden in das Gefängniss des Irrthums und wären darinnen blieben, wo es wäre möglich gewest. Also können wir uns trösten über denen, die im Pabstthum gestorben sind, dass Gott zuletzt ihnen Gnade gegeben hat, dass sie durch Erinnerung des Crucifixes auf Christum verschieden und dahin gefahren sind. Dieselben sind auch im Irrthum gesteckt, aber es ist nicht möglich gewest, dass sie darinnen bleiben sollten.“ (XIII, 2313. sq.) Idem: ,,Die Auserwählten werden nicht in Irrthum geführt werden; nicht, dass sie nicht irren würden; ja, die Fährlichkeit wird (vielmehr) so gross sein, dass sie mit den Gottlosen irren werden: aber sie werden nicht darinnen verharren noch bleiben, wiewohl sie schwerlich, mit Mühe und Arbeit entgehen werden.“ (XIX, 1384.) Idem: ,,Wir lassen Jonam hier (Jon. 1, 5.) eine grosse schwere Sünde gethan.haben, dadurch er ewiglich verdammt wäre, wo er nicht in der Auserwählten Zahl im Buch des Lebens geschrieben gewesen wäre.“ (Ad Jon. 1,5. VI, 2607.) Chemnitius: ,,Hieraus ist gewiss, dass kein Auserwählter in Unbussfertigkeit und Unglauben endlich bleibet und verharret.“ (Handbüchlein u. s.w. 1574. Vid. Frank: Die Th. der Concordienf. IV, 338.) Idem: ,,Das ist aus Grund der Schrift klar und gewiss, dass diejenigen, so zum ewigen Leben auserwählet sein, alle selig werden, denn Gottes Versehung kann nicht fehlen und die ewige Gnaden wähl Gottes ist unwandelbar, kann nicht geandert oder umgestossen werden, wie das aus der Schrift genugsam kann bewiesen werden.“ (A. 1576. Antwort an den Herzog Wolf gang von BraunschweigLüneburg über einen zu Osterode vorgefallenen Streit: ,,ob praedestinatio et electio uni versaliter zu verstehen sei, oder particulariter“. Vid. Rehtmeyer, Braunschweig. Kirchenhist. III. Beilagen S. 240.) Theologi Wuertembergici: ,,Die heilige Schrift redet lauter von einer solchen Election, die proprie allein die auserwählten Kinder Gottes angehet, die Gott ewig selig machen wird, wie solches die nächstfolgenden klaren Sprüche bezeugen. Röm. 8 (29. 30.). schreibt Paulus: ,Denn welche er zuvor versehen hat‘ u. s. w. In welchem hellen Spruch der Apostel lehrt, dass die Auserwählten allein unter dem Haufen derer, die berufen sind, zu suchen, und zeigt an, dass die Verordneten oder Erwählten auch gerecht und herrlich, das ist, ewig selig gemacht werden.“ (1594. Acta Huberiana I, 266. Vid. Frank: Theologie der Concordienf. IV, 285.) Facultas Theologica Wittebergensis: ,,Die Schrift hält durchaus für eins: die, welche Gott zum Leben erwählet, und die, welche endlich solch Leben ergreifen und in den Himmel kommen; in Ansehung, dass die Wahl nicht stocken bleibt, sondern wird zur Seligkeit und Glorification ausgeführt (Röm. 8, 29. 30.), wie Paulus sagt: ,Die PART. III. CAP. XII. Wahl erlangt es‘ (Köm. 11, 7.), nämlich der Seelen Seligkeit.“ (Bescheidentliche Antw. auf das Bek. Huberi. 1595. Vid. Consil. Witteberg. I, 547.) B. Meisnerus: ,,Per mutabilitatem vero nil aliud intelligitur, quam evacuationis possibilitas, cum electione quis excidere et ex electo potest fieri reprobus. Tum enim ratione nostri mutatur praedestinatio sic, ut, qui ante per fidem catalogo electorum adscriptus fuit, ob peccata inde expungatur, si vero poenitentiam agat, vicissim inscribatur, atque sic alternis vicibus pro ratione vel fidei vel impoenitentiae jam reprobus sit, jam electus. Talis igitur mutatio reciproca num concedi debeat, numve in decreto electionis locum habeat, in controversiam vocatur. Quid vero respondendum sit, non adeo obscurum erit, si C. F. consulatur. Sic autem in Epitome legitur art. 2. p. 618. edit. Lips. anno 1606.: ,Praedestinatio seu aeterna Dei electio tantum ad bonos et dilectos filios Dei pertinet et haec est causa ipsorum salutis; etenim salutem procurat et ea, quae ad ipsam pertinent, disponit. Super hanc Dei praedestinationem salus nostra ita fundata est, ut inferorum portae eam evertere nequeant.‘ Rursus in solida decl. p. 799.: ,Aeterna electio seu praedestinatio Dei ad salutem non simul ad bonos et ad malos pertinet, sed tantum ad filios Dei, qui ad aeternam vitam consequendam electi et ordinati sunt.‘ Paulo post: ,In ea divina praedestinatione aeterna nostra salus ita fundata est, ut etiam inferorum portae adversus eam praevalere nequeant, scriptum est enim: Oves meas nemo rapi etde manu mea.‘ Et p. 803.: ,Ille idem in aeterno consilio suo decrevit, quod eos, quos elegit, vocavit, justificavit, in altera aeterna illa vita salvos facere et aeterna gloria ornare velit.‘ Mox infra: ,Decrevit, quod eo modo (quem jam recitavimus) ipsos per suam gratiam, dona atque efficaciam salutis aeternae participes facere, juvare, eorum salutem promovere, ipsos confirmare et conservare velit.‘ Ex istis Concordiae verbis sequentes aphorismos deducimus:

1. Quod electio proprie dicta tantum fideles attineat, non omnes vocatos in genere, multo minus omnes homines.

2. Quod electi omnes certo salventur, quia dicitur, 1) electionem esse causam salutis et hanc ipsam procurare; 2) portas inferorum ·non posse evertere; 3) factam esse ad vitam consequendam; 4) sic, ut oves electae nequeant rapi e manu Dei, h. e., gratia flnaliter excidere et damnari; 5) quia Deus electos suos certo vult salvare et propterea in fide ad finem vitae usque conservare. Qui ergo non conservantur, non perseverant, adeoque non salvantur, ii vere proprieque secundum Scripturae phrasin et Concordiae explicationem electi vocari nequeunt.

3. Quod praedestinatio sit immutabilis, adeo ut ex electo uon flat reprobus, vel contra. Si enim omnes praedestinati conservantur et certo salvantur, utique praedestinatus nunquam fuit, qui damnatur, licet ad tempus crediderit et gratiam Dei persenserit. Eandem sententiam tenent theologi Wittebergenses in explic. brevi contra Huberum A. 3. fac. 2. B. 2. fac. 1. B. 3. fac. 1. et 2. D. 3. fac. 2. E. 4. fac. 2. E. 1. fac. 2., theologi Tubingenses P: I.
